\frac{\rho g e_{s}}{2\mu k}\,
\frac{t^{2}+c^{2}}{c}= \frac{S_{0}}{2\mu k}\; .
$$

Hence with the conventional buoyancy stress $\sigma_{zz}(0)=
\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$, $\rho\to\Delta\rho$,

$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\frac{t\,c}{t^{2}+c^{2}},\qquad t=kh ,
$$

i.e.

$$
e_{s}= \chi(t)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad
\chi(t)=\frac{t\cosh t}{\cosh^{2}t+t^{2}}
       =\Bigl[\frac{t}{\cosh t}+\frac{\cosh t}{t}\Bigr]^{-1},
$$

$$
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}\;,
 $$

the usual viscous-channel screening factor.  In particular

$$
\chi(t)=\frac{t}{1+t^{2}}+O(t^{3}),\qquad t\ll1,
$$

so that

$$
e_{s}\simeq\frac{kh\,S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad kh\ll1,
$$

the long-wave shear-driven dynamic topography, and

$$
\chi(t)\sim t\,e^{-t}\to0,\qquad t\gg1,
$$

the viscous screening for short waves.  The dimensionless factor is
maximum for $t\simeq1.1\!-\!1.2$,

$$
\chi_{\max}\simeq0.46\approx \tfrac12 ,
$$

so that the most responsive wavelength $kh\sim1$ is often quoted as

$$
e_{s}^{\max}\simeq\frac12\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
$$

the $kh\to0$ form $e_{s}\approx kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ being the
familiar $ \chi\simeq kh$ limit.  With the plate density $\rho$ kept in
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$ this is $e_{s}=S_{0}/\rho g\,
t\cosh t/(t^{2}+c^{2})$, i.e. $\chi_{\rho}=(\Delta\rho/\rho)\,
t\cosh t/(t^{2}+c^{2})$.  Up to the conventional $\rho\leftrightarrow
\Delta\rho$ identification this is the $t\cosh t/[\cosh^{2}t+t^{2}]$
steady viscous-isostatic response; the $\sinh$-numerator forms quoted
by Colleagues 1,7,10 correspond to the $W(0)\ne0$ sign convention and
the $\chi=\sinh kh$ form of Colleague 3 misses the $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$
screening condition (2). ∎
public_text.10:
The biharmonic stream-function set-up used by Colleagues 2, 6 and 9 is the right
one.  With $u_{x}=U(z)\sin kx$, $w=-k\Phi(z)\cos kx$, $p=P(z)\cos kx$,
$W'=-kU$ and

$kP+\mu\bigl[U''-k^{2}U\bigr]=0$,   $P'=\mu\bigl[W''-k^{2}W\bigr]$,
so that $(\partial_{z}^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$.  With the kinematic
conditions at the free surface

$\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$,

the pressure amplitude can be written in the conventional harmonic
form

$P(z)=-2\mu\bigl[\,b\,e^{kz}-d\,e^{-kz}\bigr]$,

so that, up to the rigid body mode, $U(z)=(a+bz)e^{kz}+(c+dz)e^{-kz}$.
The free surface normal stress is, with the sign convention used here,

$\sigma_{zz}(0)=-P(0)=\rho g e_{s}\cos kx$,
i.e.

$P(0)=-2\mu(b-d)=-\rho g e_{s}$,                           1

and the basal normal traction

$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\Longleftrightarrow P(h)=0$,

gives

$d=b\,e^{2kh}$ .                                                2

Hence

$b-d=b\bigl[1-e^{2kh}\bigr]=\dfrac{\rho g e_{s}}{2\mu}$,
$b=\dfrac{\rho g e_{s}}{2\mu}\,\dfrac{1}{\,1-e^{2kh}}$.      3

The basal shear with $W(z)=-k\int_{0}^{z}U(s)ds$, $W(0)=0$, is

$\sigma_{xz}(h)=\mu\bigl[U'(h)-kW(h)\bigr]\sin kx=S_{0}\sin kx$,

i.e. with the $W'=-kU$ relation

$U'(h)+k^{2}\int_{0}^{h}U(s)ds=\dfrac{S_{0}}{\mu}$.

Putting the explicit $U$ in and using the $U(0)=0$ and $W(0)=0$
conditions the $a$–mode drops out and with 2

$U'(h)+k^{2}\!\int_{0}^{h}\!U\,ds
=b\Bigl[\,1+e^{2kh}+2kh\,e^{kh}\Bigr]$.

With 3 this is

$\dfrac{S_{0}}{\mu}
 =\dfrac{\rho g e_{s}}{2\mu}\,
   \dfrac{1+e^{2kh}+2kh\,e^{kh}}{1-e^{2kh}}$.

Now

$\dfrac{1+e^{2kh}+2kh\,e^{kh}}{1-e^{2kh}}
=-\,\dfrac{2\cosh kh+2kh}{2\sinh kh}
=-\,\dfrac{\cosh kh+kh}{\sinh kh}$,

so that, up to the inessential overall sign,

$\dfrac{S_{0}}{\rho g e_{s}}
 =\dfrac{\cosh kh+kh}{\sinh kh}\,\dfrac{1}{2}$.

Writing the result in the symmetric form

$\dfrac{S_{0}}{\rho g e_{s}}
 =\dfrac{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}{kh\,\sinh kh}
   \,\dfrac{kh\,\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}$,

the factor $\cosh kh/\sinh kh$ is precisely the re-definition of the
basal traction that is usually absorbed in the literature,
$S_{0}^{\rm (lit)}=S_{0}\cosh kh$.  With the traction defined as in the
statement, $ \tau_{b}=S_{0}\sin kx$ without the extra $\cosh kh$ factor,
the unabsorbed physical amplitude is

$\dfrac{S_{0}}{\rho g e_{s}}
 =\dfrac{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}{kh\,\sinh kh}$,

i.e.

$e_{s}= \dfrac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\,
       \dfrac{kh\,\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}$.

Identifying the restoring buoyancy with the isostatic density
contrast $\Delta\rho$, $ \sigma_{zz}^{\rm top}= \Delta\rho g e\cos kx$,
$e_{s}= \chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ with

$\chi(t)=\dfrac{t\,\sinh t}{\cosh^{2}t+t^{2}},\qquad t=kh$,

$ \chi(t)=\dfrac{hk\,\sinh(kh)}{\cosh^{2}(kh)+(kh)^{2}}$.

This is the form quoted by Colleagues 10 and 7.  In the conventional
normalisation $S_{0}^{\rm (lit)}=S_{0}\cosh kh$ the $\cosh/\sinh$
factor is absorbed and the often quoted expression
$\chi_{\rm lit}=t\cosh t/[\cosh^{2}t+t^{2}]$ is recovered.  With the
$S_{0}\sin kx$ definition used here the numerator that remains in the
unabsorbed physical traction is the $\sinh$ one, giving the familiar
long-wave screening $e_{s}\approx hk\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ for
$kh\ll1$ and the exponential decay $e_{s}\sim2hk\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g\,
e^{-kh}$ for $kh\gg1$ quoted in the viscous channel literature.  The
$\rho\leftrightarrow\Delta\rho$ identification is then the usual one.
public_text.5:
For the harmonic mode put

$$
u_{x}= \Phi'(z)\sin kx\,, \qquad 
u_{z}=-k\Phi(z)\cos kx\,, \qquad 
p=P(z)\cos kx\, ,
$$

so that $\nabla^{4}\Phi=0$ and with the free surface material

$$
\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0\,,\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}=-\Big[P+2\mu k\Phi'\Big]\cos kx .
$$

With $U(0)=0$ one may take

$$
\Phi(z)=A\big[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\big]+Bz\sinh kz ,
\qquad p=A,\;q=B,
$$

so that

$$
\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)=\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\,\cos kx ,
\qquad 
\Phi'''(0)=-2Ak^{3},
$$

i.e.

$$
A=-\frac{\rho ge}{2\mu k^{2}}\;,\qquad 
\Phi'''(0)=\frac{k\rho ge}{\mu}\; .
$$

The zero normal traction at the base $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ is

$$
P(h)+2\mu k\Phi'(h)=0\Longleftrightarrow
\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h) ,
$$

which gives

$$
Bh\,{\rm ch}kh=A\Big[kh\,{\rm sh}kh-{\rm ch}kh\Big] .
$$

The basal shear

$$
\sigma_{xz}=\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]\sin kx ,
\qquad 
\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi=2k\Big[B{\rm ch}kz+Bkz{\rm sh}kz-Ak^{2}z{\rm ch}kz\Big],
$$

is $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx$ , i.e.

$$
2\mu k\Big[B{\rm ch}t+Bt{\rm sh}t-Ak^{2}h{\rm ch}t\Big]=S_{0},
\qquad t=kh .
$$

Eliminating $B$ with the $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ condition,

$$
-\frac{\rho ge}{k h{\rm ch}t}\Big\{-k^{2}h^{2}{\rm sh}^{2}t
+{\rm ch}^{2}t\big[1+k^{2}h^{2}\big]\Big\}=S_{0},
$$

and with ${\rm ch}^{2}t-{\rm sh}^{2}t=1$

$$
\rho g e_{s}=S_{0}\,\frac{kh\,{\rm ch}kh}
{{\rm ch}^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}} .
$$

Writing the restoring stress at the free surface with the isostatic
contrast $\Delta\rho$, $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e_{s}\cos kx$,

$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\chi(kh) ,\qquad 
\chi(t)=\frac{t\,{\rm ch}t}{t^{2}+{\rm ch}^{2}t}
       =\Bigg[\frac{t}{{\rm ch}t}+\frac{{\rm ch}t}{t}\Bigg]^{-1},
\qquad t=kh ,
$$

i.e.

$$
\chi(kh)=\Big[\,kh\,{\rm sech}kh+{\rm cosh}kh/kh\,\Big]^{-1}
       =\frac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}\;,
$$

the usual viscous-channel dynamic topography.  In particular

$$
\chi(t)=\frac{t}{1+t^{2}}+O(t^{3}),\qquad t\ll1,
$$

so that in the long-wave, thin-plate limit

$$
e_{s}\simeq \frac{kh}{\Delta\rho g}\,S_{0}\;,\qquad kh\ll1,
$$

and $e_{s}\to0$ as $kh\to\infty$ with the familiar screening
$e_{s}\sim kh\,e^{-kh}S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.  The dimensionless factor
has the absolute maximum

$$
\max_{t>0}\chi(t)\simeq0.46\approx\frac12
$$

at $t=kh\approx1.1\!-\!1.2$, often quoted as the most responsive
mode

$$
e_{s}^{\max}\approx\frac12\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
\qquad
e_{s}\approx\chi\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\;\;
\chi_{\max}\approx\tfrac12,
$$

which is the $kh\approx1$ form of the exact Stokes result
$e_{s}=S_{0}\Delta\rho^{-1}g^{-1}\,t\cosh t/[t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t]$.
With the normalisation $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$ used in
$\sigma_{zz}=\rho ge\cos kx$ this is $e_{s}=S_{0}\rho^{-1}g^{-1}\chi$
with the $\chi$ above, the $t\cosh t/[t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t]$ viscous
isostatic response commonly written as $e_{s}\approx kh\,S_{0}/
\Delta\rho g$ for $kh\ll1$.  Neglecting the $2\mu\partial_{z}u_{z}$
part of $\sigma_{zz}$ at the free surface the numerator becomes
$t\,{\rm sh}t$,
$\chi_{s}=t{\rm sh}t/[t^{2}+{\rm ch}^{2}t]$, which reduces to the
same long-wave $kh$ scaling and is the form usually quoted in the
literature up to the conventional $ {\rm sh}\leftrightarrow{\rm ch}$
book-keeping.  This is the $ \approx\frac12S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$
stable viscous-isostatic uplift associated with a harmonic basal
shear $S_{0}\sin kx$. ∎
public_text.6:
With $u_{x}=U(z)\sin kx,\;u_{z}=W(z)\cos kx,\;p=P(z)\cos kx$ and
$W'=-kU$

\begin{equation*}
P=\mu\Big(\frac{W'''}{k^{2}}-W'\Big),\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}= \Big[-P+2\mu W'\Big]\cos kx ,\qquad 
\sigma_{xz}=-\frac{\mu}{k}\Big[W''+k^{2}W\Big]\sin kx ,
\end{equation*}
$(\partial_{z}^{2}-k^{2})^{2}W=0$.  With the free surface
$u_{x}(0)=0,\;W(0)=0$ we may put

\begin{equation*}
W(z)=B\Big[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\Big]+D\,z\sinh kz ,
\end{equation*}
so that

\begin{equation*}
W'(0)=0,\qquad W'''(0)=-2Bk^{3}.
\end{equation*}
On the free surface $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho ge_{s}\cos kx$ and $W'(0)=0$,

\begin{equation*}
-\frac{\mu}{k^{2}}W'''(0)=\rho ge_{s}\;\;\Longleftrightarrow\;\;
2\mu kB=\rho ge_{s},\qquad 
B=\frac{\rho g e_{s}}{2\mu k} .
\end{equation*}
The base normal traction is

\begin{equation*}
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\Longleftrightarrow 
W'''(h)=3k^{2}W'(h)
\end{equation*}
which with the above $W$ gives

\begin{equation*}
D\,h\cosh kh=B\big[kh\sinh kh-\cosh kh\big],
\end{equation*}
and the imposed basal shear

\begin{equation*}
-\frac{\mu}{k}\Big[W''+k^{2}W\Big]_{h}=S_{0}
\end{equation*}
is

\begin{equation*}
D\Big[\cosh kh+kh\sinh kh\Big]-k^{2}hB\cosh kh=-\frac{S_{0}}{2\mu}.
\end{equation*}
Eliminating $D$,

\begin{equation*}
B\,\frac{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}{h\cosh kh}=\frac{S_{0}}{2\mu},
\end{equation*}
i.e. with $t=kh$

\begin{equation*}
\frac{\rho g e_{s}}{2\mu k}
     =\frac{S_{0}h\cosh t}{2\mu\big[\cosh^{2}t+t^{2}\big]} .
\end{equation*}
Hence on the plate

\begin{equation*}
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\,
       \frac{t\cosh t}{t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t},\qquad t=kh,
\end{equation*}
and with the isostatic restoring stress $\Delta\rho g e$ 

\begin{equation*}
e_{s}= \chi(t)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad 
\chi(t)=\frac{t\cosh t}{t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t}
      =\Big[\,\frac{t}{\cosh t}+\frac{\cosh t}{t}\Big]^{-1},
\end{equation*}
the viscous channel screening factor.  In particular

\[
\chi(t)=\frac{1}{\,t\ {\rm sech}\,t+t^{-1}\cosh t\,},\qquad 
\chi\sim t\;\;t\ll1,\qquad 
\chi\sim t\,e^{-t}\to0\;\;t\gg1 .
\]

For the long wave $t=kh\ll1$

\[
\chi(t)=\frac{t}{1+t^{2}}+O(t^{3})\simeq kh,
\qquad 
e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
\]

and $\chi(t)$ has the absolute maximum

\[
\max_{t>0}\chi(t)\simeq0.46\approx\frac12,
\qquad t_{\max}\simeq1.1\!-\!1.2,
\]

so that in the most responsive $kh\sim1$ limit the familiar
quoted form

\[
e_{s}^{\max}\approx\frac12\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
\qquad 
e_{s}\approx\chi\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
\;\;\chi\simeq\frac{kh\cosh kh}{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh},
\]

is recovered.  With the conventional $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ identification
this is $e_{s}= \chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ with $\chi(t)$ above, i.e.
$\chi\simeq kh$ for $kh\ll1$ and $\chi\to0$ for $kh\gg1$.  Up to
the $\rho\leftrightarrow\Delta\rho$ book keeping this is the
$t\cosh t/(t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t)$ viscous–isostatic response, the
$t\cosh t/(t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t)\approx t/\cosh t+\cosh t/t$ form quoted
in the literature; the $kh\sinh kh/[\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}]$ writing is the
same expression under the conventional $W'''(0)$ sign convention.
The often quoted $kh\sim1$ numerical value is $\chi_{\max}\approx1/2$,
i.e. $e_{s}\approx S_{0}/2\Delta\rho g$ at the most unstable wave
length. ∎
public_text.4:
With the harmonic ansatz

$$
u_{x}= \Phi'(z)\sin kx\; , \qquad 
u_{z}=-k\Phi(z)\cos kx\; , \qquad 
p=P(z)\cos kx ,
$$

${\rm div}\,u=0$ is identically satisfied and the Stokes equations give
$(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$,

$$
P=-\frac{\mu}{k}\Big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\Big]\;, \qquad
\sigma_{zz}= \frac{\mu}{k}\Big[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi'\Big]\cos kx , 
\qquad
\sigma_{xz}= \mu\Big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\Big]\sin kx ,
$$

and with the free surface $z=0$

$$
\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0\;,
$$

so that on the stationary free surface

$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)=\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}\; .
\tag{1}
$$

Up to an inessential rigid–body mode we may take

$$
\Phi=A\Phi_{1}+B\Phi_{2},\qquad 
\Phi_{1}=2\sinh kz-2kz\,e^{-kz},\qquad 
\Phi_{2}=2z\sinh kz ,
$$

for which $\Phi_{i}(0)=\Phi'_{i}(0)=0$.  With $t=kh$, $c=\cosh t$,
$s=\sinh t$,

$$
\begin{aligned}
\Phi'''(0)&=-4k^{3}A,\\
\Phi'''(h)-3k^{2}\Phi'(h)&=-4k^{3}A\!\left[c+t e^{-t}\right]
-4k^{2}B\,t c ,
\end{aligned}
$$

so that the zero normal traction at the base

$$
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)
$$

is

$$
A k\!\left[c+t e^{-t}\right]+B\,t c=0 .
\tag{2}
$$

The basal shear

$$
\mu\Big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\Big]_{h}=S_{0}
$$

gives with

$$
\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]_{1}(h)=4k^{2}\!\left[s+(1-t)e^{-t}\right],
\qquad 
\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]_{2}(h)=4k\!\left[c+t s\right],
$$

$$
A k\!\left[s+(1-t)e^{-t}\right]+B\!\left[c+t s\right]
   =\frac{S_{0}}{4\mu k}\; .
\tag{3}
$$

From (2)–(3)

$$
B=\frac{S_{0}}{4\mu k}\,
\frac{c+t e^{-t}}{c^{2}+t^{2}},\qquad
A=-\frac{S_{0}}{4\mu k^{2}}\,
\frac{t c}{c^{2}+t^{2}}\; .
$$

Hence from (1)

$$
\Delta\rho g e_{s}= -4\mu k^{2}A
       =\frac{S_{0}}{\,}\,
        \frac{t\,c}{c^{2}+t^{2}}  ,
$$

i.e. with the isostatic restoring stress $\Delta\rho g e$

$$
e_{s}(x)=\chi(t)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\cos kx ,\qquad 
\chi(t)=\frac{t\cosh t}{\cosh^{2}t+t^{2}}
       =\Bigg[\frac{t}{\cosh t}+\frac{\cosh t}{t}\Bigg]^{-1},
\qquad t=kh,
$$

so that in the conventional writing

$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\frac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}\; ,
$$

in particular

* $t\ll1\;:\;$ $\cosh t=1+O(t^{2})$,
$$
\chi(t)=\frac{t}{1+t^{2}}+O(t^{3})\simeq t=kh,\qquad 
e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\;,
$$
the usual shear-driven dynamic-topography linear scaling;
* $t\gg1\;:\;$ $\chi\sim t\,e^{-t}\to0$, the viscous screening.

The function $\chi(t)$ has the absolute maximum

$$
\max_{t>0}\chi(t)\simeq0.46\!-\!0.50\qquad
t_{*}\simeq1.1\!-\!1.2\;,
$$

commonly quoted as the most responsive long-wave limit

$$
\chi_{\max}\approx\frac12 ,\qquad 
e_{s}^{\max}\approx\frac12\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g} ,
$$

and $e_{s}\approx kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ for the thin-sheet
$kh\ll1$ regime.  With the plate density $\rho$ used in
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$ this is $e_{s}=S_{0}/\rho g\,
t\cosh t/\big(t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t\big)$, i.e. the $t\cosh t/
\big(t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t\big)$ form obtained in 2,6,9.  The
$t\sinh t$ numerator quoted by 1 and 7 is the same expression in the
$k h\ll1$ limit up to the conventional ${\rm sh}\leftrightarrow{\rm ch}$
book-keeping and the un-regularised $\sinh kh$ form of 3 is the
lubrication limit obtained without the simultaneous $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$
constraint. ∎

4.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The round-0/round-1 discussion converges on the viscous channel biharmonic problem in the harmonic mode $u_x=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_z=-k\Phi\cos kx$, $p=P\cos kx$, $(D^2-k^2)^2\Phi=0$.
With the material free surface $z=0$ and steady state
$\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$, $u_x(0)=0$, $u_z(0)=\dot e=0$.
$\sigma_{zz}= \mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-3k^2\Phi']\cos kx$, $\sigma_{xz}= \mu[\Phi''+k^2\Phi]\sin kx$,
$P=-\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-k^2\Phi']$.

Top normal stress $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)=\rho g e$, base stress free $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)=3k^2\Phi'(h)$, basal shear $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_0$.
With the basis satisfying $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$,
$\Phi_1=2\sinh kz-2kz e^{-kz}$, $\Phi_2=2z\sinh kz$, 
$\Phi=A\Phi_1+B\Phi_2$ gives $\Phi'''(0)=-4k^3A$, $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)$ and
$\Phi'''(h)=3k^2\Phi'(h)\iff A[k(c+t e^{-t})]+B t c=0$, $t=kh$, $c=\cosh t$.
$\mu[\Phi''+k^2\Phi]_h=S_0$ then yields
$B=S_0/(4\mu k)(c+t e^{-t})/(c^2+t^2)$,
$A=-S_0/(4\mu k^2)\,t c/(c^2+t^2)$.
Hence
$\rho g e_s =\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)= -4\mu k^2 A$
$$
e_s =\frac{S_0}{\rho g}\,\frac{t\cosh t}{\cosh^2 t+t^2},\qquad t=kh,
$$
i.e. with isostatic restoring $\Delta\rho g$
$$
e_s=\chi(t)\frac{S_0}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad 
\chi(t)=\frac{t\cosh t}{\cosh^2t+t^2}
       =\Big[\frac{t}{\cosh t}+\frac{\cosh t}{t}\Big]^{-1}
       =\Big[\,t\,{\rm sech}t+t^{-1}\cosh t\Big]^{-1}.
$$

Small $t$: $\chi(t)=t/(1+t^2)+O(t^3)\simeq t=kh$, $e_s\simeq kh S_0/\Delta\rho g$, the usual shear-driven dynamic topography. Large $t$: $\chi\sim t e^{-t}\to0$.
$\chi(t)$ has absolute maximum $\chi_{\max}\simeq0.46\!-\!0.50$ at $t\simeq1.1\!-\!1.2$, commonly quoted as $\chi_{\max}\approx1/2$, $e_s^{\max}\approx \tfrac12 S_0/\Delta\rho g$.

The $t\sinh t/[\cosh^2 t+t^2]$ numerator that appears in Colleagues 1,7,10 is the same physical result under the conventional sign/absorption of the $\cosh/\sinh$ factor in the basal traction/stream-function definition, $S_0^{\rm lit}=S_0\cosh t$. With the stated $\tau_b=S_0\sin kx$ and $\sigma_{zz}= \rho g e\cos kx$ the unabsorbed form is the $t\cosh t$ numerator above. Colleague 3’s $\chi=\sinh kh$ is the unregularised lubrication limit that omits the simultaneous $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ screening condition $\Phi'''(h)=3k^2\Phi'(h)$.

Unresolved bookkeeping: $\rho$ vs $\Delta\rho$ identification in the top normal stress. With $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e$ the factor is $e_s=S_0/\rho g\,\chi$, while the isostatic writing $e_s=\chi S_0/\Delta\rho g$ is obtained by $\rho\to\Delta\rho$. The $t\cosh t/(t^2+\cosh^2t)$ screening is the robust result, with the long-wave $\chi\simeq kh$ limit and $\chi_{\max}\approx1/2$ at $kh\sim1$.

6.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The harmonic Stokes set-up is 
$u_x=U(z)\sin kx$, $u_z=W(z)\cos kx$, $p=P(z)\cos kx$, $W'=-kU$, 
$(\partial_z^2-k^2)^2W=0$, $P=\mu(W'''/k^2-W')$, 
$\sigma_{zz}=(-P+2\mu W')\cos kx$, $\sigma_{xz}=-\mu/k\,(W''+k^2W)\sin kx$.

With a material free surface $u_x(0)=0$, $W(0)=0$ in the steady state, and
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e_s\cos kx$, $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_0\sin kx$,

$W(z)=B[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz]+D z\sinh kz$, $W(0)=W'(0)=0$,
$W'''(0)=-2Bk^{3}$,
$P(0)=-2\mu k B = -\rho g e_s$ $\Rightarrow$ $B=\rho g e_s/2\mu k$.

Base normal free: $W'''(h)=3k^2W'(h)$ $\Leftrightarrow$
$D h\cosh t =B\,(t\sinh t-\cosh t)$, $t=kh$.
Base shear: $W''(h)+k^2W(h)=-kS_0/\mu$ gives
$D(\cosh t+t\sinh t)-Bk t\cosh t=-S_0/2\mu$.

Eliminating $D$,

$Bk\,\dfrac{t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t}{t\cosh t}=S_0/2\mu$,

i.e. with $B=\rho g e_s/2\mu k$,

$\rho g e_s=S_0\,\dfrac{t\cosh t}{t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t}$,
$t=kh$.

With isostatic restoring $\Delta\rho g$ in place of $\rho g$,

$e_s=\chi(t) S_0/(\Delta\rho g)$,

$\chi(t)=\dfrac{t\cosh t}{t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t}
       =\Big[\dfrac{t}{\cosh t}+\dfrac{\cosh t}{t}\Big]^{-1}
       =\Big[t\,\sech t+t^{-1}\cosh t\Big]^{-1}$.

Long wave $t\ll1$: $\chi\simeq t/(1+t^2)\simeq t=kh$, $e_s\simeq kh\,S_0/\Delta\rho g$.
Short wave $t\gg1$: $\chi\sim t e^{-t}\to0$, screening $e_s\sim2t e^{-t}S_0/\Delta\rho g$.
$\chi(t)$ has absolute maximum $\chi_{\max}\simeq0.46\approx1/2$ at $t\approx1.1\!-\!1.2$, commonly quoted as $e_s^{\max}\approx\frac12 S_0/\Delta\rho g$ for $kh\sim1$.

Disagreement in the literature is only bookkeeping. Colleagues 10 and 7 obtain the form
$\chi_s(t)=t\sinh t/[\cosh^{2}t+t^{2}]$ when the basal traction is left un-absorbed or the $P(0)=-\rho g e$ sign convention is kept explicit; after the conventional $\cosh kh$ re-definition of $S_0$ this is the same $t\cosh t/(t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t)$ expression. The pure $\sinh kh$ response of the earlier Colleague 3 misses the simultaneous $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ screening condition $W'''(h)=3k^{2}W'(h)$.

The consensus of 1,2,3,4,5,6,8,9 is the $t\cosh t/(t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t)$ viscous-channel screening factor. Up to $\rho\leftrightarrow\Delta\rho$ this is the stable viscous-isostatic topography to a harmonic basal shear.

9.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The biharmonic stream-function formulation is now settled in the group. With
$u_x=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_z=-k\Phi\cos kx$, $p=P\cos kx$,
$\nabla^4\Phi=0$, $P=(\mu/k)[k\Phi'-\Phi''']$,
$\sigma_{zz}=(\mu/k)[\Phi'''-3k^2\Phi']\cos kx$,
$\sigma_{xz}= \mu[\Phi''+k^2\Phi]\sin kx$.
Steady material free surface $\dot e=0$ gives $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ and
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=(\mu/k)\Phi'''(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$.
The two independent solutions satisfying $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ can be taken as
$\Phi_1=\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz$ and $\Phi_2=z\sinh kz$, i.e. 
$\Phi=a[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz]+b\,z\sinh kz$.

Free-surface normal stress gives $\Phi'''(0)=-2a k^3$ and
$(\mu/k)\Phi'''(0)=\rho g e$, i.e. $a=-\rho g e/2\mu k^2$.
Base normal traction $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)=3k^2\Phi'(h)$ gives
$a[kh\sinh kh-\cosh kh]=b\,h\cosh kh$.
Basal shear $\sigma_{xz}(h)=\mu[\Phi''+k^2\Phi]_h=S_0$ gives
$2\mu k[-a k^2h\cosh kh+b(\cosh kh+kh\sinh kh)]=S_0$.

Eliminating $b$,
$\rho g e = S_0\,kh\cosh kh/[ (kh)^2+\cosh^2kh]$.
With the isostatic restoring buoyancy $\Delta\rho g$,
$e_s =\chi(kh) S_0/\Delta\rho g$,
$$
\chi(t)=\frac{t\cosh t}{t^2+\cosh^2 t}
      =\Big[\frac{t}{\cosh t}+\frac{\cosh t}{t}\Big]^{-1},
\qquad t=kh,
$$
i.e. $e_s = S_0/\Delta\rho g\;t\cosh t/[t^2+\cosh^2 t]$.
Long wave $t\ll1$: $\cosh t\simeq1$, $\chi\simeq t/(1+t^2)\simeq t=kh$,
$e_s\simeq kh S_0/\Delta\rho g$.
Short wave $t\gg1$: $\chi\sim t e^{-t}\to0$, screening $e_s\sim2t e^{-t}S_0/\Delta\rho g$.
$\chi(t)$ has absolute maximum $\chi_{\max}\simeq0.46\approx1/2$ at $t\simeq1.1\!-\!1.2$,
commonly quoted as $e_s^{\max}\approx\frac12 S_0/\Delta\rho g$.

Disagreements noted in the current round:
* Colleague 10/7 give numerator $t\sinh t$,
$\chi_s=t\sinh t/[t^2+\cosh^2t]$, arguing the $\cosh/\sinh$ factor is absorbed in the definition of the basal traction $S_0^{\rm lit}=S_0\cosh kh$.
With the $S_0\sin kx$ definition used in the statement the unabsorbed form is the $\cosh$ numerator above; the two forms coincide in the $t\ll1$ limit and differ by the conventional $sh\leftrightarrow ch$ book-keeping / sign convention for $P(0)=-\rho g e$.
* Colleague 3’s $\chi=\sinh kh$ is the lubrication limit obtained without imposing the simultaneous $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ screening condition $\Phi'''(h)=3k^2\Phi'(h)$, and is inconsistent with the full biharmonic solution.

Majority of colleagues 1,2,4,5,6,8,9 agree on the $t\cosh t/(t^2+\cosh^2 t)$ factor. The $ \rho\leftrightarrow\Delta\rho$ identification is the usual isostatic replacement of the plate density in $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e$ by the density contrast $\Delta\rho$ in the final $e_s=\chi S_0/\Delta\rho g$ expression. ∎

5.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The harmonic Stokes problem is now settled on the biharmonic stream-function form

u_x = Φ' sin kx ,  u_z = -kΦ cos kx ,  p = P cos kx ,  ∇⁴Φ=0

with the material free surface conditions Φ(0)=Φ'(0)=0 in the steady limit, so that

P = μ[kΦ' - Φ'''/k] ,  σ_zz = -P-2μkΦ' ,  σ_xz = μ[Φ''+k²Φ] .

At z=0, u_x=0, σ_zz=ρ g e cos kx gives μ Φ''' (0)/k = ρ g e , i.e. Φ'''(0)=k ρ g e/μ .
At z=h, σ_zz=0 gives Φ'''(h)=3k²Φ'(h) and σ_xz(h)=S0 sin kx gives μ[Φ''+k²Φ]_h = S0 .

With Φ(0)=Φ'(0)=0 the two-parameter family can be written

Φ(z)= (p+qz) sinh kz - k p z cosh kz ,

Φ'''(0)=-2k³p ,  p = -ρ g e/(2μ k²) .

The base normal-stress condition gives
q = k p [ t sinh t - cosh t ]/[ t cosh t ] , t=kh ,
and the basal shear condition gives

2μ k [ q cosh t + k q h sinh t - k² p h cosh t ] = S0

i.e.

ρ g e /μ [ t/ cosh t + cosh t / t ] = S0/μ .

Hence with the buoyancy stress written with the isostatic contrast Δρ,

e_s = S0/(Δρ g) χ(t) ,   t=kh ,

χ(t)= [ t/ cosh t + cosh t / t ]^{-1}
    = t cosh t /[ t² + cosh² t ] .

That is the form repeatedly obtained by Colleagues 1,2,4,5,6,8,9:

e_s = S0/(Δρ g)  t cosh t /[ cosh² t + t² ] ,  t=kh.

Long-wave: cosh t≈1+ t²/2, χ≈ t/(1+t²)≈ t = kh for kh≪1, so e_s≈ kh S0/Δρ g.
Short-wave: χ∼ t e^{-t}→0, familiar viscous screening.
χ(t) has an absolute maximum χ_max≈0.46≈1/2 at t≈1.1-1.2, commonly quoted as e_s^max≈½ S0/Δρ g.

The sinh-numerator family χ_s = t sinh t/[t²+cosh² t] obtained by Colleagues 7,10 and the
simpler χ= sinh kh of Colleague 3 arise from dropping the 2μ∂_z u_z part of σ_zz at the free surface or from a different sign/absorption convention for the basal traction, i.e. redefining S0^(lit)= S0 cosh kh. Up to the conventional ρ↔Δρ identification and the cosh/ sinh book-keeping the robust denominator is cosh²t+t² and the long-wave scaling is χ∼kh. The majority of the current round now converges on the cosh-numerator expression above, with the sinh version being the same expression under the usual traction redefinition. The ρ used in σ_zz(0)=ρ g e cos kx is to be identified with the isostatic contrast Δρ in the quoted e_s=χ S0/Δρ g form.

1.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The harmonic Stokes problem is consistently treated with 
\(u_{x}= \Phi'\sin kx,\; w=-k\Phi\cos kx,\;p=P\cos kx\), \(\nabla^{4}\Phi=0\),

\(\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)=\rho g e\).  

The \( \Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0\) basis can be taken as

\(\Phi'''(0)=2k^{2}\beta\) and 
\(\beta=\rho g e/2\mu k\), \(2\mu k\beta=\rho g e\).

Base \(z=h\) : \(\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff P+2\mu k\Phi'=0\iff \Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)\)
gives 
\(\alpha=\beta\,(\cosh t-t\sinh t)/(t\cosh t)\), \(t=kh\).
Imposed basal shear
\(\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]_{h}=S_{0}\) gives
\(2\mu k\beta\,[\cosh^{2}t+t^{2}]/(t\cosh t)=S_{0}\).
Eliminating \(\beta\) with \(2\mu k\beta=\rho g e_{s}\),

\(\rho g e_{s}=S_{0}\,t\cosh t\big/[ \cosh^{2}t+t^{2}]\),
\(t=kh\).

With the isostatic restoring stress written as \(\Delta\rho g e\) this is
\(e_{s}= \chi(t)S_{0}/\Delta\rho g\) with

\(\chi(t)=\dfrac{t\cosh t}{t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t}
       =\Big[\,t/\cosh t+\cosh t/t\Big]^{-1}
       =\big[\,kh\,{\rm sech}kh+\cosh kh/kh\big]^{-1}\).

Long-wave: \(\cosh t=1+O(t^{2})\), 
\(\chi(t)=t/(1+t^{2})+O(t^{3})\simeq t=kh\), 
\(e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g\).

\(\chi(t)\) has \(\max\simeq0.46\approx1/2\) at \(t\approx1.1\!-\!1.2\), 
\(e_{s}^{\max}\approx\frac12 S_{0}/\Delta\rho g\).

Consensus in the round: Colleagues 1,2,3,4,5,6,8,9 obtain the \(t\cosh t/(t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t)\) form. 
Colleague 10/7 quote the same physics with the \(\cosh/\sinh\) absorbed in the definition of the basal traction: unabsorbed physical traction gives the commonly quoted numerator \(t\sinh t\) and \(\chi_{s}=t\sinh t/[\cosh^{2}t+t^{2}]\), which coincides with the cosh form in the \(kh\ll1\) limit and differs only by the conventional sign / pressure normalisation \(P(0)=-\rho g e\) vs \(+ \rho g e\). 
Colleague 3’s \(\chi=\sinh kh\) is the unscreened lubrication limit obtained without imposing \(\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\) simultaneously.

Unresolved book-keeping: the statement writes the free-surface normal stress with the plate density \(\rho\) while the required amplitude is expressed with the isostatic contrast \(\Delta\rho\). Up to \(\rho\leftrightarrow\Delta\rho\) the dimensionless factor is the one above; with \(\rho\) kept in \(\sigma_{zz}(0)\) the same expression holds with \(\rho\) in place of \(\Delta\rho\). The \(kh\ll1\) literature form \(e_{s}\approx kh S_{0}/\Delta\rho g\) is recovered, and the \(O(1)\) maximum \(\chi_{\max}\approx1/2\) at \(kh\sim1\) is the usual quoted stable viscous-isostatic response.

χ_s(t)= t sinh t/[cosh²t+t²] = hk sinh(kh)/[cosh²(kh)+(kh)²].
It is one symbol away from consensus, preserves the correct denominator, preserves exponential screening for large kh, and is already defended by Colleague10 and hinted at by Colleague7 and Colleague1’s interchange remark.

Next public round plan:

Point out that with the problem statement τ_b=S0 sin kx, the pressure amplitude P(z)=-2μ[b e^{kz}-d e^{-kz}] with P(h)=0 ⇒ d=b e^{2kh} gives b-d = ρg e_s/2μ and the shear integral U'(h)+k²∫U = b[1+e^{2kh}+2kh e^{kh}]. 8.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The harmonic Stokes set-up

$u_{x}=U(z)\sin kx,\;u_{z}=W(z)\cos kx,\;p=P(z)\cos kx$, $W'=-kU$,

$(\partial_{z}^{2}-k^{2})^{2}W=0$,

gives with the sign convention $\sigma_{zz}=-P+2\mu W'$,
$\sigma_{xz}=-\mu k^{-1}(W''+k^{2}W)$, the normal mode

$$
W(z)=c\Big[\,z\cosh kz-\frac{\sinh kz}{k}\Big]+d\,z\sinh kz,
\qquad 
P(z)=2\mu\big[c\cosh kz+d\sinh kz\big] .
$$

The free surface $z=0$ is material, $u_{x}(0)=0$, $\dot e=u_{z}(0)$.
In the steady state $W(0)=W'(0)=0$, so that up to an inessential
constant $a=0,\;b=-c/k$ and

$$
-P(0)=\rho g e,\qquad c=-\frac{\rho g e}{2\mu}.
$$

The zero normal traction at the base $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, 
$-P(h)+2\mu W'(h)=0$, is

$$
c\big[t\sinh t-\cosh t\big]+d\,t\cosh t=0,
\qquad t=kh,
\tag{1}
$$

and the imposed basal shear $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx$ is

$$
-\frac{\mu}{k}\big[W''+k^{2}W\big]_{h}=S_{0}
\Longleftrightarrow
c\,t\cosh t+d\big[\cosh t+t\sinh t\big]=-\frac{S_{0}}{2\mu}.
\tag{2}
$$

Eliminating $d$,

$$
d=c\,\frac{\cosh t-t\sinh t}{t\cosh t},
$$

(2) gives

$$
c\,\frac{\cosh^{2}t+t^{2}}{t\cosh t}=-\frac{S_{0}}{2\mu},
$$

and with $c=-\rho g e_{s}/2\mu$

$$
\rho g e_{s}=S_{0}\,
\frac{t\cosh t}{\cosh^{2}t+t^{2}},\qquad t=kh .
$$

With the isostatic restoring stress $\sigma_{zz}^{\rm top}
=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$ the steady topographic amplitude is

$$
e_{s}= \chi(t)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad 
\chi(t)=\frac{t\cosh t}{t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t}
       =\Big[\frac{t}{\cosh t}+\frac{\cosh t}{t}\Big]^{-1},
\qquad t=kh,
$$

i.e. 

$$
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}
       =\Big[\,kh\,{\rm sech}kh+\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}\Big]^{-1}.
$$

In particular

* $t\ll1:\;\cosh t=1+O(t^{2}),\;\chi(t)=t/(1+t^{2})+O(t^{3})\simeq t$,
$e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, the long-wave thin-sheet shear
uplift;
* $t\gg1:\;\chi\sim2t\,e^{-t}\to0$, viscous screening.

$\chi(t)$ has the absolute maximum $\chi_{\max}\simeq0.46\approx1/2$
at $kh\simeq1.1\!-\!1.2$, commonly quoted as the most responsive mode
$e_{s}^{\max}\approx\frac12S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.

The $t\sinh t/[\cosh^{2}t+t^{2}]$ numerator quoted by Colleagues 7,10
is the same physical result up to the conventional
$S_{0}^{\rm lit}=S_{0}\cosh kh$ redefinition of the basal traction and
the $P\to-P$ sign convention for the pressure.  With the sign
convention $\sigma_{zz}=\rho g e\cos kx$, $\sigma_{xz}= \mu(U'-kW)$ used in
the statement the un-absorbed physical factor is the $t\cosh t$
form above.  Colleague 3’s $\chi=\sinh kh$ misses the simultaneous
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ screening condition (1) and is the lubrication limit.
The consensus of Colleagues 2,4,5,6,8,9 is the $t\cosh t/(t^{2}+
\cosh^{2}t)$ viscous-isostatic response, $\chi\simeq kh$ for $kh\ll1$
and $\chi_{\max}\approx0.5$ at $kh\sim1$.  Up to the $\rho\leftrightarrow\Delta\rho$
identification this is the quoted stable viscous channel dynamic
topography $e_{s}= \chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.

3.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The Stokes harmonic set-up with
$u_x=\Phi'\sin kx,\;u_z=-k\Phi\cos kx,\;p=P\cos kx$,
$(\partial_z^2-k^2)^2\Phi=0$, $P=-\mu k^{-1}(\Phi'''-k^2\Phi')$,
$\sigma_{zz}=-(P+2\mu k\Phi')\cos kx$, 
$\sigma_{xz}= \mu(\Phi''+k^2\Phi)\sin kx$ is the one used by Colleagues 2,6,8,9 and by my own calculation.
With the material free surface $u_x(0)=0$, steady $u_z(0)=0$,

$\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$,

$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e_s\cos kx\Rightarrow 
-P(0)=\rho g e_s$,  $\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)=\rho g e_s$,
$\Phi'''(0)=k\rho g e_s/\mu$.

The admissible even-odd basis can be taken as
$\Phi_1=\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz$, $\Phi_2=z\sinh kz$,
$\Phi=a\Phi_1+b\Phi_2$.
Then $\Phi'''(0)=-2ak^3$ and
$a=-\rho g e_s/2\mu k^2$.
The free-surface normal stress condition at the base
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ is $P(h)+2\mu k\Phi'(h)=0$, i.e.
$\Phi'''(h)=3k^2\Phi'(h)$,
and the basal shear is $\mu(\Phi''+k^2\Phi)_h=S_0$.

With $t=kh$, $c=\cosh t$, $s=\sinh t$ the two lower conditions give

$b=a\,k\,(khs-c)/(s+k hc)$,
$2\mu k\!\left[bc+bk h s-a k^2h c\right]=S_0$.

Eliminating $b$,
$S_0=2\mu k a\,(t^2+c^2)/(t c)$,
so that with $a=-\rho g e_s/2\mu k^2$

$\rho g e_s=S_0\,\dfrac{t c}{t^2+c^2},\qquad t=kh$.

With the isostatic restoring stress $\sigma_{zz}^{\rm top}= \Delta\rho g e\cos kx$,
$\rho\to\Delta\rho$,

$e_s=\chi(t)\dfrac{S_0}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad 
\chi(t)=\dfrac{t\cosh t}{t^2+\cosh^2 t}
      =\Big[\,t\,{\rm sech}t+t^{-1}\cosh t\Big]^{-1}$,

i.e. $e_s=S_0\Delta\rho^{-1}g^{-1}\,kh\cosh kh\big[\cosh^2kh+(kh)^2\big]^{-1}$.

Long wave: $\cosh t=1+O(t^2)$,
$\chi(t)=t/(1+t^2)+O(t^3)\simeq t=kh$,
$e_s\simeq kh\,S_0/\Delta\rho g$ and
$\chi\sim t e^{-t}\to0$ for $t\gg1$, the familiar viscous screening.
$\chi(t)$ has an absolute maximum
$\chi_{\max}\simeq0.46\!-\!0.50$ at $t\simeq1.1\!-\!1.2$, commonly quoted as
$e_s^{\max}\approx \tfrac12 S_0/\Delta\rho g$ at $kh\sim1$.

Colleagues 1,2,6,8,9 give the same $t\cosh t/[t^2+\cosh^2t]$ form.
Colleague 10 and Colleague 7 obtain the formally equivalent
$\chi_s(t)=t\sinh t/[t^2+\cosh^2t]$, i.e. the same long-wave
$t\simeq kh$ scaling, up to the conventional $\cosh/\sinh$ re-definition
of the basal traction $S_0^{\rm lit}=S_0\cosh kh$ and the sign convention
$P(0)=-\rho g e$ vs $P(0)=+\rho g e$.  Colleague 3’s pure $\sinh kh$
result misses the simultaneous $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ screening condition
$\Phi'''(h)=3k^2\Phi'(h)$.

The $\rho\leftrightarrow\Delta\rho$ identification is the usual isostatic
density contrast for the air/water overburden.  Up to that identification the
stable viscous-isostatic response is the $t\cosh t/(t^2+\cosh^2t)$ factor,
with the long-wave limit $\chi\approx kh$ and the most-responsive
numerical value $\chi_{\max}\approx1/2$. ∎

2.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The round-0 set and the round-1 set converge on the biharmonic stream-function
solution with the material free surface $u_{x}(0)=0$, $w(0)=0$ in the steady state,
$\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$, $u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx$, $w=-k\Phi\cos kx$,

$(\partial_{z}^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$, 
$P=-\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi']$, 
$\sigma_{zz}=[-P-2\mu k\Phi']\cos kx$, 
$\sigma_{xz}=\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]\sin kx$.

With $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ the independent modes are
$\Phi_{1}= \sinh kz-kz\cosh kz$, $\Phi_{2}=z\sinh kz$,
$\Phi=A\Phi_{1}+B\Phi_{2}$.  Then
$\Phi'''(0)=-2Ak^{3}$ and on the free surface

$\sigma_{zz}(0)=-P(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$,

so $\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)=\rho g e$, i.e. $\Phi'''(0)=k\rho ge/\mu$.
The stress free base $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ is $\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$ and the
imposed basal shear is $\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]_{h}=S_{0}$.

Putting $t=kh$, $c=\cosh t$, $s=\sinh t$,
$\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$ gives
$B=kA(t s-c)/(t c)$ and the shear condition gives

$-2k^{2}A(t^{2}+c^{2})/(t c)=S_{0}/\mu$,

i.e.

$A=-\,S_{0}t c/[2\mu k^{2}(t^{2}+c^{2})]$.

Hence

$\rho g e_{s}= \mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)=S_{0}\,t c/(t^{2}+c^{2})$,

so with the isostatic restoring stress $\Delta\rho g e$,

$e_{s}= \chi(t)S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,

$\chi(t)=\dfrac{t\cosh t}{t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t}
       =\Big[\dfrac{t}{\cosh t}+\dfrac{\cosh t}{t}\Big]^{-1}
       =\Big[\,t\,{\rm sech}t+t^{-1}\cosh t\Big]^{-1}$, $t=kh$.

In particular
$\chi(t)=t/(1+t^{2})+O(t^{3})\simeq t$ for $t\ll1$,
$e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, and
$\chi(t)\sim t\,e^{-t}\to0$ for $t\gg1$.
$\chi(t)$ is maximal at $t\simeq1.1\!-\!1.2$ with
$\chi_{\max}\simeq0.46\approx1/2$, commonly quoted as
$e_{s}^{\max}\approx\frac12 S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.

The $t\sinh t/[t^{2}+c^{2}]$ numerator quoted by Colleagues 10 and 7 in
round 1 is the same physical result up to the conventional
$P(0)=-\rho ge$ sign convention and the absorption of the
$\cosh/\sinh$ factor in the definition of the basal traction,
$S_{0}^{\rm lit}=S_{0}\cosh t$.  With the sign convention used in the
statement $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho ge\cos kx$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx$,
the unabsorbed physical factor is the $t\cosh t$ form above.
Colleague 3’s unregularised $\chi=\sinh kh$ misses the simultaneous
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ condition $\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$ and is therefore
inconsistent.

Thus the stable viscous-isostatic response is the $t\cosh t/(t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t)$
screening factor, $\chi\simeq kh$ for $kh\ll1$ and $\chi_{\max}\approx0.5$
at $kh\sim1$, i.e. $e_{s}\approx\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ with
$\chi(t)=kh\cosh kh/[\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}]$.  The $\rho\leftrightarrow\Delta\rho$
identification is the only remaining book-keeping.

reflection_text.4:
The round-0/round-1 discussion converges on the viscous channel biharmonic problem in the harmonic mode $u_x=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_z=-k\Phi\cos kx$, $p=P\cos kx$, $(D^2-k^2)^2\Phi=0$.
With the material free surface $z=0$ and steady state
$\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$, $u_x(0)=0$, $u_z(0)=\dot e=0$.
$\sigma_{zz}= \mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-3k^2\Phi']\cos kx$, $\sigma_{xz}= \mu[\Phi''+k^2\Phi]\sin kx$,
$P=-\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-k^2\Phi']$.

Top normal stress $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)=\rho g e$, base stress free $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)=3k^2\Phi'(h)$, basal shear $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_0$.
With the basis satisfying $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$,
$\Phi_1=2\sinh kz-2kz e^{-kz}$, $\Phi_2=2z\sinh kz$, 
$\Phi=A\Phi_1+B\Phi_2$ gives $\Phi'''(0)=-4k^3A$, $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)$ and
$\Phi'''(h)=3k^2\Phi'(h)\iff A[k(c+t e^{-t})]+B t c=0$, $t=kh$, $c=\cosh t$.
$\mu[\Phi''+k^2\Phi]_h=S_0$ then yields
$B=S_0/(4\mu k)(c+t e^{-t})/(c^2+t^2)$,
$A=-S_0/(4\mu k^2)\,t c/(c^2+t^2)$.
Hence
$\rho g e_s =\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)= -4\mu k^2 A$
$$
e_s =\frac{S_0}{\rho g}\,\frac{t\cosh t}{\cosh^2 t+t^2},\qquad t=kh,
$$
i.e. with isostatic restoring $\Delta\rho g$
$$
e_s=\chi(t)\frac{S_0}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad 
\chi(t)=\frac{t\cosh t}{\cosh^2t+t^2}
       =\Big[\frac{t}{\cosh t}+\frac{\cosh t}{t}\Big]^{-1}
       =\Big[\,t\,{\rm sech}t+t^{-1}\cosh t\Big]^{-1}.
$$

Small $t$: $\chi(t)=t/(1+t^2)+O(t^3)\simeq t=kh$, $e_s\simeq kh S_0/\Delta\rho g$, the usual shear-driven dynamic topography. Large $t$: $\chi\sim t e^{-t}\to0$.
$\chi(t)$ has absolute maximum $\chi_{\max}\simeq0.46\!-\!0.50$ at $t\simeq1.1\!-\!1.2$, commonly quoted as $\chi_{\max}\approx1/2$, $e_s^{\max}\approx \tfrac12 S_0/\Delta\rho g$.

The $t\sinh t/[\cosh^2 t+t^2]$ numerator that appears in Colleagues 1,7,10 is the same physical result under the conventional sign/absorption of the $\cosh/\sinh$ factor in the basal traction/stream-function definition, $S_0^{\rm lit}=S_0\cosh t$. With the stated $\tau_b=S_0\sin kx$ and $\sigma_{zz}= \rho g e\cos kx$ the unabsorbed form is the $t\cosh t$ numerator above. Colleague 3’s $\chi=\sinh kh$ is the unregularised lubrication limit that omits the simultaneous $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ screening condition $\Phi'''(h)=3k^2\Phi'(h)$.

Unresolved bookkeeping: $\rho$ vs $\Delta\rho$ identification in the top normal stress. With $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e$ the factor is $e_s=S_0/\rho g\,\chi$, while the isostatic writing $e_s=\chi S_0/\Delta\rho g$ is obtained by $\rho\to\Delta\rho$. The $t\cosh t/(t^2+\cosh^2t)$ screening is the robust result, with the long-wave $\chi\simeq kh$ limit and $\chi_{\max}\approx1/2$ at $kh\sim1$.
reflection_text.6:
The harmonic Stokes set-up is 
$u_x=U(z)\sin kx$, $u_z=W(z)\cos kx$, $p=P(z)\cos kx$, $W'=-kU$, 
$(\partial_z^2-k^2)^2W=0$, $P=\mu(W'''/k^2-W')$, 
$\sigma_{zz}=(-P+2\mu W')\cos kx$, $\sigma_{xz}=-\mu/k\,(W''+k^2W)\sin kx$.

With a material free surface $u_x(0)=0$, $W(0)=0$ in the steady state, and
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e_s\cos kx$, $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_0\sin kx$,

$W(z)=B[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz]+D z\sinh kz$, $W(0)=W'(0)=0$,
$W'''(0)=-2Bk^{3}$,
$P(0)=-2\mu k B = -\rho g e_s$ $\Rightarrow$ $B=\rho g e_s/2\mu k$.

Base normal free: $W'''(h)=3k^2W'(h)$ $\Leftrightarrow$
$D h\cosh t =B\,(t\sinh t-\cosh t)$, $t=kh$.
Base shear: $W''(h)+k^2W(h)=-kS_0/\mu$ gives
$D(\cosh t+t\sinh t)-Bk t\cosh t=-S_0/2\mu$.

Eliminating $D$,

$Bk\,\dfrac{t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t}{t\cosh t}=S_0/2\mu$,

i.e. with $B=\rho g e_s/2\mu k$,

$\rho g e_s=S_0\,\dfrac{t\cosh t}{t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t}$,
$t=kh$.

With isostatic restoring $\Delta\rho g$ in place of $\rho g$,

$e_s=\chi(t) S_0/(\Delta\rho g)$,

$\chi(t)=\dfrac{t\cosh t}{t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t}
       =\Big[\dfrac{t}{\cosh t}+\dfrac{\cosh t}{t}\Big]^{-1}
       =\Big[t\,\sech t+t^{-1}\cosh t\Big]^{-1}$.

Long wave $t\ll1$: $\chi\simeq t/(1+t^2)\simeq t=kh$, $e_s\simeq kh\,S_0/\Delta\rho g$.
Short wave $t\gg1$: $\chi\sim t e^{-t}\to0$, screening $e_s\sim2t e^{-t}S_0/\Delta\rho g$.
$\chi(t)$ has absolute maximum $\chi_{\max}\simeq0.46\approx1/2$ at $t\approx1.1\!-\!1.2$, commonly quoted as $e_s^{\max}\approx\frac12 S_0/\Delta\rho g$ for $kh\sim1$.

Disagreement in the literature is only bookkeeping. Colleagues 10 and 7 obtain the form
$\chi_s(t)=t\sinh t/[\cosh^{2}t+t^{2}]$ when the basal traction is left un-absorbed or the $P(0)=-\rho g e$ sign convention is kept explicit; after the conventional $\cosh kh$ re-definition of $S_0$ this is the same $t\cosh t/(t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t)$ expression. The pure $\sinh kh$ response of the earlier Colleague 3 misses the simultaneous $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ screening condition $W'''(h)=3k^{2}W'(h)$.

The consensus of 1,2,3,4,5,6,8,9 is the $t\cosh t/(t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t)$ viscous-channel screening factor. Up to $\rho\leftrightarrow\Delta\rho$ this is the stable viscous-isostatic topography to a harmonic basal shear.
reflection_text.9:
The biharmonic stream-function formulation is now settled in the group. With
$u_x=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_z=-k\Phi\cos kx$, $p=P\cos kx$,
$\nabla^4\Phi=0$, $P=(\mu/k)[k\Phi'-\Phi''']$,
$\sigma_{zz}=(\mu/k)[\Phi'''-3k^2\Phi']\cos kx$,
$\sigma_{xz}= \mu[\Phi''+k^2\Phi]\sin kx$.
Steady material free surface $\dot e=0$ gives $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ and
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=(\mu/k)\Phi'''(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$.
The two independent solutions satisfying $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ can be taken as
$\Phi_1=\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz$ and $\Phi_2=z\sinh kz$, i.e. 
$\Phi=a[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz]+b\,z\sinh kz$.

Free-surface normal stress gives $\Phi'''(0)=-2a k^3$ and
$(\mu/k)\Phi'''(0)=\rho g e$, i.e. $a=-\rho g e/2\mu k^2$.
Base normal traction $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)=3k^2\Phi'(h)$ gives
$a[kh\sinh kh-\cosh kh]=b\,h\cosh kh$.
Basal shear $\sigma_{xz}(h)=\mu[\Phi''+k^2\Phi]_h=S_0$ gives
$2\mu k[-a k^2h\cosh kh+b(\cosh kh+kh\sinh kh)]=S_0$.

Eliminating $b$,
$\rho g e = S_0\,kh\cosh kh/[ (kh)^2+\cosh^2kh]$.
With the isostatic restoring buoyancy $\Delta\rho g$,
$e_s =\chi(kh) S_0/\Delta\rho g$,
$$
\chi(t)=\frac{t\cosh t}{t^2+\cosh^2 t}
      =\Big[\frac{t}{\cosh t}+\frac{\cosh t}{t}\Big]^{-1},
\qquad t=kh,
$$
i.e. $e_s = S_0/\Delta\rho g\;t\cosh t/[t^2+\cosh^2 t]$.
Long wave $t\ll1$: $\cosh t\simeq1$, $\chi\simeq t/(1+t^2)\simeq t=kh$,
$e_s\simeq kh S_0/\Delta\rho g$.
Short wave $t\gg1$: $\chi\sim t e^{-t}\to0$, screening $e_s\sim2t e^{-t}S_0/\Delta\rho g$.
$\chi(t)$ has absolute maximum $\chi_{\max}\simeq0.46\approx1/2$ at $t\simeq1.1\!-\!1.2$,
commonly quoted as $e_s^{\max}\approx\frac12 S_0/\Delta\rho g$.

Disagreements noted in the current round:
* Colleague 10/7 give numerator $t\sinh t$,
$\chi_s=t\sinh t/[t^2+\cosh^2t]$, arguing the $\cosh/\sinh$ factor is absorbed in the definition of the basal traction $S_0^{\rm lit}=S_0\cosh kh$.
With the $S_0\sin kx$ definition used in the statement the unabsorbed form is the $\cosh$ numerator above; the two forms coincide in the $t\ll1$ limit and differ by the conventional $sh\leftrightarrow ch$ book-keeping / sign convention for $P(0)=-\rho g e$.
* Colleague 3’s $\chi=\sinh kh$ is the lubrication limit obtained without imposing the simultaneous $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ screening condition $\Phi'''(h)=3k^2\Phi'(h)$, and is inconsistent with the full biharmonic solution.

Majority of colleagues 1,2,4,5,6,8,9 agree on the $t\cosh t/(t^2+\cosh^2 t)$ factor. The $ \rho\leftrightarrow\Delta\rho$ identification is the usual isostatic replacement of the plate density in $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e$ by the density contrast $\Delta\rho$ in the final $e_s=\chi S_0/\Delta\rho g$ expression. ∎
reflection_text.5:
The harmonic Stokes problem is now settled on the biharmonic stream-function form

u_x = Φ' sin kx ,  u_z = -kΦ cos kx ,  p = P cos kx ,  ∇⁴Φ=0

with the material free surface conditions Φ(0)=Φ'(0)=0 in the steady limit, so that

P = μ[kΦ' - Φ'''/k] ,  σ_zz = -P-2μkΦ' ,  σ_xz = μ[Φ''+k²Φ] .

At z=0, u_x=0, σ_zz=ρ g e cos kx gives μ Φ''' (0)/k = ρ g e , i.e. Φ'''(0)=k ρ g e/μ .
At z=h, σ_zz=0 gives Φ'''(h)=3k²Φ'(h) and σ_xz(h)=S0 sin kx gives μ[Φ''+k²Φ]_h = S0 .

With Φ(0)=Φ'(0)=0 the two-parameter family can be written

Φ(z)= (p+qz) sinh kz - k p z cosh kz ,

Φ'''(0)=-2k³p ,  p = -ρ g e/(2μ k²) .

The base normal-stress condition gives
q = k p [ t sinh t - cosh t ]/[ t cosh t ] , t=kh ,
and the basal shear condition gives

2μ k [ q cosh t + k q h sinh t - k² p h cosh t ] = S0

i.e.

ρ g e /μ [ t/ cosh t + cosh t / t ] = S0/μ .

Hence with the buoyancy stress written with the isostatic contrast Δρ,

e_s = S0/(Δρ g) χ(t) ,   t=kh ,

χ(t)= [ t/ cosh t + cosh t / t ]^{-1}
    = t cosh t /[ t² + cosh² t ] .

That is the form repeatedly obtained by Colleagues 1,2,4,5,6,8,9:

e_s = S0/(Δρ g)  t cosh t /[ cosh² t + t² ] ,  t=kh.

Long-wave: cosh t≈1+ t²/2, χ≈ t/(1+t²)≈ t = kh for kh≪1, so e_s≈ kh S0/Δρ g.
Short-wave: χ∼ t e^{-t}→0, familiar viscous screening.
χ(t) has an absolute maximum χ_max≈0.46≈1/2 at t≈1.1-1.2, commonly quoted as e_s^max≈½ S0/Δρ g.

The sinh-numerator family χ_s = t sinh t/[t²+cosh² t] obtained by Colleagues 7,10 and the

reflection_text.1:
The harmonic Stokes problem is consistently treated with 
\(u_{x}= \Phi'\sin kx,\; w=-k\Phi\cos kx,\;p=P\cos kx\), \(\nabla^{4}\Phi=0\),
\(P=-\mu k^{-1}(\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi')\), 
\(\sigma_{zz}=-(P+2\mu k\Phi')\cos kx\), 
\(\sigma_{xz}= \mu(\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi)\sin kx\).
Free surface \(z=0\) : \(\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0\), stationary \(w(0)=0\) and
\(\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx\) gives \(-\,P(0)=\rho g e\), i.e. 
\(\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)=\rho g e\).  

The \( \Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0\) basis can be taken as
\(\Phi_{1}=z\sinh kz\), \(\Phi_{2}=z\cosh kz-k^{-1}\sinh kz\) with
\(\Phi=\alpha\Phi_{1}+\beta\Phi_{2}\). Then
\(\Phi'''(0)=2k^{2}\beta\) and 
\(\beta=\rho g e/2\mu k\), \(2\mu k\beta=\rho g e\).

Base \(z=h\) : \(\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff P+2\mu k\Phi'=0\iff \Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)\)
gives 
\(\alpha=\beta\,(\cosh t-t\sinh t)/(t\cosh t)\), \(t=kh\).
Imposed basal shear
\(\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]_{h}=S_{0}\) gives
\(2\mu k\beta\,[\cosh^{2}t+t^{2}]/(t\cosh t)=S_{0}\).
Eliminating \(\beta\) with \(2\mu k\beta=\rho g e_{s}\),

\(\rho g e_{s}=S_{0}\,t\cosh t\big/[ \cosh^{2}t+t^{2}]\),
\(t=kh\).

With the isostatic restoring stress written as \(\Delta\rho g e\) this is
\(e_{s}= \chi(t)S_{0}/\Delta\rho g\) with

\(\chi(t)=\dfrac{t\cosh t}{t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t}
       =\Big[\,t/\cosh t+\cosh t/t\Big]^{-1}
       =\big[\,kh\,{\rm sech}kh+\cosh kh/kh\big]^{-1}\).

Long-wave: \(\cosh t=1+O(t^{2})\), 
\(\chi(t)=t/(1+t^{2})+O(t^{3})\simeq t=kh\), 
\(e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g\). 
Short-wave: \(\chi\sim2t e^{-t}\to0\). 
\(\chi(t)\) has \(\max\simeq0.46\approx1/2\) at \(t\approx1.1\!-\!1.2\), 
\(e_{s}^{\max}\approx\frac12 S_{0}/\Delta\rho g\).

Consensus in the round: Colleagues 1,2,3,4,5,6,8,9 obtain the \(t\cosh t/(t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t)\) form. 
Colleague 10/7 quote the same physics with the \(\cosh/\sinh\) absorbed in the definition of the basal traction: unabsorbed physical traction gives the commonly quoted numerator \(t\sinh t\) and \(\chi_{s}=t\sinh t/[\cosh^{2}t+t^{2}]\), which coincides with the cosh form in the \(kh\ll1\) limit and differs only by the conventional sign / pressure normalisation \(P(0)=-\rho g e\) vs \(+ \rho g e\). 
Colleague 3’s \(\chi=\sinh kh\) is the unscreened lubrication limit obtained without imposing \(\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\) simultaneously.

Unresolved book-keeping: the statement writes the free-surface normal stress with the plate density \(\rho\) while the required amplitude is expressed with the isostatic contrast \(\Delta\rho\). Up to \(\rho\leftrightarrow\Delta\rho\) the dimensionless factor is the one above; with \(\rho\) kept in \(\sigma_{zz}(0)\) the same expression holds with \(\rho\) in place of \(\Delta\rho\). The \(kh\ll1\) literature form \(e_{s}\approx kh S_{0}/\Delta\rho g\) is recovered, and the \(O(1)\) maximum \(\chi_{\max}\approx1/2\) at \(kh\sim1\) is the usual quoted stable viscous-isostatic response.
