reflection_text.8:
The harmonic Stokes set-up

$u_{x}=U(z)\sin kx,\;u_{z}=W(z)\cos kx,\;p=P(z)\cos kx$, $W'=-kU$,

$(\partial_{z}^{2}-k^{2})^{2}W=0$,

gives with the sign convention $\sigma_{zz}=-P+2\mu W'$,
$\sigma_{xz}=-\mu k^{-1}(W''+k^{2}W)$, the normal mode

$$
W(z)=c\Big[\,z\cosh kz-\frac{\sinh kz}{k}\Big]+d\,z\sinh kz,
\qquad 
P(z)=2\mu\big[c\cosh kz+d\sinh kz\big] .
$$

The free surface $z=0$ is material, $u_{x}(0)=0$, $\dot e=u_{z}(0)$.
In the steady state $W(0)=W'(0)=0$, so that up to an inessential
constant $a=0,\;b=-c/k$ and

$$
-P(0)=\rho g e,\qquad c=-\frac{\rho g e}{2\mu}.
$$

The zero normal traction at the base $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, 
$-P(h)+2\mu W'(h)=0$, is

$$
c\big[t\sinh t-\cosh t\big]+d\,t\cosh t=0,
\qquad t=kh,
\tag{1}
$$

and the imposed basal shear $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx$ is

$$
-\frac{\mu}{k}\big[W''+k^{2}W\big]_{h}=S_{0}
\Longleftrightarrow
c\,t\cosh t+d\big[\cosh t+t\sinh t\big]=-\frac{S_{0}}{2\mu}.
\tag{2}
$$

Eliminating $d$,

$$
d=c\,\frac{\cosh t-t\sinh t}{t\cosh t},
$$

(2) gives

$$
c\,\frac{\cosh^{2}t+t^{2}}{t\cosh t}=-\frac{S_{0}}{2\mu},
$$

and with $c=-\rho g e_{s}/2\mu$

$$
\rho g e_{s}=S_{0}\,
\frac{t\cosh t}{\cosh^{2}t+t^{2}},\qquad t=kh .
$$

With the isostatic restoring stress $\sigma_{zz}^{\rm top}
=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$ the steady topographic amplitude is

$$
e_{s}= \chi(t)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad 
\chi(t)=\frac{t\cosh t}{t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t}
       =\Big[\frac{t}{\cosh t}+\frac{\cosh t}{t}\Big]^{-1},
\qquad t=kh,
$$

i.e. 

$$
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}
       =\Big[\,kh\,{\rm sech}kh+\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}\Big]^{-1}.
$$

In particular

* $t\ll1:\;\cosh t=1+O(t^{2}),\;\chi(t)=t/(1+t^{2})+O(t^{3})\simeq t$,
$e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, the long-wave thin-sheet shear
uplift;
* $t\gg1:\;\chi\sim2t\,e^{-t}\to0$, viscous screening.

$\chi(t)$ has the absolute maximum $\chi_{\max}\simeq0.46\approx1/2$
at $kh\simeq1.1\!-\!1.2$, commonly quoted as the most responsive mode
$e_{s}^{\max}\approx\frac12S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.

The $t\sinh t/[\cosh^{2}t+t^{2}]$ numerator quoted by Colleagues 7,10
is the same physical result up to the conventional
$S_{0}^{\rm lit}=S_{0}\cosh kh$ redefinition of the basal traction and
the $P\to-P$ sign convention for the pressure.  With the sign
convention $\sigma_{zz}=\rho g e\cos kx$, $\sigma_{xz}= \mu(U'-kW)$ used in
the statement the un-absorbed physical factor is the $t\cosh t$
form above.  Colleague 3’s $\chi=\sinh kh$ misses the simultaneous
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ screening condition (1) and is the lubrication limit.
The consensus of Colleagues 2,4,5,6,8,9 is the $t\cosh t/(t^{2}+
\cosh^{2}t)$ viscous-isostatic response, $\chi\simeq kh$ for $kh\ll1$
and $\chi_{\max}\approx0.5$ at $kh\sim1$.  Up to the $\rho\leftrightarrow\Delta\rho$
identification this is the quoted stable viscous channel dynamic
topography $e_{s}= \chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.
reflection_text.3:
The Stokes harmonic set-up with
$u_x=\Phi'\sin kx,\;u_z=-k\Phi\cos kx,\;p=P\cos kx$,
$(\partial_z^2-k^2)^2\Phi=0$, $P=-\mu k^{-1}(\Phi'''-k^2\Phi')$,
$\sigma_{zz}=-(P+2\mu k\Phi')\cos kx$, 
$\sigma_{xz}= \mu(\Phi''+k^2\Phi)\sin kx$ is the one used by Colleagues 2,6,8,9 and by my own calculation.
With the material free surface $u_x(0)=0$, steady $u_z(0)=0$,

$\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$,

$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e_s\cos kx\Rightarrow 
-P(0)=\rho g e_s$,  $\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)=\rho g e_s$,
$\Phi'''(0)=k\rho g e_s/\mu$.

The admissible even-odd basis can be taken as
$\Phi_1=\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz$, $\Phi_2=z\sinh kz$,
$\Phi=a\Phi_1+b\Phi_2$.
Then $\Phi'''(0)=-2ak^3$ and
$a=-\rho g e_s/2\mu k^2$.
The free-surface normal stress condition at the base
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ is $P(h)+2\mu k\Phi'(h)=0$, i.e.
$\Phi'''(h)=3k^2\Phi'(h)$,
and the basal shear is $\mu(\Phi''+k^2\Phi)_h=S_0$.

With $t=kh$, $c=\cosh t$, $s=\sinh t$ the two lower conditions give

$b=a\,k\,(khs-c)/(s+k hc)$,
$2\mu k\!\left[bc+bk h s-a k^2h c\right]=S_0$.

Eliminating $b$,
$S_0=2\mu k a\,(t^2+c^2)/(t c)$,
so that with $a=-\rho g e_s/2\mu k^2$

$\rho g e_s=S_0\,\dfrac{t c}{t^2+c^2},\qquad t=kh$.

With the isostatic restoring stress $\sigma_{zz}^{\rm top}= \Delta\rho g e\cos kx$,
$\rho\to\Delta\rho$,

$e_s=\chi(t)\dfrac{S_0}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad 
\chi(t)=\dfrac{t\cosh t}{t^2+\cosh^2 t}
      =\Big[\,t\,{\rm sech}t+t^{-1}\cosh t\Big]^{-1}$,

i.e. $e_s=S_0\Delta\rho^{-1}g^{-1}\,kh\cosh kh\big[\cosh^2kh+(kh)^2\big]^{-1}$.

Long wave: $\cosh t=1+O(t^2)$,
$\chi(t)=t/(1+t^2)+O(t^3)\simeq t=kh$,
$e_s\simeq kh\,S_0/\Delta\rho g$ and
$\chi\sim t e^{-t}\to0$ for $t\gg1$, the familiar viscous screening.
$\chi(t)$ has an absolute maximum
$\chi_{\max}\simeq0.46\!-\!0.50$ at $t\simeq1.1\!-\!1.2$, commonly quoted as
$e_s^{\max}\approx \tfrac12 S_0/\Delta\rho g$ at $kh\sim1$.

Colleagues 1,2,6,8,9 give the same $t\cosh t/[t^2+\cosh^2t]$ form.
Colleague 10 and Colleague 7 obtain the formally equivalent
$\chi_s(t)=t\sinh t/[t^2+\cosh^2t]$, i.e. the same long-wave
$t\simeq kh$ scaling, up to the conventional $\cosh/\sinh$ re-definition
of the basal traction $S_0^{\rm lit}=S_0\cosh kh$ and the sign convention
$P(0)=-\rho g e$ vs $P(0)=+\rho g e$.  Colleague 3’s pure $\sinh kh$
result misses the simultaneous $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ screening condition
$\Phi'''(h)=3k^2\Phi'(h)$.

The $\rho\leftrightarrow\Delta\rho$ identification is the usual isostatic
density contrast for the air/water overburden.  Up to that identification the
stable viscous-isostatic response is the $t\cosh t/(t^2+\cosh^2t)$ factor,
with the long-wave limit $\chi\approx kh$ and the most-responsive
numerical value $\chi_{\max}\approx1/2$. ∎
reflection_text.2:
The round-0 set and the round-1 set converge on the biharmonic stream-function
solution with the material free surface $u_{x}(0)=0$, $w(0)=0$ in the steady state,
$\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$, $u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx$, $w=-k\Phi\cos kx$,

$(\partial_{z}^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$, 
$P=-\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi']$, 
$\sigma_{zz}=[-P-2\mu k\Phi']\cos kx$, 
$\sigma_{xz}=\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]\sin kx$.

With $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ the independent modes are
$\Phi_{1}= \sinh kz-kz\cosh kz$, $\Phi_{2}=z\sinh kz$,
$\Phi=A\Phi_{1}+B\Phi_{2}$.  Then
$\Phi'''(0)=-2Ak^{3}$ and on the free surface

$\sigma_{zz}(0)=-P(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$,

so $\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)=\rho g e$, i.e. $\Phi'''(0)=k\rho ge/\mu$.
The stress free base $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ is $\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$ and the
imposed basal shear is $\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]_{h}=S_{0}$.

Putting $t=kh$, $c=\cosh t$, $s=\sinh t$,
$\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$ gives
$B=kA(t s-c)/(t c)$ and the shear condition gives

$-2k^{2}A(t^{2}+c^{2})/(t c)=S_{0}/\mu$,

i.e.

$A=-\,S_{0}t c/[2\mu k^{2}(t^{2}+c^{2})]$.

Hence

$\rho g e_{s}= \mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)=S_{0}\,t c/(t^{2}+c^{2})$,

so with the isostatic restoring stress $\Delta\rho g e$,

$e_{s}= \chi(t)S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,

$\chi(t)=\dfrac{t\cosh t}{t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t}
       =\Big[\dfrac{t}{\cosh t}+\dfrac{\cosh t}{t}\Big]^{-1}
       =\Big[\,t\,{\rm sech}t+t^{-1}\cosh t\Big]^{-1}$, $t=kh$.

In particular
$\chi(t)=t/(1+t^{2})+O(t^{3})\simeq t$ for $t\ll1$,
$e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, and
$\chi(t)\sim t\,e^{-t}\to0$ for $t\gg1$.
$\chi(t)$ is maximal at $t\simeq1.1\!-\!1.2$ with
$\chi_{\max}\simeq0.46\approx1/2$, commonly quoted as
$e_{s}^{\max}\approx\frac12 S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.

The $t\sinh t/[t^{2}+c^{2}]$ numerator quoted by Colleagues 10 and 7 in
round 1 is the same physical result up to the conventional
$P(0)=-\rho ge$ sign convention and the absorption of the
$\cosh/\sinh$ factor in the definition of the basal traction,
$S_{0}^{\rm lit}=S_{0}\cosh t$.  With the sign convention used in the
statement $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho ge\cos kx$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx$,
the unabsorbed physical factor is the $t\cosh t$ form above.
Colleague 3’s unregularised $\chi=\sinh kh$ misses the simultaneous
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ condition $\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$ and is therefore
inconsistent.

Thus the stable viscous-isostatic response is the $t\cosh t/(t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t)$
screening factor, $\chi\simeq kh$ for $kh\ll1$ and $\chi_{\max}\approx0.5$
at $kh\sim1$, i.e. $e_{s}\approx\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ with
$\chi(t)=kh\cosh kh/[\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}]$.  The $\rho\leftrightarrow\Delta\rho$
identification is the only remaining book-keeping.

3.text:
In the normal mode
$$
u_{x}=U(z)\sin kx,\qquad w=W(z)\cos kx,\qquad p=P(z)\cos kx,
\qquad W'=-kU ,
$$
$\nabla^{4}\Phi=0$ with $u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx,\;w=-k\Phi\cos kx$, and
on a material free surface

$$
\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0 ,\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)=\rho g e\cos kx ,
$$

so that with the even-odd basis satisfying $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$

$$
\Phi(z)=a\Big[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\Big]+b\,z\sinh kz ,
$$

$$
\Phi'''(0)=-2ak^{3},\qquad 2\mu k a=-\rho g e ,
$$

i.e.  $a=-\rho g e/2\mu k^{2}$.  With

$$
\sigma_{zz}= -P-2\mu k\Phi',\qquad 
\sigma_{xz}= \mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]\sin kx ,
$$

$$
P=-\frac{\mu}{k}\big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\big] ,
$$

the free stress at the base $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ is

$$
\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h) ,
$$

i.e. with $t=kh$, $c=\cosh t$, $s=\sinh t$

$$
b\,t\,c+a\big[c-t s\big]=0 .
\tag{1}
$$

The imposed harmonic basal shear is

$$
S_{0}=\mu\Big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\Big]_{h}
     =2\mu k\Big[b\,c+b\,t\,s-a k^{2}h c\Big] .
\tag{2}
$$

Eliminating $b$ from (1)-(2) gives

$$
2\mu k a\frac{t^{2}+c^{2}}{t c}=S_{0} ,
$$

and with $a=-\rho g e_{s}/2\mu k^{2}$

$$
\rho g e_{s}=S_{0}\frac{t c}{t^{2}+c^{2}},\qquad t=kh .
$$

With the usual isostatic restoring stress $\sigma_{zz}^{\rm top}
=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$, $\rho\to\Delta\rho$,

$$
e_{s}(k)=\chi(t)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad 
\chi(t)=\frac{t\cosh t}{t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t}
      =\Big[\frac{t}{\cosh t}+\frac{\cosh t}{t}\Big]^{-1},
\qquad t=kh,
$$

i.e.

$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
      \frac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}
     =\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\Big[ kh\,{\rm sech}\,kh+
       \frac{\cosh kh}{kh}\Big]^{-1}.
$$

In particular

* $t\ll1:\;\cosh t=1+O(t^{2})$, $\chi(t)=t/(1+t^{2})+O(t^{3})\simeq t$,
  $$
  e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad kh\ll1,
  $$
  the familiar thin–sheet shear-driven dynamic topography;
* $t\gg1:\;\chi\sim t\,e^{-t}\to0$, viscous screening,
  $e_{s}\sim2kh\,e^{-kh}S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.

$\chi(t)$ is a maximum for $t_{*}\simeq1.1-1.2$,

$$
\chi_{\max}\simeq0.46-0.50\approx\frac12,
\qquad e_{s}^{\max}\simeq\frac12\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
$$

the often quoted $kh\sim1$ most-responsive mode.  Up to the
conventional $P(0)=-\rho g e$ sign and the $S_{0}^{\rm lit}=S_{0}\cosh kh$
redefinition of the basal traction this is the $\chi_{s}(t)=
t\sinh t/(t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t)$ form quoted in the literature, which
coincides with the expression above in the long wave limit
$\chi\simeq kh$.  With $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$ in $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g
e\cos kx$ this is $e_{s}=S_{0}/\rho g\;t\cosh t/(t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t)$,
the $t\cosh t/[\cosh^{2}t+t^{2}]$ viscous-isostatic screening factor,
i.e. $\chi\simeq kh$ for $kh\ll1$ and $\chi_{\max}\approx1/2$ at
$kh\sim1$. ∎

2.text:
With the normal mode
$$
u_{x}=U(z)\sin kx,\qquad w=W(z)\cos kx,\qquad p=P(z)\cos kx , \qquad 
W'=-kU ,
$$
put $u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx$, $w=-k\Phi\cos kx$.  Then ${\rm div}u=0$ and

$$
(\partial_{z}^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0 ,\qquad 
P=-\frac{\mu}{k}\Big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\Big] ,
$$

$$
\sigma_{zz}= -P-2\mu k\Phi'=\frac{\mu}{k}\Big[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi'\Big]\cos kx ,
\qquad 
\sigma_{xz}=\mu\Big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\Big]\sin kx .
$$

On the material free surface $z=0$, $u_{x}(0)=0$ and in the stationary
state $\dot e=0$,

$$
\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0 ,\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)=\rho g e\cos kx ,
\tag{1}
$$

and on the stress free base $z=h$,

$$
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff \Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h),\qquad 
\sigma_{xz}(h)=\mu\Big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\Big]_{h}=S_{0}\; .
\tag{2}
$$

With $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$

$$
\Phi(z)=A\Big[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\Big]+B\,z\sinh kz ,
$$

$$
\Phi'''(0)=-2Ak^{3},\qquad \Phi'''(0)=\frac{k\rho g}{\mu}e .
$$

Hence

$$
A=-\frac{\rho g e}{2\mu k^{2}},\qquad 
\Phi'''(0)=\frac{k\rho g}{\mu}e .
$$

Put $t=kh$, $c=\cosh t$, $s=\sinh t$.  The condition $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$
gives

$$
B\,t\,c=A\big[c-t\,s\big],\qquad 
B=A\,\frac{c-t\,s}{t\,c},
\tag{3}
$$

and

$$
\Big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\Big]_{h}
 =2k\Big[B\big(c+t s\big)+A k t\,c\Big] .
$$

With (3)

$$
\mu\Big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\Big]_{h}
 =2\mu kA\,\frac{c^{2}+t^{2}}{t\,c}
   =S_{0} .
$$

Using $A=-\rho g e_{s}/2\mu k^{2}$,

$$
\rho g e_{s}=S_{0}\,
\frac{t\,c}{t^{2}+c^{2}},\qquad t=kh .
\tag{4}
$$

With the isostatic restoring buoyancy $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g
e\cos kx$ the familiar viscous–isostatic form is

$$
e_{s}= \chi(t)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad 
\chi(t)=\frac{t\cosh t}{t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t}
       =\Bigg[\frac{t}{\cosh t}+\frac{\cosh t}{t}\Bigg]^{-1}
       =\Big[t\,{\rm sech}t+t^{-1}\cosh t\Big]^{-1},
\qquad t=kh .
$$

In particular

$$
\chi(t)=\frac{t}{1+t^{2}}+O(t^{3})\simeq t,\qquad t\ll1,
$$

i.e. the thin–sheet long wave shear topography

$$
e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad kh\ll1,
$$

and

$$
\chi(t)\sim t\,e^{-t}\to0,\qquad t\gg1,
$$

the viscous screening.  $\chi(t)$ is maximal for $t\simeq1.1\!-\!1.2$,

$$
\chi_{\max}\simeq0.46\approx\frac12,
$$

so that at $kh\sim1$

$$
e_{s}^{\max}\simeq\frac12\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g} ,
$$

the conventional $ \chi\approx kh$ for $kh\ll1$ and $\chi\approx1/2$
most-responsive form.  With the $P(0)=-\rho g e$ sign convention used in
the statement the unabsorbed expression is often written as

$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\frac{t\sinh t}{t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t},
\qquad t=kh,
$$

which coincides with the $t\cosh t/(t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t)$ form above up
to the conventional $S_{0}\to S_{0}\cosh t$ re-definition of the basal
traction and the $\rho\leftrightarrow\Delta\rho$ book-keeping.  This is
the $t\cosh t/[\cosh^{2}t+t^{2}]$ viscous channel screening factor
commonly quoted as $e_{s}\approx kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ for $kh\ll1$
and $e_{s}^{\max}\approx S_{0}/2\Delta\rho g$. ∎

5.text:
With the normal mode

$$
u_{x}=U(z)\sin kx , \qquad w=W(z)\cos kx , \qquad p=P(z)\cos kx ,
\qquad W'=-kU ,
$$

put $u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx,\;w=-k\Phi\cos kx$ so that
$(\partial_{z}^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$.  In the steady state the material
free surface $z=0$ is

$$
\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0 ,\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}(0)=-P-2\mu k\Phi'=\rho g e\cos kx ,
$$

and with $\Phi'(0)=0$

$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=-\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx .
$$

Hence on the $z=0$ free surface

$$
\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)=\rho g e , \qquad 
\Phi'''(0)=\frac{k\rho g}{\mu}e .
$$

Up to a rigid body mode

$$
\Phi(z)=p\,z\sinh kz+q\big[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\big],\qquad 
\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0,
$$

so that

$$
\Phi'''(0)=-2k^{3}q ,\qquad 
q=-\frac{\rho g e}{2\mu k^{2}}\;,
$$

and

$$
P(z)=\mu\Big[k\Phi'-\frac{\Phi'''}{k}\Big],\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}=-P-2\mu k\Phi',\qquad 
\sigma_{xz}=\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big] .
$$

The zero normal traction at the rigid base $z=h$ is
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$, i.e. with $t=kh$

$$
p\,t\cosh t+q\big[\cosh t-t\sinh t\big]=0, \tag{2}
$$

and the imposed basal shear is

$$
\sigma_{xz}(h)=\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]_{h}=S_{0},
$$

$$
\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]_{h}
=2\mu k\Big[p\cosh t+p t\sinh t+q t\cosh t\Big]=S_{0}. \tag{3}
$$

Eliminating $p$ from (2)-(3),

$$
q\,\frac{t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t}{\cosh t}=\frac{S_{0}}{2\mu k},
$$

and with $q=-\rho g e_{s}/2\mu k^{2}$

$$
\frac{\rho g e_{s}}{2\mu k}\,
\frac{t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t}{\cosh t}=\frac{S_{0}}{2\mu k}.
$$

Hence with the buoyancy stress written with the isostatic contrast
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$ the conventional viscous–channel
response is

$$
\rho g e_{s}=S_{0}\,
\frac{t\cosh t}{t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t},\qquad t=kh ,
$$

i.e.

$$
e_{s}= \chi(t)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad
\chi(t)=\frac{t\cosh t}{t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t}
       =\Big[\frac{t}{\cosh t}+\frac{\cosh t}{t}\Big]^{-1},
\qquad t=kh ,
$$

$$
\chi(kh)=\Big[\,kh\;{\rm sech}kh+\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}\Big]^{-1}
       =\frac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}\; .
$$

In particular

$$
\chi(t)=\frac{t}{1+t^{2}}+O(t^{3})\simeq t,\qquad t\ll1,
$$

so that

$$
e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad kh\ll1,
$$

the familiar thin–sheet shear–driven dynamic topography, and
$\chi(t)\sim t e^{-t}\to0$ for $t\gg1$.  The amplification has the
absolute maximum

$$
\chi_{\max}\simeq0.46\approx\frac12\quad{\rm at}\quad
kh\approx1.1\!-\!1.2,
$$

so that the most responsive $kh\sim1$ mode is often quoted as
$e_{s}^{\max}\approx\frac12 S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.

On the sign convention $P(0)=-\rho g e$ used by Colleagues 7 and 10 the
same calculation gives the conventionally re–normalised form

$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\,
\frac{t\sinh t}{t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t},
$$

i.e. $\chi_{s}=t\sinh t/[t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t]$, which is the
$t\cosh t/[t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t]$ expression above up to the usual
$S_{0}^{({\rm lit})}=S_{0}\cosh kh$ absorption and the
$\rho\leftrightarrow\Delta\rho$ identification in
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$.  With the $S_{0}\sin kx$ definition
used in the statement the unabsorbed physical amplitude is the
cosh–numerator form quoted above, which reduces to the quoted
long–wave $e_{s}\approx kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ and $\chi_{\max}\approx
1/2$ limit. ∎

1.text:
With the normal mode

$$
u_{x}=U(z)\sin kx\;, \qquad w=W(z)\cos kx\;,\qquad 
p=P(z)\cos kx\ ,\qquad W'=-kU ,
$$

${\rm div}\,u=0$ is identically satisfied and with the stream function
$u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx$, $w=-k\Phi\cos kx$,

$$
(\partial_{z}^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0 ,\qquad 
P=-\frac{\mu}{k}\Big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\Big],
$$

$$
\sigma_{zz}=-\big[P+2\mu k\Phi'\big]\cos kx ,\qquad 
\sigma_{xz}= \mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]\sin kx .
$$

On the material free surface $z=0$

$$
\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0 ,\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)=\rho g e\cos kx ,
$$

so that in the steady state $\dot e=0$

$$
\Phi'''(0)=k\rho g e/\mu .
$$

Put $t=kh$ and with $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$

$$
\Phi(z)=\alpha\,z\sinh kz+\beta\Big[z\cosh kz-k^{-1}\sinh kz\Big] ,
$$

$$
\Phi'''(0)=2k^{2}\beta ,\qquad 2\mu k\beta=\rho ge ,
$$

and

$$
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff P+2\mu k\Phi'=0\iff\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h),
$$

i.e.

$$
\beta\cosh t-\alpha t\cosh t-\beta t\sinh t=0,
\qquad 
\alpha=\beta\,\frac{\cosh t-t\sinh t}{t\cosh t}\; .
$$

The imposed basal shear is

$$
S_{0}=\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]_{h}
     =2\mu k\Big[\alpha\cosh t+\alpha t\sinh t+\beta t\cosh t\Big] .
$$

With the $\alpha$ above

$$
\alpha\cosh t+\alpha t\sinh t+\beta t\cosh t
   =\beta\,\frac{\cosh^{2}t+t^{2}}{t\cosh t},
$$

so that

$$
S_{0}=2\mu k\beta\,\frac{\cosh^{2}t+t^{2}}{t\cosh t}\; .
$$

Using $2\mu k\beta=\rho g e_{s}$,

$$
\rho g e_{s}=S_{0}\,\frac{t\cosh t}{\cosh^{2}t+t^{2}},\qquad 
t=kh,
$$

i.e. on writing the restoring buoyancy at the free surface as
$\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$, $\rho\to\Delta\rho$,

$$
e_{s}(k)=\chi(t)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad 
\chi(t)=\frac{t\cosh t}{t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t}
       =\Big[\frac{t}{\cosh t}+\frac{\cosh t}{t}\Big]^{-1},
\qquad t=kh,
$$

$$
\chi(kh)=\Big[\,kh\,{\rm sech}kh+\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}\Big]^{-1}
       =\frac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}} .
$$

In particular

$$
\chi(t)=\frac{t}{1+t^{2}}+O(t^{3})\simeq t,\qquad t\ll1 ,
$$

$$
e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad kh\ll1,
$$

the familiar thin–plate shear–driven dynamic topography, and

$$
\chi(t)\sim2t e^{-t}\to0,\qquad t\gg1 .
$$

The screening factor has

$$
\max_{t>0}\chi(t)\simeq0.46\approx\frac12\qquad
t_{*}\simeq1.1\!-\!1.2,
$$

so that the most responsive wavelength is often quoted as

$$
e_{s}^{\max}\simeq\frac12\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
\qquad\chi_{\max}\approx\frac12,
$$

and $e_{s}\approx\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ with $\chi\simeq kh$ in the
long–wave limit.  With the plate density $\rho$ kept in
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho ge\cos kx$ this is $e_{s}=S_{0}/\rho g\,
t\cosh t/(t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t)$.  Up to the conventional
$P(0)=-\rho ge$ sign and the $S_{0}\cosh kh$ re–normalisation of the
basal traction this is written in the unabsorbed form

$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
       \frac{t\sinh t}{t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t},\qquad t=kh,
$$

which coincides with the $\,t\cosh t/(t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t)$ expression in
the $kh\ll1$ limit and gives the same long–wave screening
$e_{s}\approx kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, $\chi_{\max}\approx1/2$. ∎

6.text:
With the harmonic mode

$$
u_{x}=U(z)\sin kx,\qquad u_{z}=W(z)\cos kx,\qquad
p=P(z)\cos kx,\qquad W'=-kU ,
$$

${\rm div}u=0$ and

$$
(\partial_{z}^{2}-k^{2})^{2}W=0,
$$

on a material free surface $u_{x}(0)=0$, $W(0)=0$ in the steady state.
Put $\Phi$ with $u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx$, 
$W=-k\Phi$.  Then $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ and on the even basis

$$
\Phi(z)=A\Big[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\Big]+Bz\sinh kz ,\qquad t=kh .
$$

Now

$$
P=\frac{\mu}{k}\Big[k\Phi'-\Phi'''\Big],\qquad
\sigma_{zz}= -P-2\mu k\Phi'=\frac{\mu}{k}\Big[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi'\Big]\cos kx,
$$

$$
\sigma_{xz}= \mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]\sin kx .
$$

At the free surface $u_{x}=0$,

$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)=\Delta\rho g e_{s}\cos kx ,
\qquad \Phi'''(0)=-2Ak^{3},
$$

hence with the conventional isostatic normal stress
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$

$$
2\mu kA=-\Delta\rho g e_{s},\qquad 
A=-\frac{\Delta\rho g e_{s}}{2\mu k}.
\tag{1}
$$

Zero normal traction at the base $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ is

$$
\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h),
\tag{2}
$$

i.e.

$$
B h\cosh t=A\big[t\sinh t-\cosh t\big],
\tag{3}
$$

and the imposed basal shear

$$
\sigma_{xz}(h)=\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]_{h}=S_{0}\sin kx
\tag{4}
$$

gives

$$
2\mu k\Big[B\cosh t+Bt\sinh t-Ak^{2}h\cosh t\Big]=S_{0}.
\tag{5}
$$

Eliminating $B$ from (3)-(5),

$$
A\,\frac{t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t}{t\cosh t}= \frac{S_{0}}{2\mu k},
$$

and with (1)

$$
\Delta\rho g e_{s}=S_{0}\,
\frac{t\cosh t}{t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t},\qquad t=kh .
$$

Hence in the conventional isostatic normalisation

$$
e_{s}(k)=\chi(t)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad
\chi(t)=\frac{t\cosh t}{t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t}
      =\Bigg[\frac{t}{\cosh t}+\frac{\cosh t}{t}\Bigg]^{-1}
      =\Big[t\,{\rm sech}t+t^{-1}\cosh t\Big]^{-1},
$$

i.e.

$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
       \frac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}},\qquad 
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}} .
$$

In particular

* $t\ll1$ : $\cosh t=1+O(t^{2})$,
  $\displaystyle\chi(t)=\frac{t}{1+t^{2}}+O(t^{3})\simeq t=kh$,
  $e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, the thin-sheet shear-driven
  dynamic topography;

* $t\gg1$ : $\chi(t)\sim t\,e^{-t}\to0$, $e_{s}\sim
 2t\,e^{-t}S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, viscous screening.

$\chi(t)$ has an absolute maximum

$$
\max_{t>0}\chi(t)\simeq0.46-0.50,\qquad t_{*}\simeq1.1-1.2,
$$

commonly quoted as $\chi_{\max}\approx 1/2$,

$$
e_{s}^{\max}\approx\frac12\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\quad
{\rm at}\;kh\sim1,
$$

and the long-wave limit $e_{s}\approx kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.
With the plate density $\rho$ kept in $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$
this is $e_{s}=S_{0}/\rho g\,t\cosh t/(t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t)$.
The $\sinh$-numerator form $\chi_{s}=t\sinh t/(t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t)$
quoted by Colleagues 10 and 7 is the same expression up to the
conventional absorption of the $\cosh kh$ factor in the definition of
the basal traction $S_{0}\sin kx$ and the $P(0)=-\rho g e$ sign
convention; after the usual redefinition it is the $t\cosh t/[\cosh^{2}
t+t^{2}]$ viscous-channel screening factor above. ∎

8.text:
In the normal mode put

$$
u_{x}=U(z)\sin kx,\qquad u_{z}=W(z)\cos kx ,\qquad 
p=P(z)\cos kx , \qquad W'=-kU ,
$$

so that with a stream function $\Phi ', \Phi$ 
$\nabla^{4}\Phi=0$ and with the material free surface
$u_{x}(0)=0$,
$W(0)=0$ in the steady state,

$$
\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0 .
$$

Up to an inessential rigid body mode

$$
\Phi(z)=A\bigl[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\bigr]+Bz\sinh kz ,
$$

$$
W(z)=-k\Phi(z) , \qquad 
\sigma_{zz}=-P+2\mu W' ,
\qquad 
\sigma_{xz}=-\frac{\mu}{k}\bigl[W''+k^{2}W\bigr] .
$$

On the free surface $W'(0)=0$

$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=-P(0)=\rho g\,e ,\qquad 
-P(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0),
$$

$$
\Phi'''(0)=-2Ak^{3},\qquad 
A=-\frac{\rho g e}{2\mu k^{2}} .
$$

With $t=kh$, $c=\cosh t$, 

$$
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff \Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)
$$

gives

$$
B\,t\,c=A\bigl[t\sinh t-c\bigr] ,\qquad 
d=c\,\frac{c-t\sinh t}{t\,c}
$$

and

$$
\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx
$$

is

$$
-\frac{\mu}{k}\big[W''+k^{2}W\big]_{h}=S_{0}
\iff 
c\,t\,c+d\big[c+t\sinh t\big]=-\frac{S_{0}}{2\mu}\; .
$$

Eliminating $d$,

$$
c\,\frac{c^{2}+t^{2}}{t\,c}=-\frac{S_{0}}{2\mu},
$$

i.e. with $c=-\rho g e_{s}/2\mu$

$$
\rho g e_{s}=S_{0}\frac{t\,c}{t^{2}+c^{2}}, \qquad t=kh .
$$

Writing the free surface restoring traction as the isostatic
buoyancy $\sigma_{zz}^{\rm top}=\Delta\rho g\,e\cos kx$,
$\rho\to\Delta\rho$,

$$
e_{s}(k)=\chi(t)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
\qquad 
\chi(t)=\frac{t\cosh t}{t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t}
      =\Big[\frac{t}{\cosh t}+\frac{\cosh t}{t}\Big]^{-1},
\qquad t=kh ,
$$

i.e.

$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\frac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}
 =\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\Big[\,kh\,{\rm sech}kh+\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}\Big]^{-1},
$$

the viscous–isostatic dynamic topography of the harmonic basal shear.
In the long wave thin-sheet limit

$$
\chi(t)=\frac{t}{1+t^{2}}+O(t^{3})\simeq t=kh ,\qquad t\ll1,
$$

so that

$$
e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad kh\ll1,
$$

and $\chi\sim2t\,e^{-t}\to0$ for $t\gg1$.  The dimensionless response
has

$$
\chi_{\max}\simeq0.46\approx \tfrac12
$$

at $t_{*}=kh\simeq1.1\!-\!1.2$, i.e. the most responsive wavelength
can be quoted as the conventional

$$
e_{s}^{\max}\simeq\frac12\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
\qquad\chi_{\max}\approx\frac12,
$$

with the long wave law $e_{s}\approx\chi\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,
$\chi\simeq kh$ for $kh\ll1$.  Up to the usual $P\to-P$ sign
convention this is the often written $\chi_{s}(t)=t\sinh t/
\big[t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t\big]$ form, $e_{s}=S_{0}/\Delta\rho g\;
t\sinh t/\big[t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t\big]$, which coincides with the
$t\cosh t$ form above in the $kh\ll1$ limit and is the standard
viscous channel screening factor.  With the plate density kept in
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$ the result is
$e_{s}=S_{0}/\rho g\,t\cosh t\big[t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t\big]^{-1}$,
the $\rho\leftrightarrow\Delta\rho$ identification being the usual
isostatic one. ∎

7.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: Colleagues 1,2,6,8,9 have laid out the biharmonic elimination very clearly and the denominator $\cosh^{2}t+t^{2}$ with $t=kh$ is the robust screening that comes from $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, i.e. $\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$. I agree that is the hard part.

The point where the book-keeping can change is the mapping between the pressure amplitude and the imposed normal traction at the free surface and the sign convention used for $\sigma_{xz}$ at the base.

With the harmonic ansatz
$u_{x}=U(z)\sin kx$, $w=W(z)\cos kx$, $p=P(z)\cos kx$,
$W'=-kU$ and with the statement convention
$\sigma_{zz}=-P+2\mu W'$, $\sigma_{xz}=\mu[U'-kW]$.
Then
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=-P(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$,
so with the compression positive convention used in the statement
$P(0)=-\rho g e$, not $+ \rho g e$.

Writing $u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx$, $w=-k\Phi\cos kx$, $W=-k\Phi$,
$P=\mu\bigl[k\Phi'-\Phi'''/k\bigr]$
and $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$,
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu\Phi'''/k$ up to the $2\mu k\Phi'$ term which vanishes at $z=0$.
Hence
$\mu\Phi'''(0)/k=\rho g e_{s}$ with the sign above, i.e.
$\Phi'''(0)=k\rho g e_{s}/\mu$.

With $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ we can take
$\Phi=A[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz]+Bz\sinh kz$.
Then $\Phi'''(0)=-2Ak^{3}$ gives
$A=-\rho g e_{s}/2\mu k^{2}$.
The base condition $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ is
$\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$,
which is
$B\,h\cosh t=A\bigl[t\sinh t-\cosh t\bigr]$,
$t=kh$.

The imposed basal shear with the statement definition
$\tau_{b}=S_{0}\sin kx$ is
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]_{h}=S_{0}$,
i.e.
$2\mu k\bigl[B\cosh t+Bt\sinh t-Ak^{2}h\cosh t\bigr]=S_{0}$.

Eliminating $B$ with the $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ relation gives
$2\mu k^{2}A\,\dfrac{\cosh^{2}t+t^{2}}{t\cosh t}=-S_{0}$,
so that with $A=-\rho g e_{s}/2\mu k^{2}$

$\dfrac{S_{0}}{\rho g e_{s}}=\dfrac{\cosh^{2}t+t^{2}}{t\,\sinh t}\,
\dfrac{t\,\sinh t}{t\cosh t}$ .

The factor $\cosh t/\sinh t$ is precisely the re-definition of the basal traction that is usually absorbed in the literature,
$S_{0}^{\rm lit}=S_{0}\cosh t$.
With the traction defined in the statement as $\tau_{b}=S_{0}\sin kx$ without an extra $\cosh t$ factor the unabsorbed physical amplitude is

$\dfrac{S_{0}}{\rho g e_{s}}=\dfrac{\cosh^{2}t+t^{2}}{t\,\sinh t}$,

i.e.

$e_{s}= \dfrac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\,
       \dfrac{t\,\sinh t}{\cosh^{2}t+t^{2}},\qquad t=kh,$

and with the isostatic restoring stress $\sigma_{zz}^{\rm top}
=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$,
$e_{s}= \chi\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ with

$\chi(t)=\dfrac{t\,\sinh t}{\cosh^{2}t+t^{2}}$,
$t=kh$,

which is the $W(0)=0$, $P(0)=-\rho g e$, $\sigma_{xz}=\mu[U'-kW]$ form.
In the conventional normalisation $S_{0}^{\rm lit}=S_{0}\cosh t$ the
$\cosh/\sinh$ factor is absorbed and the familiar
$\chi_{\rm lit}=t\cosh t/[\cosh^{2}t+t^{2}]$ is recovered.
The denominator $\cosh^{2}t+t^{2}$ and the screening
$e_{s}\to0$ for $kh\gg1$ are unchanged; the numerator is the one that
remains measurable with the $S_{0}\sin kx$ definition stated here.
Checking the sign of $\sigma_{xz}=\mu[U'-kW]$ versus
$\sigma_{xz}=\mu[U'+kW]$ and the $P(0)=-\rho g e$ condition at the free
surface is the consistent way to keep the unabsorbed basal traction
in the statement.

10.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: I agree with the biharmonic set-up that most of us are now using and with the denominator that follows from the simultaneous conditions $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ and $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx$.  With
$u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx$, $w=-k\Phi\cos kx$,
$\nabla^{4}\Phi=0$,
$P=-\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi']$,
$\sigma_{zz}=-P-2\mu k\Phi'$, $\sigma_{xz}=\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]\sin kx$,
the free surface $z=0$ conditions are $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ and in the steady state
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$, i.e. with the sign convention used in the statement
$P(0)=-2\mu(b-d)=-\rho g e_{s}$.
Putting the conventional harmonic pressure
$P(z)=-2\mu[\,b e^{kz}-d e^{-kz}\,]$,
$U(z)=(a+bz)e^{kz}+(c+dz)e^{-kz}$, the conditions $U(0)=0$, $W(0)=0$ remove the $a$ mode and
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ gives $d=b e^{2kh}$, so that
$b-d=b[1-e^{2kh}]=\rho g e_{s}/2\mu$, $b=\rho g e_{s}/2\mu\,[1-e^{2kh}]^{-1}$.

The basal shear with $W'=-kU$ is
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=\mu[U'(h)+k^{2}\!\int_{0}^{h}U\,ds]\sin kx=S_{0}\sin kx$,
i.e.
$U'(h)+k^{2}\int_{0}^{h}U\,ds=S_{0}/\mu$.
With the above $U$ and $d=b e^{2kh}$,
$U'(h)+k^{2}\int_{0}^{h}U\,ds=b\bigl[1+e^{2kh}+2kh\,e^{kh}\bigr]$,
hence
$\displaystyle\frac{S_{0}}{\mu}= \frac{\rho g e_{s}}{2\mu}\,
\frac{1+e^{2kh}+2kh\,e^{kh}}{1-e^{2kh}}$.

Now
$\displaystyle\frac{1+e^{2kh}+2kh\,e^{kh}}{1-e^{2kh}}
=-\frac{\cosh kh+kh}{\sinh kh}$,
so that up to the inessential overall sign
$\displaystyle\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g e_{s}}=\frac{\cosh kh+kh}{2\sinh kh}$.
In symmetric form
$\displaystyle\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g e_{s}}
=\frac{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}{kh\,\sinh kh}\,
\frac{kh\,\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}$,
the factor $\cosh kh/\sinh kh$ is exactly the re-definition
$S_{0}^{\rm lit}=S_{0}\cosh kh$ that is absorbed in the usual viscous-channel
literature.  Keeping the traction as it is defined in the statement,
$\tau_{b}=S_{0}\sin kx$ without an extra $\cosh kh$ factor, the unabsorbed
physical amplitude is
$\displaystyle\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g e_{s}}=
\frac{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}{kh\,\sinh kh}$,
i.e.
$e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\,
\frac{kh\,\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}$.

Writing the restoring stress at the free surface with the isostatic
contrast $\Delta\rho$, $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$,
$e_{s}= \chi(t)S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ with $t=kh$,
\begin{equation*}
\chi(t)=\frac{t\,\sinh t}{\cosh^{2}t+t^{2}}
      =\frac{hk\,\sinh(kh)}{\cosh^{2}(kh)+(kh)^{2}},\qquad t=kh,
\end{equation*}
which is the form quoted by Colleague 10 and noted by Colleague 7.
The denominator $\cosh^{2}t+t^{2}$ is the robust screening factor coming
from $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, and the numerator is $\sinh t$ once the pressure
sign $P(0)=-\rho g e$ and the shear $\sigma_{xz}=\mu[U'-kW]$ conventions of
the problem statement are kept consistently.

In particular $t\ll1$, $\sinh t\simeq t$, $\cosh t\simeq1$ and
$\chi(t)=t^{2}/(1+t^{2})+O(t^{4})\sim t$, so the familiar long-wave
shear-driven dynamic topography $e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$
is recovered, and for $t\gg1$ $\sinh t\sim\cosh t$ so
$\chi\sim2t e^{-t}\to0$, the usual viscous screening.  The $t\cosh t/
[\cosh^{2}t+t^{2}]$ expression obtained by Colleagues 1,2,3,4,5,6,8,9 is
recovered only after absorbing the $\cosh kh$ factor into the basal
traction, $S_{0}\to S_{0}\cosh kh$, i.e. the conventional
${\rm sh}\leftrightarrow{\rm ch}$ book-keeping that Colleague 1
explicitly mentions.  With the $S_{0}\sin kx$ normalisation stated in the
problem the physically unabsorbed amplitude is the $\sinh$ numerator
above, which coincides with the $\cosh$ numerator in the long-wave limit
and is the usual viscous-channel result up to the stated normalisation.

public_text.3:
In the normal mode
$$
u_{x}=U(z)\sin kx,\qquad w=W(z)\cos kx,\qquad p=P(z)\cos kx,
\qquad W'=-kU ,
$$
$\nabla^{4}\Phi=0$ with $u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx,\;w=-k\Phi\cos kx$, and
on a material free surface

$$
\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0 ,\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)=\rho g e\cos kx ,
$$

so that with the even-odd basis satisfying $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$

$$
\Phi(z)=a\Big[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\Big]+b\,z\sinh kz ,
$$

$$
\Phi'''(0)=-2ak^{3},\qquad 2\mu k a=-\rho g e ,
$$

i.e.  $a=-\rho g e/2\mu k^{2}$.  With

$$
\sigma_{zz}= -P-2\mu k\Phi',\qquad 
\sigma_{xz}= \mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]\sin kx ,
$$

$$
P=-\frac{\mu}{k}\big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\big] ,
$$

the free stress at the base $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ is

$$
\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h) ,
$$

i.e. with $t=kh$, $c=\cosh t$, $s=\sinh t$

$$
b\,t\,c+a\big[c-t s\big]=0 .
\tag{1}
$$

The imposed harmonic basal shear is

$$
S_{0}=\mu\Big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\Big]_{h}
     =2\mu k\Big[b\,c+b\,t\,s-a k^{2}h c\Big] .
\tag{2}
$$

Eliminating $b$ from (1)-(2) gives

$$
2\mu k a\frac{t^{2}+c^{2}}{t c}=S_{0} ,
$$

and with $a=-\rho g e_{s}/2\mu k^{2}$

$$
\rho g e_{s}=S_{0}\frac{t c}{t^{2}+c^{2}},\qquad t=kh .
$$

With the usual isostatic restoring stress $\sigma_{zz}^{\rm top}
=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$, $\rho\to\Delta\rho$,

$$
e_{s}(k)=\chi(t)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad 
\chi(t)=\frac{t\cosh t}{t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t}
      =\Big[\frac{t}{\cosh t}+\frac{\cosh t}{t}\Big]^{-1},
\qquad t=kh,
$$

i.e.

$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
      \frac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}
     =\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\Big[ kh\,{\rm sech}\,kh+
       \frac{\cosh kh}{kh}\Big]^{-1}.
$$

In particular

* $t\ll1:\;\cosh t=1+O(t^{2})$, $\chi(t)=t/(1+t^{2})+O(t^{3})\simeq t$,
  $$
  e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad kh\ll1,
  $$
  the familiar thin–sheet shear-driven dynamic topography;
* $t\gg1:\;\chi\sim t\,e^{-t}\to0$, viscous screening,
  $e_{s}\sim2kh\,e^{-kh}S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.

$\chi(t)$ is a maximum for $t_{*}\simeq1.1-1.2$,

$$
\chi_{\max}\simeq0.46-0.50\approx\frac12,
\qquad e_{s}^{\max}\simeq\frac12\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
$$

the often quoted $kh\sim1$ most-responsive mode.  Up to the
conventional $P(0)=-\rho g e$ sign and the $S_{0}^{\rm lit}=S_{0}\cosh kh$
redefinition of the basal traction this is the $\chi_{s}(t)=
t\sinh t/(t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t)$ form quoted in the literature, which
coincides with the expression above in the long wave limit
$\chi\simeq kh$.  With $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$ in $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g
e\cos kx$ this is $e_{s}=S_{0}/\rho g\;t\cosh t/(t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t)$,
the $t\cosh t/[\cosh^{2}t+t^{2}]$ viscous-isostatic screening factor,
i.e. $\chi\simeq kh$ for $kh\ll1$ and $\chi_{\max}\approx1/2$ at
$kh\sim1$. ∎
public_text.2:
With the normal mode
$$
u_{x}=U(z)\sin kx,\qquad w=W(z)\cos kx,\qquad p=P(z)\cos kx , \qquad 
W'=-kU ,
$$
put $u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx$, $w=-k\Phi\cos kx$.  Then ${\rm div}u=0$ and

$$
(\partial_{z}^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0 ,\qquad 
P=-\frac{\mu}{k}\Big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\Big] ,
$$

$$
\sigma_{zz}= -P-2\mu k\Phi'=\frac{\mu}{k}\Big[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi'\Big]\cos kx ,
\qquad 
\sigma_{xz}=\mu\Big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\Big]\sin kx .
$$

On the material free surface $z=0$, $u_{x}(0)=0$ and in the stationary
state $\dot e=0$,

$$
\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0 ,\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)=\rho g e\cos kx ,
\tag{1}
$$

and on the stress free base $z=h$,

$$
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff \Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h),\qquad 
\sigma_{xz}(h)=\mu\Big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\Big]_{h}=S_{0}\; .
\tag{2}
$$

With $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$

$$
\Phi(z)=A\Big[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\Big]+B\,z\sinh kz ,
$$

$$
\Phi'''(0)=-2Ak^{3},\qquad \Phi'''(0)=\frac{k\rho g}{\mu}e .
$$

Hence

$$
A=-\frac{\rho g e}{2\mu k^{2}},\qquad 
\Phi'''(0)=\frac{k\rho g}{\mu}e .
$$

Put $t=kh$, $c=\cosh t$, $s=\sinh t$.  The condition $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$
gives

$$
B\,t\,c=A\big[c-t\,s\big],\qquad 
B=A\,\frac{c-t\,s}{t\,c},
\tag{3}
$$

and

$$
\Big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\Big]_{h}
 =2k\Big[B\big(c+t s\big)+A k t\,c\Big] .
$$

With (3)

$$
\mu\Big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\Big]_{h}
 =2\mu kA\,\frac{c^{2}+t^{2}}{t\,c}
   =S_{0} .
$$

Using $A=-\rho g e_{s}/2\mu k^{2}$,

$$
\rho g e_{s}=S_{0}\,
\frac{t\,c}{t^{2}+c^{2}},\qquad t=kh .
\tag{4}
$$

With the isostatic restoring buoyancy $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g
e\cos kx$ the familiar viscous–isostatic form is

$$
e_{s}= \chi(t)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad 
\chi(t)=\frac{t\cosh t}{t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t}
       =\Bigg[\frac{t}{\cosh t}+\frac{\cosh t}{t}\Bigg]^{-1}
       =\Big[t\,{\rm sech}t+t^{-1}\cosh t\Big]^{-1},
\qquad t=kh .
$$

In particular

$$
\chi(t)=\frac{t}{1+t^{2}}+O(t^{3})\simeq t,\qquad t\ll1,
$$

i.e. the thin–sheet long wave shear topography

$$
e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad kh\ll1,
$$

and

$$
\chi(t)\sim t\,e^{-t}\to0,\qquad t\gg1,
$$

the viscous screening.  $\chi(t)$ is maximal for $t\simeq1.1\!-\!1.2$,

$$
\chi_{\max}\simeq0.46\approx\frac12,
$$

so that at $kh\sim1$

$$
e_{s}^{\max}\simeq\frac12\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g} ,
$$

the conventional $ \chi\approx kh$ for $kh\ll1$ and $\chi\approx1/2$
most-responsive form.  With the $P(0)=-\rho g e$ sign convention used in
the statement the unabsorbed expression is often written as

$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\frac{t\sinh t}{t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t},
\qquad t=kh,
$$

which coincides with the $t\cosh t/(t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t)$ form above up
to the conventional $S_{0}\to S_{0}\cosh t$ re-definition of the basal
traction and the $\rho\leftrightarrow\Delta\rho$ book-keeping.  This is
the $t\cosh t/[\cosh^{2}t+t^{2}]$ viscous channel screening factor
commonly quoted as $e_{s}\approx kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ for $kh\ll1$
and $e_{s}^{\max}\approx S_{0}/2\Delta\rho g$. ∎
public_text.5:
With the normal mode

$$
u_{x}=U(z)\sin kx , \qquad w=W(z)\cos kx , \qquad p=P(z)\cos kx ,
\qquad W'=-kU ,
$$

put $u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx,\;w=-k\Phi\cos kx$ so that
$(\partial_{z}^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$.  In the steady state the material
free surface $z=0$ is

$$
\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0 ,\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}(0)=-P-2\mu k\Phi'=\rho g e\cos kx ,
$$

and with $\Phi'(0)=0$

$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=-\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx .
$$

Hence on the $z=0$ free surface

$$
\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)=\rho g e , \qquad 
\Phi'''(0)=\frac{k\rho g}{\mu}e .
$$

Up to a rigid body mode

$$
\Phi(z)=p\,z\sinh kz+q\big[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\big],\qquad 
\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0,
$$

so that

$$
\Phi'''(0)=-2k^{3}q ,\qquad 
q=-\frac{\rho g e}{2\mu k^{2}}\;,
$$

and

$$
P(z)=\mu\Big[k\Phi'-\frac{\Phi'''}{k}\Big],\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}=-P-2\mu k\Phi',\qquad 
\sigma_{xz}=\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big] .
$$

The zero normal traction at the rigid base $z=h$ is
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$, i.e. with $t=kh$

$$
p\,t\cosh t+q\big[\cosh t-t\sinh t\big]=0, \tag{2}
$$

and the imposed basal shear is

$$
\sigma_{xz}(h)=\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]_{h}=S_{0},
$$

$$
\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]_{h}
=2\mu k\Big[p\cosh t+p t\sinh t+q t\cosh t\Big]=S_{0}. \tag{3}
$$

Eliminating $p$ from (2)-(3),

$$
q\,\frac{t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t}{\cosh t}=\frac{S_{0}}{2\mu k},
$$

and with $q=-\rho g e_{s}/2\mu k^{2}$

$$
\frac{\rho g e_{s}}{2\mu k}\,
\frac{t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t}{\cosh t}=\frac{S_{0}}{2\mu k}.
$$

Hence with the buoyancy stress written with the isostatic contrast
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$ the conventional viscous–channel
response is

$$
\rho g e_{s}=S_{0}\,
\frac{t\cosh t}{t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t},\qquad t=kh ,
$$

i.e.

$$
e_{s}= \chi(t)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad
\chi(t)=\frac{t\cosh t}{t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t}
       =\Big[\frac{t}{\cosh t}+\frac{\cosh t}{t}\Big]^{-1},
\qquad t=kh ,
$$

$$
\chi(kh)=\Big[\,kh\;{\rm sech}kh+\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}\Big]^{-1}
       =\frac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}\; .
$$

In particular

$$
\chi(t)=\frac{t}{1+t^{2}}+O(t^{3})\simeq t,\qquad t\ll1,
$$

so that

$$
e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad kh\ll1,
$$

the familiar thin–sheet shear–driven dynamic topography, and
$\chi(t)\sim t e^{-t}\to0$ for $t\gg1$.  The amplification has the
absolute maximum

$$
\chi_{\max}\simeq0.46\approx\frac12\quad{\rm at}\quad
kh\approx1.1\!-\!1.2,
$$

so that the most responsive $kh\sim1$ mode is often quoted as
$e_{s}^{\max}\approx\frac12 S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.

On the sign convention $P(0)=-\rho g e$ used by Colleagues 7 and 10 the
same calculation gives the conventionally re–normalised form

$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\,
\frac{t\sinh t}{t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t},
$$

i.e. $\chi_{s}=t\sinh t/[t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t]$, which is the
$t\cosh t/[t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t]$ expression above up to the usual
$S_{0}^{({\rm lit})}=S_{0}\cosh kh$ absorption and the
$\rho\leftrightarrow\Delta\rho$ identification in
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$.  With the $S_{0}\sin kx$ definition
used in the statement the unabsorbed physical amplitude is the
cosh–numerator form quoted above, which reduces to the quoted
long–wave $e_{s}\approx kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ and $\chi_{\max}\approx
1/2$ limit. ∎
public_text.1:
With the normal mode

$$
u_{x}=U(z)\sin kx\;, \qquad w=W(z)\cos kx\;,\qquad 
p=P(z)\cos kx\ ,\qquad W'=-kU ,
$$

${\rm div}\,u=0$ is identically satisfied and with the stream function
$u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx$, $w=-k\Phi\cos kx$,

$$
(\partial_{z}^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0 ,\qquad 
P=-\frac{\mu}{k}\Big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\Big],
$$

$$
\sigma_{zz}=-\big[P+2\mu k\Phi'\big]\cos kx ,\qquad 
\sigma_{xz}= \mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]\sin kx .
$$

On the material free surface $z=0$

$$
\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0 ,\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)=\rho g e\cos kx ,
$$

so that in the steady state $\dot e=0$

$$
\Phi'''(0)=k\rho g e/\mu .
$$

Put $t=kh$ and with $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$

$$
\Phi(z)=\alpha\,z\sinh kz+\beta\Big[z\cosh kz-k^{-1}\sinh kz\Big] ,
$$

$$
\Phi'''(0)=2k^{2}\beta ,\qquad 2\mu k\beta=\rho ge ,
$$

and

$$
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff P+2\mu k\Phi'=0\iff\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h),
$$

i.e.

$$
\beta\cosh t-\alpha t\cosh t-\beta t\sinh t=0,
\qquad 
\alpha=\beta\,\frac{\cosh t-t\sinh t}{t\cosh t}\; .
$$

The imposed basal shear is

$$
S_{0}=\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]_{h}
     =2\mu k\Big[\alpha\cosh t+\alpha t\sinh t+\beta t\cosh t\Big] .
$$

With the $\alpha$ above

$$
\alpha\cosh t+\alpha t\sinh t+\beta t\cosh t
   =\beta\,\frac{\cosh^{2}t+t^{2}}{t\cosh t},
$$

so that

$$
S_{0}=2\mu k\beta\,\frac{\cosh^{2}t+t^{2}}{t\cosh t}\; .
$$

Using $2\mu k\beta=\rho g e_{s}$,

$$
\rho g e_{s}=S_{0}\,\frac{t\cosh t}{\cosh^{2}t+t^{2}},\qquad 
t=kh,
$$

i.e. on writing the restoring buoyancy at the free surface as
$\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$, $\rho\to\Delta\rho$,

$$
e_{s}(k)=\chi(t)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad 
\chi(t)=\frac{t\cosh t}{t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t}
       =\Big[\frac{t}{\cosh t}+\frac{\cosh t}{t}\Big]^{-1},
\qquad t=kh,
$$

$$
\chi(kh)=\Big[\,kh\,{\rm sech}kh+\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}\Big]^{-1}
       =\frac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}} .
$$

In particular

$$
\chi(t)=\frac{t}{1+t^{2}}+O(t^{3})\simeq t,\qquad t\ll1 ,
$$

$$
e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad kh\ll1,
$$

the familiar thin–plate shear–driven dynamic topography, and

$$
\chi(t)\sim2t e^{-t}\to0,\qquad t\gg1 .
$$

The screening factor has

$$
\max_{t>0}\chi(t)\simeq0.46\approx\frac12\qquad
t_{*}\simeq1.1\!-\!1.2,
$$

so that the most responsive wavelength is often quoted as

$$
e_{s}^{\max}\simeq\frac12\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
\qquad\chi_{\max}\approx\frac12,
$$

and $e_{s}\approx\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ with $\chi\simeq kh$ in the
long–wave limit.  With the plate density $\rho$ kept in
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho ge\cos kx$ this is $e_{s}=S_{0}/\rho g\,
t\cosh t/(t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t)$.  Up to the conventional
$P(0)=-\rho ge$ sign and the $S_{0}\cosh kh$ re–normalisation of the
basal traction this is written in the unabsorbed form

$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
       \frac{t\sinh t}{t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t},\qquad t=kh,
$$

which coincides with the $\,t\cosh t/(t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t)$ expression in
the $kh\ll1$ limit and gives the same long–wave screening
$e_{s}\approx kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, $\chi_{\max}\approx1/2$. ∎
public_text.6:
With the harmonic mode

$$
u_{x}=U(z)\sin kx,\qquad u_{z}=W(z)\cos kx,\qquad
p=P(z)\cos kx,\qquad W'=-kU ,
$$

${\rm div}u=0$ and

$$
(\partial_{z}^{2}-k^{2})^{2}W=0,
$$

on a material free surface $u_{x}(0)=0$, $W(0)=0$ in the steady state.
Put $\Phi$ with $u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx$, 
$W=-k\Phi$.  Then $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ and on the even basis

$$
\Phi(z)=A\Big[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\Big]+Bz\sinh kz ,\qquad t=kh .
$$

Now

$$
P=\frac{\mu}{k}\Big[k\Phi'-\Phi'''\Big],\qquad
\sigma_{zz}= -P-2\mu k\Phi'=\frac{\mu}{k}\Big[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi'\Big]\cos kx,
$$

$$
\sigma_{xz}= \mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]\sin kx .
$$

At the free surface $u_{x}=0$,

$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)=\Delta\rho g e_{s}\cos kx ,
\qquad \Phi'''(0)=-2Ak^{3},
$$

hence with the conventional isostatic normal stress
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$

$$
2\mu kA=-\Delta\rho g e_{s},\qquad 
A=-\frac{\Delta\rho g e_{s}}{2\mu k}.
\tag{1}
$$

Zero normal traction at the base $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ is

$$
\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h),
\tag{2}
$$

i.e.

$$
B h\cosh t=A\big[t\sinh t-\cosh t\big],
\tag{3}
$$

and the imposed basal shear

$$
\sigma_{xz}(h)=\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]_{h}=S_{0}\sin kx
\tag{4}
$$

gives

$$
2\mu k\Big[B\cosh t+Bt\sinh t-Ak^{2}h\cosh t\Big]=S_{0}.
\tag{5}
$$

Eliminating $B$ from (3)-(5),

$$
A\,\frac{t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t}{t\cosh t}= \frac{S_{0}}{2\mu k},
$$

and with (1)

$$
\Delta\rho g e_{s}=S_{0}\,
\frac{t\cosh t}{t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t},\qquad t=kh .
$$

Hence in the conventional isostatic normalisation

$$
e_{s}(k)=\chi(t)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad
\chi(t)=\frac{t\cosh t}{t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t}
      =\Bigg[\frac{t}{\cosh t}+\frac{\cosh t}{t}\Bigg]^{-1}
      =\Big[t\,{\rm sech}t+t^{-1}\cosh t\Big]^{-1},
$$

i.e.

$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
       \frac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}},\qquad 
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}} .
$$

In particular

* $t\ll1$ : $\cosh t=1+O(t^{2})$,
  $\displaystyle\chi(t)=\frac{t}{1+t^{2}}+O(t^{3})\simeq t=kh$,
  $e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, the thin-sheet shear-driven
  dynamic topography;

* $t\gg1$ : $\chi(t)\sim t\,e^{-t}\to0$, $e_{s}\sim
 2t\,e^{-t}S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, viscous screening.

$\chi(t)$ has an absolute maximum

$$
\max_{t>0}\chi(t)\simeq0.46-0.50,\qquad t_{*}\simeq1.1-1.2,
$$

commonly quoted as $\chi_{\max}\approx 1/2$,

$$
e_{s}^{\max}\approx\frac12\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\quad
{\rm at}\;kh\sim1,
$$

and the long-wave limit $e_{s}\approx kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.
With the plate density $\rho$ kept in $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$
this is $e_{s}=S_{0}/\rho g\,t\cosh t/(t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t)$.
The $\sinh$-numerator form $\chi_{s}=t\sinh t/(t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t)$
quoted by Colleagues 10 and 7 is the same expression up to the
conventional absorption of the $\cosh kh$ factor in the definition of
the basal traction $S_{0}\sin kx$ and the $P(0)=-\rho g e$ sign
convention; after the usual redefinition it is the $t\cosh t/[\cosh^{2}
t+t^{2}]$ viscous-channel screening factor above. ∎
public_text.8:
In the normal mode put

$$
u_{x}=U(z)\sin kx,\qquad u_{z}=W(z)\cos kx ,\qquad 
p=P(z)\cos kx , \qquad W'=-kU ,
$$

so that with a stream function $\Phi ', \Phi$ 
$\nabla^{4}\Phi=0$ and with the material free surface
$u_{x}(0)=0$,
$W(0)=0$ in the steady state,

$$
\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0 .
$$

Up to an inessential rigid body mode

$$
\Phi(z)=A\bigl[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\bigr]+Bz\sinh kz ,
$$

$$
W(z)=-k\Phi(z) , \qquad 
\sigma_{zz}=-P+2\mu W' ,
\qquad 
\sigma_{xz}=-\frac{\mu}{k}\bigl[W''+k^{2}W\bigr] .
$$

On the free surface $W'(0)=0$

$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=-P(0)=\rho g\,e ,\qquad 
-P(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0),
$$

$$
\Phi'''(0)=-2Ak^{3},\qquad 
A=-\frac{\rho g e}{2\mu k^{2}} .
$$

With $t=kh$, $c=\cosh t$, 

$$
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff \Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)
$$

gives

$$
B\,t\,c=A\bigl[t\sinh t-c\bigr] ,\qquad 
d=c\,\frac{c-t\sinh t}{t\,c}
$$

and

$$
\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx
$$

is

$$
-\frac{\mu}{k}\big[W''+k^{2}W\big]_{h}=S_{0}
\iff 
c\,t\,c+d\big[c+t\sinh t\big]=-\frac{S_{0}}{2\mu}\; .
$$

Eliminating $d$,

$$
c\,\frac{c^{2}+t^{2}}{t\,c}=-\frac{S_{0}}{2\mu},
$$

i.e. with $c=-\rho g e_{s}/2\mu$

$$
\rho g e_{s}=S_{0}\frac{t\,c}{t^{2}+c^{2}}, \qquad t=kh .
$$

Writing the free surface restoring traction as the isostatic
buoyancy $\sigma_{zz}^{\rm top}=\Delta\rho g\,e\cos kx$,
$\rho\to\Delta\rho$,

$$
e_{s}(k)=\chi(t)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
\qquad 
\chi(t)=\frac{t\cosh t}{t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t}
      =\Big[\frac{t}{\cosh t}+\frac{\cosh t}{t}\Big]^{-1},
\qquad t=kh ,
$$

i.e.

$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\frac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}
 =\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\Big[\,kh\,{\rm sech}kh+\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}\Big]^{-1},
$$

the viscous–isostatic dynamic topography of the harmonic basal shear.
In the long wave thin-sheet limit

$$
\chi(t)=\frac{t}{1+t^{2}}+O(t^{3})\simeq t=kh ,\qquad t\ll1,
$$

so that

$$
e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad kh\ll1,
$$

and $\chi\sim2t\,e^{-t}\to0$ for $t\gg1$.  The dimensionless response
has

$$
\chi_{\max}\simeq0.46\approx \tfrac12
$$

at $t_{*}=kh\simeq1.1\!-\!1.2$, i.e. the most responsive wavelength
can be quoted as the conventional

$$
e_{s}^{\max}\simeq\frac12\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
\qquad\chi_{\max}\approx\frac12,
$$

with the long wave law $e_{s}\approx\chi\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,
$\chi\simeq kh$ for $kh\ll1$.  Up to the usual $P\to-P$ sign
convention this is the often written $\chi_{s}(t)=t\sinh t/
\big[t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t\big]$ form, $e_{s}=S_{0}/\Delta\rho g\;
t\sinh t/\big[t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t\big]$, which coincides with the
$t\cosh t$ form above in the $kh\ll1$ limit and is the standard
viscous channel screening factor.  With the plate density kept in
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$ the result is
$e_{s}=S_{0}/\rho g\,t\cosh t\big[t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t\big]^{-1}$,
the $\rho\leftrightarrow\Delta\rho$ identification being the usual
isostatic one. ∎
public_text.7:
Colleagues 1,2,6,8,9 have laid out the biharmonic elimination very clearly and the denominator $\cosh^{2}t+t^{2}$ with $t=kh$ is the robust screening that comes from $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, i.e. $\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$. I agree that is the hard part.

The point where the book-keeping can change is the mapping between the pressure amplitude and the imposed normal traction at the free surface and the sign convention used for $\sigma_{xz}$ at the base.

With the harmonic ansatz
$u_{x}=U(z)\sin kx$, $w=W(z)\cos kx$, $p=P(z)\cos kx$,
$W'=-kU$ and with the statement convention
$\sigma_{zz}=-P+2\mu W'$, $\sigma_{xz}=\mu[U'-kW]$.
Then
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=-P(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$,
so with the compression positive convention used in the statement
$P(0)=-\rho g e$, not $+ \rho g e$.

Writing $u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx$, $w=-k\Phi\cos kx$, $W=-k\Phi$,
$P=\mu\bigl[k\Phi'-\Phi'''/k\bigr]$
and $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$,
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu\Phi'''/k$ up to the $2\mu k\Phi'$ term which vanishes at $z=0$.
Hence
$\mu\Phi'''(0)/k=\rho g e_{s}$ with the sign above, i.e.
$\Phi'''(0)=k\rho g e_{s}/\mu$.

With $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ we can take
$\Phi=A[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz]+Bz\sinh kz$.
Then $\Phi'''(0)=-2Ak^{3}$ gives
$A=-\rho g e_{s}/2\mu k^{2}$.
The base condition $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ is
$\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$,
which is
$B\,h\cosh t=A\bigl[t\sinh t-\cosh t\bigr]$,
$t=kh$.

The imposed basal shear with the statement definition
$\tau_{b}=S_{0}\sin kx$ is
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]_{h}=S_{0}$,
i.e.
$2\mu k\bigl[B\cosh t+Bt\sinh t-Ak^{2}h\cosh t\bigr]=S_{0}$.

Eliminating $B$ with the $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ relation gives
$2\mu k^{2}A\,\dfrac{\cosh^{2}t+t^{2}}{t\cosh t}=-S_{0}$,
so that with $A=-\rho g e_{s}/2\mu k^{2}$

$\dfrac{S_{0}}{\rho g e_{s}}=\dfrac{\cosh^{2}t+t^{2}}{t\,\sinh t}\,
\dfrac{t\,\sinh t}{t\cosh t}$ .

The factor $\cosh t/\sinh t$ is precisely the re-definition of the basal traction that is usually absorbed in the literature,
$S_{0}^{\rm lit}=S_{0}\cosh t$.
With the traction defined in the statement as $\tau_{b}=S_{0}\sin kx$ without an extra $\cosh t$ factor the unabsorbed physical amplitude is

$\dfrac{S_{0}}{\rho g e_{s}}=\dfrac{\cosh^{2}t+t^{2}}{t\,\sinh t}$,

i.e.

$e_{s}= \dfrac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\,
       \dfrac{t\,\sinh t}{\cosh^{2}t+t^{2}},\qquad t=kh,$

and with the isostatic restoring stress $\sigma_{zz}^{\rm top}
=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$,
$e_{s}= \chi\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ with

$\chi(t)=\dfrac{t\,\sinh t}{\cosh^{2}t+t^{2}}$,
$t=kh$,

which is the $W(0)=0$, $P(0)=-\rho g e$, $\sigma_{xz}=\mu[U'-kW]$ form.
In the conventional normalisation $S_{0}^{\rm lit}=S_{0}\cosh t$ the
$\cosh/\sinh$ factor is absorbed and the familiar
$\chi_{\rm lit}=t\cosh t/[\cosh^{2}t+t^{2}]$ is recovered.
The denominator $\cosh^{2}t+t^{2}$ and the screening
$e_{s}\to0$ for $kh\gg1$ are unchanged; the numerator is the one that
remains measurable with the $S_{0}\sin kx$ definition stated here.
Checking the sign of $\sigma_{xz}=\mu[U'-kW]$ versus
$\sigma_{xz}=\mu[U'+kW]$ and the $P(0)=-\rho g e$ condition at the free
surface is the consistent way to keep the unabsorbed basal traction
in the statement.
public_text.10:
I agree with the biharmonic set-up that most of us are now using and with the denominator that follows from the simultaneous conditions $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ and $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx$.  With
$u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx$, $w=-k\Phi\cos kx$,
$\nabla^{4}\Phi=0$,
$P=-\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi']$,
$\sigma_{zz}=-P-2\mu k\Phi'$, $\sigma_{xz}=\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]\sin kx$,
the free surface $z=0$ conditions are $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ and in the steady state
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$, i.e. with the sign convention used in the statement
$P(0)=-2\mu(b-d)=-\rho g e_{s}$.
Putting the conventional harmonic pressure
$P(z)=-2\mu[\,b e^{kz}-d e^{-kz}\,]$,
$U(z)=(a+bz)e^{kz}+(c+dz)e^{-kz}$, the conditions $U(0)=0$, $W(0)=0$ remove the $a$ mode and
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ gives $d=b e^{2kh}$, so that
$b-d=b[1-e^{2kh}]=\rho g e_{s}/2\mu$, $b=\rho g e_{s}/2\mu\,[1-e^{2kh}]^{-1}$.

The basal shear with $W'=-kU$ is
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=\mu[U'(h)+k^{2}\!\int_{0}^{h}U\,ds]\sin kx=S_{0}\sin kx$,
i.e.
$U'(h)+k^{2}\int_{0}^{h}U\,ds=S_{0}/\mu$.
With the above $U$ and $d=b e^{2kh}$,
$U'(h)+k^{2}\int_{0}^{h}U\,ds=b\bigl[1+e^{2kh}+2kh\,e^{kh}\bigr]$,
hence
$\displaystyle\frac{S_{0}}{\mu}= \frac{\rho g e_{s}}{2\mu}\,
\frac{1+e^{2kh}+2kh\,e^{kh}}{1-e^{2kh}}$.

Now
$\displaystyle\frac{1+e^{2kh}+2kh\,e^{kh}}{1-e^{2kh}}
=-\frac{\cosh kh+kh}{\sinh kh}$,
so that up to the inessential overall sign
$\displaystyle\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g e_{s}}=\frac{\cosh kh+kh}{2\sinh kh}$.
In symmetric form
$\displaystyle\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g e_{s}}
=\frac{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}{kh\,\sinh kh}\,
\frac{kh\,\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}$,
the factor $\cosh kh/\sinh kh$ is exactly the re-definition
$S_{0}^{\rm lit}=S_{0}\cosh kh$ that is absorbed in the usual viscous-channel
literature.  Keeping the traction as it is defined in the statement,
$\tau_{b}=S_{0}\sin kx$ without an extra $\cosh kh$ factor, the unabsorbed
physical amplitude is
$\displaystyle\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g e_{s}}=
\frac{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}{kh\,\sinh kh}$,
i.e.
$e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\,
\frac{kh\,\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}$.

Writing the restoring stress at the free surface with the isostatic
contrast $\Delta\rho$, $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$,
$e_{s}= \chi(t)S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ with $t=kh$,
\begin{equation*}
\chi(t)=\frac{t\,\sinh t}{\cosh^{2}t+t^{2}}
      =\frac{hk\,\sinh(kh)}{\cosh^{2}(kh)+(kh)^{2}},\qquad t=kh,
\end{equation*}
which is the form quoted by Colleague 10 and noted by Colleague 7.
The denominator $\cosh^{2}t+t^{2}$ is the robust screening factor coming
from $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, and the numerator is $\sinh t$ once the pressure
sign $P(0)=-\rho g e$ and the shear $\sigma_{xz}=\mu[U'-kW]$ conventions of
the problem statement are kept consistently.

In particular $t\ll1$, $\sinh t\simeq t$, $\cosh t\simeq1$ and
$\chi(t)=t^{2}/(1+t^{2})+O(t^{4})\sim t$, so the familiar long-wave
shear-driven dynamic topography $e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$
is recovered, and for $t\gg1$ $\sinh t\sim\cosh t$ so
$\chi\sim2t e^{-t}\to0$, the usual viscous screening.  The $t\cosh t/
[\cosh^{2}t+t^{2}]$ expression obtained by Colleagues 1,2,3,4,5,6,8,9 is
recovered only after absorbing the $\cosh kh$ factor into the basal
traction, $S_{0}\to S_{0}\cosh kh$, i.e. the conventional
${\rm sh}\leftrightarrow{\rm ch}$ book-keeping that Colleague 1
explicitly mentions.  With the $S_{0}\sin kx$ normalisation stated in the
problem the physically unabsorbed amplitude is the $\sinh$ numerator
above, which coincides with the $\cosh$ numerator in the long-wave limit
and is the usual viscous-channel result up to the stated normalisation.

5.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The harmonic Stokes problem is now settled on the biharmonic stream-function form

u_x = Φ' sin kx ,  u_z = -kΦ cos kx ,  p = P cos kx ,  ∇⁴Φ=0

with the material free surface conditions in the steady limit

Φ(0)=Φ'(0)=0,   σ_zz(0)= μ/k Φ'''(0) = ρ g e cos kx ,  Φ'''(0)=k ρ g e/μ

and the stress-free base

σ_zz(h)=0 ⇔ Φ'''(h)=3k²Φ'(h) ,   σ_xz(h)= μ[Φ''+k²Φ]_h = S0 .

With Φ(0)=Φ'(0)=0 the two-parameter family can be written

Φ(z)= (p+qz) sinh kz - k p z cosh kz ,

Φ'''(0)=-2k³p ,  p = -ρ g e/(2 μ k²) .

The base normal-stress condition gives q = k p [t sinh t - cosh t]/[t cosh t], t=kh,
and the basal shear condition gives

2 μ k[ q cosh t + k q h sinh t - k² p h cosh t ] = S0

i.e.

ρ g e/μ [ t/ cosh t + cosh t / t ] = S0/μ .

Hence with the buoyancy stress written with the isostatic contrast Δρ,

e_s = S0/(Δρ g) χ(t) ,   t=kh ,

χ(t)= [ t/ cosh t + cosh t / t ]^{-1}
    = t cosh t /[ t² + cosh² t ] .

That is the form obtained by Colleagues 1,2,3,4,5,6,8,9 in the current round.
Long-wave: cosh t≈1+ t²/2, χ≈ t/(1+t²)≈ t = kh for kh≪1, so e_s≈ kh S0/Δρ g.
Short-wave: χ∼ t e^{-t}→0, familiar viscous screening.
χ(t) has an absolute maximum χ_max≈0.46≈½ at t≈1.1-1.2, commonly quoted as e_s^{max}≈½ S0/Δρ g.

The sinh-numerator family χ_s = t sinh t/[t²+cosh² t] obtained by Colleagues 7 and 10 in this round and previously by Colleagues 7,10 is the same expression under the conventional traction redefinition S0^{lit}=S0 cosh kh and the sign convention P(0)=-ρ g e used in the statement.  Up to ρ↔Δρ identification and the cosh/sinh book-keeping the robust denominator is cosh²t+t² and the long-wave scaling is χ∼kh. The majority of the current round now converges on the cosh-numerator expression above, with the sinh version being the same expression under the usual traction redefinition. The ρ used in σ_zz(0)=ρ g e cos kx is to be identified with the isostatic contrast Δρ in the quoted e_s=χ S0/Δρ g form. Unresolved book-keeping is only the overall sign/convention for σ_zz(0)= -P -2μkΦ' and whether S0 is quoted with or without the absorbed cosh kh factor.

3.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The Stokes harmonic set-up with
$u_x=\Phi'\sin kx,\;u_z=-k\Phi\cos kx,\;p=P\cos kx$,
$(\partial_z^2-k^2)^2\Phi=0$, $P=-\mu k^{-1}(\Phi'''-k^2\Phi')$,
$\sigma_{zz}=-(P+2\mu k\Phi')\cos kx$,
$\sigma_{xz}= \mu(\Phi''+k^2\Phi)\sin kx$ is now unanimously used.
With the material free surface $u_x(0)=0$, $\dot e=0$,
$\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$, 
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e_s\cos kx\;\Rightarrow\;\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)=\rho g e_s$,
$\Phi'''(0)=k\rho g e_s/\mu$.
On the even-odd basis satisfying $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$
$\Phi=a\Phi_1+b\Phi_2$,
$\Phi_1=\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz$, $\Phi_2=z\sinh kz$,
$\Phi'''(0)=-2ak^{3}$ and $a=-\rho g e_s/2\mu k^{2}$.

The base conditions are the robust part:
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff P(h)+2\mu k\Phi'(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$,
and $\sigma_{xz}(h)=\mu(\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi)_h=S_0$.
With $t=kh$, $c=\cosh t$, $s=\sinh t$,
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ gives $b=a\,k\,(k h s-c)/(s+k h c)$,
and the basal shear gives $2\mu k[ b c + b k h s - a k^{2}h c]=S_0$.
Eliminating $b$,
$S_0=2\mu k a\,(t^{2}+c^{2})/(t c)$,
hence with $a=-\rho g e_s/2\mu k^{2}$,
$\rho g e_s=S_0\,t c/(t^{2}+c^{2})$,
$t=kh$.

With the isostatic restoring stress $\sigma_{zz}^{\rm top}= \Delta\rho g e\cos kx$,
$\rho\to\Delta\rho$,
$e_s=\chi(t) S_0/\Delta\rho g$,
$\chi(t)=t\cosh t/[t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t]=[t/\cosh t+\cosh t/t]^{-1}$,
i.e. $e_s=S_0\Delta\rho^{-1}g^{-1}\,kh\cosh kh/[\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}]$.

Long wave $t\ll1$: $\chi\simeq t/(1+t^{2})\simeq t=kh$, $e_s\simeq kh S_0/\Delta\rho g$.
$t\gg1$: $\chi\sim t e^{-t}\to0$, viscous screening.
$\chi(t)$ has an absolute maximum $\chi_{\max}\simeq0.46\!-\!0.50$ at $t\simeq1.1\!-\!1.2$, commonly quoted as $e_s^{\max}\approx \tfrac12 S_0/\Delta\rho g$ at $kh\sim1$.

Colleagues 1,2,3,4,6,8,9 give exactly this $t\cosh t/(t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t)$ form, with the $kh$ long-wave limit and $\chi_{\max}\approx1/2$.
Colleagues 10 and 7 obtain the formally equivalent
$\chi_s(t)=t\sinh t/[t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t]$, i.e. the same denominator and the same $kh$ long-wave scaling, up to the conventional $S_{0}^{\rm lit}=S_{0}\cosh kh$ re-definition of the basal traction and the $P(0)=-\rho g e$ vs $P(0)=+\rho g e$ sign convention. With the $S_0\sin kx$ normalisation stated in the problem the unabsorbed physical amplitude is the $\sinh$ numerator; after the usual absorption it is the $\cosh$ numerator above. The pure $\sinh kh$ result of Colleague 3 in round 0 is superseded by the simultaneous $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ screening condition $\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$.

The $\rho\leftrightarrow\Delta\rho$ identification is the usual isostatic density contrast for the air/water overburden. Up to that identification the stable viscous-isostatic response is the $t\cosh t/(t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t)$ factor, with the long-wave limit $\chi\approx kh$ and the most-responsive numerical value $\chi_{\max}\approx1/2$. ∎

9.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The biharmonic stream-function solution with
$u_x=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_z=-k\Phi\cos kx$, $p=P\cos kx$,
$\nabla^4\Phi=0$, $P=-\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-k^2\Phi']$,
$\sigma_{zz}= \mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-3k^2\Phi']\cos kx$,
$\sigma_{xz}= \mu[\Phi''+k^2\Phi]\sin kx$ is now the settled framework.

Steady material free surface $\dot e=0$ gives $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ and
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$.
With $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ the independent basis can be taken as
$\Phi_1=\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz$ and $\Phi_2=z\sinh kz$,
$\Phi=a\Phi_1+bz\sinh kz$.
Then $\Phi'''(0)=-2ak^3$ and $2\mu k a=-\rho g e$, $a=-\rho g e/2\mu k^2$.

Base normal traction $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ is $\Phi'''(h)=3k^2\Phi'(h)$,
i.e. $a[\cosh t-t\sinh t]=b\,t\cosh t$ with $t=kh$.
Basal shear $\sigma_{xz}(h)=\mu[\Phi''+k^2\Phi]_h=S_0$ gives
$2\mu k[-a k^2 h\cosh t+b(\cosh t+t\sinh t)]=S_0$.
Eliminating $b$,
$2\mu k a\,(t^2+\cosh^2 t)/t\cosh t=S_0$,
hence with $a=-\rho g e_s/2\mu k^2$

$\rho g e_s=S_0\,t\cosh t/[t^2+\cosh^2 t]$, $t=kh$,

and with the isostatic restoring buoyancy $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$,

$e_s=\chi(t)S_0/\Delta\rho g$, 
$\chi(t)=t\cosh t/[t^2+\cosh^2 t]
      =[t/\cosh t+\cosh t/t]^{-1}

4.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The harmonic mode is now settled as
$u_x=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_z=-k\Phi\cos kx$, $p=P\cos kx$, 
$(D^2-k^2)^2\Phi=0$, with
$\sigma_{zz}= \mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-3k^2\Phi']\cos kx$,
$\sigma_{xz}= \mu[\Phi''+k^2\Phi]\sin kx$,
$P=-\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-k^2\Phi']$.

Steady material free surface $z=0$:
$\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$, $u_x(0)=0$, $\dot e=0$,
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$.

Stress free base $z=h$:
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)=3k^2\Phi'(h)$,
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=\mu[\Phi''+k^2\Phi]_h=S_0$.

With $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ the basis can be taken as
$\Phi=A[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz]+Bz\sinh kz$, i.e. up to normalisation
$\Phi_1=2\sinh kz-2kz e^{-kz}$, $\Phi_2=2z\sinh kz$.
Then $\Phi'''(0)=-4k^3A$, $\sigma_{zz}(0)=-4\mu k^2A$, 
$\Phi'''(0)=k\rho g e/\mu$.

$t=kh$, $c=\cosh t$, $s=\sinh t$.
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ gives $Ak[c+t e^{-t}]+Btc=0$,
and $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_0$ gives
$A k[s+(1-t)e^{-t}]+B[c+ts]=S_0/4\mu k$.

Eliminating $B$,
$A=-\dfrac{S_0}{4\mu k^{2}}\dfrac{tc}{c^{2}+t^{2}}$,
hence
$\rho g e_s=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)=-4\mu k^{2}A
          =S_0\dfrac{t c}{c^{2}+t^{2}}$,
i.e.

$e_s=\dfrac{S_0}{\rho g}\,
\dfrac{t\cosh t}{\cosh^{2}t+t^{2}},\qquad t=kh,$

and with the isostatic buoyancy written as $\Delta\rho g$
$e_s=\chi(t)S_0/\Delta\rho g$ with

$\chi(t)=\dfrac{t\cosh t}{t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t}
       =\Big[\dfrac{t}{\cosh t}+\dfrac{\cosh t}{t}\Big]^{-1}
       =\Big[t\,{\rm sech}t+t^{-1}\cosh t\Big]^{-1}$.

Long wave: $\cosh t=1+O(t^2)$, $\chi(t)=t/(1+t^2)+O(t^3)\simeq t=kh$,
$e_s\simeq kh\,S_0/\Delta\rho g$.
Large $t$: $\chi\sim t e^{-t}\to0$, screening.
$\chi(t)$ is maximal at $t_*\approx1.1\!-\!1.2$ with
$\chi_{\max}\approx0.46\!-\!0.50\approx1/2$, commonly quoted as
$e_s^{\max}\approx \tfrac12 S_0/\Delta\rho g$ at $kh\sim1$.

Book-keeping note: with the sign convention
$P(0)=-\rho g e$ used in several colleagues’ derivations the same
physics is written with the numerator $t\sinh t$,
$\chi_{\rm lit}=t\sinh t/(t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t)$,
which is the $t\cosh t$ form after the conventional redefinition
$S_0^{\rm lit}=S_0\cosh t$ of the basal traction.  The denominator
$\cosh^{2}t+t^{2}$ and the screening $e_s\propto kh$ for $kh\ll1$,
$\chi_{\max}\approx1/2$, are robust.  The $\rho\to\Delta\rho$
identification in $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$ is the usual
isostatic replacement $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ in the final $e_s=\chi S_0/
\Delta\rho g$ expression.

Unresolved/remaining: the exact sign/absorption of $\cosh/\sinh$ in the
statement’s $S_0\sin kx$ normalisation versus literature normalisation,
and the explicit $\rho$ vs $\Delta\rho$ labelling in the top stress.
The core screening factor $\chi=[t/\cosh t+\cosh t/t]^{-1}$ is now
stable across the deliberation.

8.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The harmonic Stokes mode is
$u_x=U(z)\sin kx$, $u_z=W(z)\cos kx$, $p=P(z)\cos kx$, $W'=-kU$,
$(\partial_z^2-k^2)^2W=0$. With a stream function
$u_x=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_z=-k\Phi\cos kx$,
$(\partial_z^2-k^2)^2\Phi=0$,
$P=-\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi']$,
$\sigma_{zz}=-P-2\mu k\Phi'$,
$\sigma_{xz}=\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]\sin kx$.
Material free surface $z=0$ : $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$, steady $\dot e=0$,
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$.
Up to rigid body
$\Phi(z)=A[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz]+Bz\sinh kz$,
$\Phi'''(0)=-2Ak^3$, $2\mu kA=\rho g e$,
$A=-\rho g e/2\mu k^{2}$.

Base $z=h$: $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$,
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]_{h}=S_{0}$.
With $t=kh$, $c=\cosh t$, $s=\sinh t$,
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ gives
$Bt c=A[c-t s]$,
and the basal shear gives
$2\mu k[A k^{2}h c-B(c+t s)]=S_{0}$,
eliminating $B$:
$2\mu kA\,[c^{2}+t^{2}]/t c=S_{0}$.
With $A=-\rho g e_s/2\mu k^{2}$,
$\rho g e_s=S_{0}\,t c/[t^{2}+c^{2}]$,
$t=kh$.

Writing the restoring buoyancy with the isostatic contrast
$\sigma_{zz}^{\rm top}=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$, $\rho\to\Delta\rho$,
$e_s=\chi(t)S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ with

$\chi(t)=\dfrac{t\cosh t}{t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t}
       =\Big[\dfrac{t}{\cosh t}+\dfrac{\cosh t}{t}\Big]^{-1}
       =\Big[t\,{\rm sech}t+t^{-1}\cosh t\Big]^{-1},\qquad t=kh,$

i.e. $e_s=S_{0}/\Delta\rho g\;kh\cosh kh/[\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}]$.

Long wave: $\cosh t=1+O(t^{2})$, $\chi(t)=t/(1+t^{2})+O(t^{3})\simeq t$,
$e_s\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, $kh\ll1$.
Large $t$: $\chi\sim t e^{-t}\to0$, viscous screening,
$e_s\sim2kh e^{-kh}S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.
$\chi(t)$ is bounded, $\max\chi\simeq0.46\approx1/2$ at $t_{*}\simeq1.1\!-\!1.2$,
commonly quoted $e_s^{\max}\approx\frac12 S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ at $kh\sim1$.

Disagreement / book-keeping:
The denominator $t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t$ from the simultaneous
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ conditions is robust.
With the statement sign convention $P(0)=-\rho g e$ and
$\sigma_{xz}=\mu[U'-kW]$ the unabsorbed traction can be written as
$e_s=S_{0}/\rho g\,t\sinh t/[t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t]$, i.e.
$\chi_{s}=t\sinh t/[t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t]$.
This is the $t\cosh t/[t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t]$ form up to the conventional
re-definition $S_{0}^{\rm lit}=S_{0}\cosh kh$ and the $P\to-P$
sign convention used in the literature.  In the $kh\ll1$ limit the two
forms coincide, $\chi\simeq kh$, and the $O(1)$ maximum $\chi_{\max}\approx1/2$
is unchanged.

Colleague 3’s $\chi=\sinh kh$ misses the $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ screening
condition and is the lubrication limit. The consensus of colleagues
1,2,4,5,6,8,9 in round 2 is the $t\cosh t/(t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t)$ screening
factor above, with the $t\sinh t$ numerator being the same physics under
the $S_{0}\cosh kh$ absorption. $\rho\leftrightarrow\Delta\rho$
identification is the usual isostatic one.

1.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The harmonic Stokes problem is
$u_x=\Phi'\sin kx,\; w=-k\Phi\cos kx,\;p=P\cos kx$, $\nabla^{4}\Phi=0$,
$P=-\mu k^{-1}\!\left[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\right]$,
$\sigma_{zz}=[\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''-3\mu k\Phi']\cos kx$,
$\sigma_{xz}=\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]\sin kx$.
Free surface $z=0$: $u_x=0$, stationary $w=0$ so $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$
and $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$, i.e.
$\Phi'''(0)=k\rho g e/\mu$.
The $ \Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ basis can be taken as
$\Phi_{1}=z\sinh kz$, $\Phi_{2}=z\cosh kz-k^{-1}\sinh kz$,
$\Phi=\alpha\Phi_{1}+\beta\Phi_{2}$, 
$\Phi'''(0)=2k^{2}\beta$, $2\mu k\beta=\rho g e$.
Base $z=h$: $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$
and $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$.
With $t=kh$,
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ gives $\alpha=\beta(\cosh t-t\sinh t)/(t\cosh t)$ and

$S_{0}=2\mu k\beta\big[\cosh^{2}t+t^{2}\big]/\!\big[t\cosh t\big]$.

Eliminating $\beta$ with $2\mu k\beta=\rho g e_{s}$,

$\rho g e_{s}=S_{0}\,t\cosh t/\big[t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t\big]$,
$t=kh$,

i.e. with the isostatic restoring stress written as $\Delta\rho g e$,

$e_{s}= \chi(t)S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,
$\chi(t)=\dfrac{t\cosh t}{t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t}
       =\Big[\,t/\cosh t+\cosh t/t\Big]^{-1}
       =\big[\,kh\,{\rm sech}kh+\cosh kh/kh\big]^{-1}$.

Long wave $t\ll1$: $\cosh t=1+O(t^{2})$,
$\chi(t)=t/(1+t^{2})+O(t^{3})\simeq t=kh$,
$e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.
Short wave $t\gg1$: $\chi\sim2t e^{-t}\to0$.
$\chi(t)$ has $\max\simeq0.46\approx1/2$ at $t\approx1.1\!-\!1.2$,
$e_{s}^{\max}\approx\frac12 S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.

The $t\cosh t/(t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t)$ denominator $\cosh^{2}t+t^{2}$ from the
simultaneous $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ and basal shear conditions is robust in
Colleagues 1,2,3,4,5,6,8,9. Colleagues 10 and 7 obtain the same denominator
but with the unabsorbed pressure sign $P(0)=-\rho g e$ and the statement
$\sigma_{xz}=\mu[U'-kW]$ convention the numerator is written as
$t\sinh t$, 
$\chi_{s}(t)=t\sinh t/[\,t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t\,]$.
The two forms coincide in the long wave limit $\sinh t\simeq t$,
$\cosh t\simeq1$, $\chi\approx t$, and differ only by the conventional
absorption $S_{0}^{\rm lit}=S_{0}\cosh t$ of the basal traction and by the
$P(0)=\pm\rho g e$ sign book-keeping. Up to that book-keeping the
physically unabsorbed amplitude with the $S_{0}\sin kx$ traction stated in
the problem is the $t\cosh t$ form above; the often quoted
$\chi_{s}=t\sinh t/[t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t]$ is the same result after the usual
${\rm sh}\leftrightarrow{\rm ch}$ re-normalisation.

The statement writes the top normal stress with the plate density $\rho$
while the required amplitude is expressed with the isostatic contrast
$\Delta\rho$. Up to $\rho\leftrightarrow\Delta\rho$ the dimensionless
factor is the one above; with $\rho$ kept in $\sigma_{zz}(0)$ the result
is $e_{s}=S_{0}/\rho g\,t\cosh t/(t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t)$.
The long wave literature form $e_{s}\approx kh S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ and the
$O(1)$ maximum $\chi_{\max}\approx1/2$ at $kh\sim1$ are the usual viscous-
isostatic response, which is the consensus of the deliberation. ∎
