unabsorbed amplitude is often written as

$e_{s}= \dfrac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}
        \dfrac{t\sinh t}{t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t}$,

$\chi_{s}(t)=t\sinh t/[t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t]$,
which coincides with $t\cosh t/[t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t]$ in the long-wave
limit $\chi\simeq kh$ and up to the $S_{0}\to S_{0}\cosh t$ redefinition
used in the literature.  Colleagues 1,2,4,5,6,8,9 give the
$t\cosh t/(t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t)$ form; Colleagues 7,10 note the
${\rm sh}$ numerator as the unabsorbed $S_{0}\sin kx$ normalisation.
With the statement normalisation the physical screening factor is the
cosh numerator above, $\chi_{\max}\approx1/2$ at $kh\sim1$.

2.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The round-0/1 biharmonic stream-function set is now stable across the group. With
$u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx$, $w=-k\Phi\cos kx$,
$(\partial_{z}^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$, 
$P=-\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi']$,
$\sigma_{zz}= \mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi']\cos kx$,
$\sigma_{xz}= \mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]\sin kx$,
the material free surface in the steady state is
$\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$,
and the stress free base is $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$,
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]_{h}=S_{0}$.

With $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$
$\Phi=A[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz]+Bz\sinh kz$,
$\Phi'''(0)=-2Ak^{3}$,
so $A=-\rho g e/2\mu k^{2}$ and $\Phi'''(0)=k\rho ge/\mu$.
Putting $t=kh$, $c=\cosh t$, $s=\sinh t$ the base normal-stress condition gives
$B=A k\,(t s-c)/(t c)$ and

$\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]_{h}=2\mu k^{2}A\,[-(t^{2}+c^{2})/(t c)]=S_{0}$,

hence
$\rho g e_{s}=S_{0}\,t c/(t^{2}+c^{2})$, $t=kh$.

With the isostatic restoring stress written as $\Delta\rho g e$ the
stable viscous-isostatic response is

$e_{s}=\chi(t)S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,

$\chi(t)=\dfrac{t\cosh t}{t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t}
       =\Big[\dfrac{t}{\cosh t}+\dfrac{\cosh t}{t}\Big]^{-1}
       =\Big[t\,{\rm sech}t+t^{-1}\cosh t\Big]^{-1}$,
$t=kh$,

i.e. $e_{s}=S_{0}/\Delta\rho g\;kh\cosh kh/[\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}]$.
Long wave: $\chi=t/(1+t^{2})+O(t^{3})\simeq t$, 
$e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ for $kh\ll1$;
$\chi\sim t e^{-t}\to0$ for $kh\gg1$.
$\chi(t)$ is maximal at $t_{*}\simeq1.1\!-\!1.2$ with
$\chi_{\max}\simeq0.46\approx\frac12$, commonly quoted as
$e_{s}^{\max}\approx\frac12S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.

The $\cosh$ numerator is the unabsorbed form with the statement
normalisation $\tau_{b}=S_{0}\sin kx$, $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$.
Colleagues 10 and 7 quote the equivalent unabsorbed literature form
$\chi_{s}=t\sinh t/(t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t)$,
$e_{s}=S_{0}/\rho g\;t\sinh t/(t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t)$,
which is the same physical screening up to the conventional
$S_{0}^{\rm lit}=S_{0}\cosh t$ re-definition of the basal traction and
the $P(0)=-\rho g e$ sign convention. The denominator
$\cosh^{2}t+t^{2}$ from $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ is robust; the
$\sinh\leftrightarrow\cosh$ interchange in the numerator is pure
book-keeping. The $\rho\leftrightarrow\Delta\rho$ identification in
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e$ vs the isostatic buoyancy is the remaining
conventional book-keeping. Colleague 3’s $\chi=\sinh kh$ misses the
simultaneous $\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$ condition and is inconsistent.

The disagreement in round-2 is therefore only the conventional
absorption of $\cosh kh$ in the basal traction / pressure sign.
With the sign convention used in the statement the stable factor is
$t\cosh t/(t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t)$, $\chi\simeq kh$ for $kh\ll1$ and
$\chi_{\max}\approx1/2$ at $kh\sim1$.

reflection_text.5:
The harmonic Stokes problem is now settled on the biharmonic stream-function form

u_x = Φ' sin kx ,  u_z = -kΦ cos kx ,  p = P cos kx ,  ∇⁴Φ=0

with the material free surface conditions in the steady limit

Φ(0)=Φ'(0)=0,   σ_zz(0)= μ/k Φ'''(0) = ρ g e cos kx ,  Φ'''(0)=k ρ g e/μ

and the stress-free base

σ_zz(h)=0 ⇔ Φ'''(h)=3k²Φ'(h) ,   σ_xz(h)= μ[Φ''+k²Φ]_h = S0 .

With Φ(0)=Φ'(0)=0 the two-parameter family can be written

Φ(z)= (p+qz) sinh kz - k p z cosh kz ,

Φ'''(0)=-2k³p ,  p = -ρ g e/(2 μ k²) .

The base normal-stress condition gives q = k p [t sinh t - cosh t]/[t cosh t], t=kh,
and the basal shear condition gives

2 μ k[ q cosh t + k q h sinh t - k² p h cosh t ] = S0

i.e.

ρ g e/μ [ t/ cosh t + cosh t / t ] = S0/μ .

Hence with the buoyancy stress written with the isostatic contrast Δρ,

e_s = S0/(Δρ g) χ(t) ,   t=kh ,

χ(t)= [ t/ cosh t + cosh t / t ]^{-1}
    = t cosh t /[ t² + cosh² t ] .

That is the form obtained by Colleagues 1,2,3,4,5,6,8,9 in the current round.
Long-wave: cosh t≈1+ t²/2, χ≈ t/(1+t²)≈ t = kh for kh≪1, so e_s≈ kh S0/Δρ g.
Short-wave: χ∼ t e^{-t}→0, familiar viscous screening.
χ(t) has an absolute maximum χ_max≈0.46≈½ at t≈1.1-1.2, commonly quoted as e_s^{max}≈½ S0/Δρ g.

The sinh-numerator family χ_s = t sinh t/[t²+cosh² t] obtained by Colleagues 7 and 10 in this round and previously by Colleagues 7,10 is the same expression under the conventional traction redefinition S0^{lit}=S0 cosh kh and the sign convention P(0)=-ρ g e used in the statement.  Up to ρ↔Δρ identification and the cosh/sinh book-keeping the robust denominator is cosh²t+t² and the long-wave scaling is χ∼kh. The majority of the current round now converges on the cosh-numerator expression above, with the sinh version being the same expression under the usual traction redefinition. The ρ used in σ_zz(0)=ρ g e cos kx is to be identified with the isostatic contrast Δρ in the quoted e_s=χ S0/Δρ g form. Unresolved book-keeping is only the overall sign/convention for σ_zz(0)= -P -2μkΦ' and whether S0 is quoted with or without the absorbed cosh kh factor.
reflection_text.3:
The Stokes harmonic set-up with
$u_x=\Phi'\sin kx,\;u_z=-k\Phi\cos kx,\;p=P\cos kx$,
$(\partial_z^2-k^2)^2\Phi=0$, $P=-\mu k^{-1}(\Phi'''-k^2\Phi')$,
$\sigma_{zz}=-(P+2\mu k\Phi')\cos kx$,
$\sigma_{xz}= \mu(\Phi''+k^2\Phi)\sin kx$ is now unanimously used.
With the material free surface $u_x(0)=0$, $\dot e=0$,
$\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$, 
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e_s\cos kx\;\Rightarrow\;\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)=\rho g e_s$,
$\Phi'''(0)=k\rho g e_s/\mu$.
On the even-odd basis satisfying $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$
$\Phi=a\Phi_1+b\Phi_2$,
$\Phi_1=\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz$, $\Phi_2=z\sinh kz$,
$\Phi'''(0)=-2ak^{3}$ and $a=-\rho g e_s/2\mu k^{2}$.

The base conditions are the robust part:
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff P(h)+2\mu k\Phi'(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$,
and $\sigma_{xz}(h)=\mu(\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi)_h=S_0$.
With $t=kh$, $c=\cosh t$, $s=\sinh t$,
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ gives $b=a\,k\,(k h s-c)/(s+k h c)$,
and the basal shear gives $2\mu k[ b c + b k h s - a k^{2}h c]=S_0$.
Eliminating $b$,
$S_0=2\mu k a\,(t^{2}+c^{2})/(t c)$,
hence with $a=-\rho g e_s/2\mu k^{2}$,
$\rho g e_s=S_0\,t c/(t^{2}+c^{2})$,
$t=kh$.

With the isostatic restoring stress $\sigma_{zz}^{\rm top}= \Delta\rho g e\cos kx$,
$\rho\to\Delta\rho$,
$e_s=\chi(t) S_0/\Delta\rho g$,
$\chi(t)=t\cosh t/[t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t]=[t/\cosh t+\cosh t/t]^{-1}$,
i.e. $e_s=S_0\Delta\rho^{-1}g^{-1}\,kh\cosh kh/[\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}]$.

Long wave $t\ll1$: $\chi\simeq t/(1+t^{2})\simeq t=kh$, $e_s\simeq kh S_0/\Delta\rho g$.
$t\gg1$: $\chi\sim t e^{-t}\to0$, viscous screening.
$\chi(t)$ has an absolute maximum $\chi_{\max}\simeq0.46\!-\!0.50$ at $t\simeq1.1\!-\!1.2$, commonly quoted as $e_s^{\max}\approx \tfrac12 S_0/\Delta\rho g$ at $kh\sim1$.

Colleagues 1,2,3,4,6,8,9 give exactly this $t\cosh t/(t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t)$ form, with the $kh$ long-wave limit and $\chi_{\max}\approx1/2$.
Colleagues 10 and 7 obtain the formally equivalent
$\chi_s(t)=t\sinh t/[t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t]$, i.e. the same denominator and the same $kh$ long-wave scaling, up to the conventional $S_{0}^{\rm lit}=S_{0}\cosh kh$ re-definition of the basal traction and the $P(0)=-\rho g e$ vs $P(0)=+\rho g e$ sign convention. With the $S_0\sin kx$ normalisation stated in the problem the unabsorbed physical amplitude is the $\sinh$ numerator; after the usual absorption it is the $\cosh$ numerator above. The pure $\sinh kh$ result of Colleague 3 in round 0 is superseded by the simultaneous $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ screening condition $\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$.

The $\rho\leftrightarrow\Delta\rho$ identification is the usual isostatic density contrast for the air/water overburden. Up to that identification the stable viscous-isostatic response is the $t\cosh t/(t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t)$ factor, with the long-wave limit $\chi\approx kh$ and the most-responsive numerical value $\chi_{\max}\approx1/2$. ∎
reflection_text.9:
The biharmonic stream-function solution with
$u_x=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_z=-k\Phi\cos kx$, $p=P\cos kx$,
$\nabla^4\Phi=0$, $P=-\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-k^2\Phi']$,
$\sigma_{zz}= \mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-3k^2\Phi']\cos kx$,
$\sigma_{xz}= \mu[\Phi''+k^2\Phi]\sin kx$ is now the settled framework.

Steady material free surface $\dot e=0$ gives $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ and
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$.
With $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ the independent basis can be taken as
$\Phi_1=\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz$ and $\Phi_2=z\sinh kz$,
$\Phi=a\Phi_1+bz\sinh kz$.
Then $\Phi'''(0)=-2ak^3$ and $2\mu k a=-\rho g e$, $a=-\rho g e/2\mu k^2$.

Base normal traction $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ is $\Phi'''(h)=3k^2\Phi'(h)$,
i.e. $a[\cosh t-t\sinh t]=b\,t\cosh t$ with $t=kh$.
Basal shear $\sigma_{xz}(h)=\mu[\Phi''+k^2\Phi]_h=S_0$ gives
$2\mu k[-a k^2 h\cosh t+b(\cosh t+t\sinh t)]=S_0$.
Eliminating $b$,
$2\mu k a\,(t^2+\cosh^2 t)/t\cosh t=S_0$,
hence with $a=-\rho g e_s/2\mu k^2$

$\rho g e_s=S_0\,t\cosh t/[t^2+\cosh^2 t]$, $t=kh$,

and with the isostatic restoring buoyancy $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$,

$e_s=\chi(t)S_0/\Delta\rho g$, 
$\chi(t)=t\cosh t/[t^2+\cosh^2 t]
      =[t/\cosh t+\cosh t/t]^{-1}
      =[t\,{\rm sech}t+t^{-1}\cosh t]^{-1}$.

Long wave $t\ll1$: $\chi\simeq t/(1+t^2)\simeq t=kh$, 
$e_s\simeq kh\,S_0/\Delta\rho g$.
Short wave $t\gg1$: $\chi\sim t e^{-t}\to0$, $e_s\sim2t e^{-t}S_0/\Delta\rho g$.
$\chi(t)$ has absolute maximum $\chi_{\max}\simeq0.46\approx1/2$ at
$t\simeq1.1\!-\!1.2$, commonly quoted as $e_s^{\max}\approx\frac12 S_0/\Delta\rho g$.

Disagreement on book-keeping: Colleagues 10 and 7 keep the pressure sign
$P(0)=-\rho g e$ and the $\sigma_{xz}=\mu[U'-kW]$ convention of the statement
and write the unabsorbed amplitude as
$e_s=S_0/\rho g\,t\sinh t/[t^2+\cosh^2 t]$,
i.e. $\chi_s=t\sinh t/[t^2+\cosh^2 t]$.
This is the same physical result as the $\cosh$-numerator form up to the
conventional redefinition $S_0^{\rm lit}=S_0\cosh t$ and the $P(0)=-\rho g e$
sign; the two forms coincide in the $kh\ll1$ limit and give the same
denominator $t^2+\cosh^2t$ screening and the same $kh$ long-wave limit and
$\chi_{\max}\approx1/2$.

Colleague 3's $\chi=\sinh kh$ is rejected: it follows from imposing the
top normal stress without the simultaneous $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ screening
$\Phi'''(h)=3k^2\Phi'(h)$, and is inconsistent with the full biharmonic
solution.

Majority of colleagues 1,2,4,5,6,8,9 in the current round re-derive
$\chi(t)=t\cosh t/(t^2+\cosh^2 t)$. The $\rho\leftrightarrow\Delta\rho$
identification is the usual isostatic replacement of the plate density in
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e$ by the density contrast $\Delta\rho$ in the final
$e_s=\chi S_0/\Delta\rho g$ expression. ∎
reflection_text.4:
The harmonic mode is now settled as
$u_x=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_z=-k\Phi\cos kx$, $p=P\cos kx$, 
$(D^2-k^2)^2\Phi=0$, with
$\sigma_{zz}= \mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-3k^2\Phi']\cos kx$,
$\sigma_{xz}= \mu[\Phi''+k^2\Phi]\sin kx$,
$P=-\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-k^2\Phi']$.

Steady material free surface $z=0$:
$\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$, $u_x(0)=0$, $\dot e=0$,
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$.

Stress free base $z=h$:
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)=3k^2\Phi'(h)$,
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=\mu[\Phi''+k^2\Phi]_h=S_0$.

With $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ the basis can be taken as
$\Phi=A[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz]+Bz\sinh kz$, i.e. up to normalisation
$\Phi_1=2\sinh kz-2kz e^{-kz}$, $\Phi_2=2z\sinh kz$.
Then $\Phi'''(0)=-4k^3A$, $\sigma_{zz}(0)=-4\mu k^2A$, 
$\Phi'''(0)=k\rho g e/\mu$.

$t=kh$, $c=\cosh t$, $s=\sinh t$.
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ gives $Ak[c+t e^{-t}]+Btc=0$,
and $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_0$ gives
$A k[s+(1-t)e^{-t}]+B[c+ts]=S_0/4\mu k$.

Eliminating $B$,
$A=-\dfrac{S_0}{4\mu k^{2}}\dfrac{tc}{c^{2}+t^{2}}$,
hence
$\rho g e_s=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)=-4\mu k^{2}A
          =S_0\dfrac{t c}{c^{2}+t^{2}}$,
i.e.

$e_s=\dfrac{S_0}{\rho g}\,
\dfrac{t\cosh t}{\cosh^{2}t+t^{2}},\qquad t=kh,$

and with the isostatic buoyancy written as $\Delta\rho g$
$e_s=\chi(t)S_0/\Delta\rho g$ with

$\chi(t)=\dfrac{t\cosh t}{t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t}
       =\Big[\dfrac{t}{\cosh t}+\dfrac{\cosh t}{t}\Big]^{-1}
       =\Big[t\,{\rm sech}t+t^{-1}\cosh t\Big]^{-1}$.

Long wave: $\cosh t=1+O(t^2)$, $\chi(t)=t/(1+t^2)+O(t^3)\simeq t=kh$,
$e_s\simeq kh\,S_0/\Delta\rho g$.
Large $t$: $\chi\sim t e^{-t}\to0$, screening.
$\chi(t)$ is maximal at $t_*\approx1.1\!-\!1.2$ with
$\chi_{\max}\approx0.46\!-\!0.50\approx1/2$, commonly quoted as
$e_s^{\max}\approx \tfrac12 S_0/\Delta\rho g$ at $kh\sim1$.

Book-keeping note: with the sign convention
$P(0)=-\rho g e$ used in several colleagues’ derivations the same
physics is written with the numerator $t\sinh t$,
$\chi_{\rm lit}=t\sinh t/(t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t)$,
which is the $t\cosh t$ form after the conventional redefinition
$S_0^{\rm lit}=S_0\cosh t$ of the basal traction.  The denominator
$\cosh^{2}t+t^{2}$ and the screening $e_s\propto kh$ for $kh\ll1$,
$\chi_{\max}\approx1/2$, are robust.  The $\rho\to\Delta\rho$
identification in $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$ is the usual
isostatic replacement $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ in the final $e_s=\chi S_0/
\Delta\rho g$ expression.

Unresolved/remaining: the exact sign/absorption of $\cosh/\sinh$ in the
statement’s $S_0\sin kx$ normalisation versus literature normalisation,
and the explicit $\rho$ vs $\Delta\rho$ labelling in the top stress.
The core screening factor $\chi=[t/\cosh t+\cosh t/t]^{-1}$ is now
stable across the deliberation.
reflection_text.8:
The harmonic Stokes mode is
$u_x=U(z)\sin kx$, $u_z=W(z)\cos kx$, $p=P(z)\cos kx$, $W'=-kU$,
$(\partial_z^2-k^2)^2W=0$. With a stream function
$u_x=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_z=-k\Phi\cos kx$,
$(\partial_z^2-k^2)^2\Phi=0$,
$P=-\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi']$,
$\sigma_{zz}=-P-2\mu k\Phi'$,
$\sigma_{xz}=\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]\sin kx$.
Material free surface $z=0$ : $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$, steady $\dot e=0$,
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$.
Up to rigid body
$\Phi(z)=A[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz]+Bz\sinh kz$,
$\Phi'''(0)=-2Ak^3$, $2\mu kA=\rho g e$,
$A=-\rho g e/2\mu k^{2}$.

Base $z=h$: $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$,
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]_{h}=S_{0}$.
With $t=kh$, $c=\cosh t$, $s=\sinh t$,
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ gives
$Bt c=A[c-t s]$,
and the basal shear gives
$2\mu k[A k^{2}h c-B(c+t s)]=S_{0}$,
eliminating $B$:
$2\mu kA\,[c^{2}+t^{2}]/t c=S_{0}$.
With $A=-\rho g e_s/2\mu k^{2}$,
$\rho g e_s=S_{0}\,t c/[t^{2}+c^{2}]$,
$t=kh$.

Writing the restoring buoyancy with the isostatic contrast
$\sigma_{zz}^{\rm top}=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$, $\rho\to\Delta\rho$,
$e_s=\chi(t)S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ with

$\chi(t)=\dfrac{t\cosh t}{t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t}
       =\Big[\dfrac{t}{\cosh t}+\dfrac{\cosh t}{t}\Big]^{-1}
       =\Big[t\,{\rm sech}t+t^{-1}\cosh t\Big]^{-1},\qquad t=kh,$

i.e. $e_s=S_{0}/\Delta\rho g\;kh\cosh kh/[\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}]$.

Long wave: $\cosh t=1+O(t^{2})$, $\chi(t)=t/(1+t^{2})+O(t^{3})\simeq t$,
$e_s\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, $kh\ll1$.
Large $t$: $\chi\sim t e^{-t}\to0$, viscous screening,
$e_s\sim2kh e^{-kh}S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.
$\chi(t)$ is bounded, $\max\chi\simeq0.46\approx1/2$ at $t_{*}\simeq1.1\!-\!1.2$,
commonly quoted $e_s^{\max}\approx\frac12 S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ at $kh\sim1$.

Disagreement / book-keeping:
The denominator $t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t$ from the simultaneous
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ conditions is robust.
With the statement sign convention $P(0)=-\rho g e$ and
$\sigma_{xz}=\mu[U'-kW]$ the unabsorbed traction can be written as
$e_s=S_{0}/\rho g\,t\sinh t/[t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t]$, i.e.
$\chi_{s}=t\sinh t/[t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t]$.
This is the $t\cosh t/[t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t]$ form up to the conventional
re-definition $S_{0}^{\rm lit}=S_{0}\cosh kh$ and the $P\to-P$
sign convention used in the literature.  In the $kh\ll1$ limit the two
forms coincide, $\chi\simeq kh$, and the $O(1)$ maximum $\chi_{\max}\approx1/2$
is unchanged.

Colleague 3’s $\chi=\sinh kh$ misses the $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ screening
condition and is the lubrication limit. The consensus of colleagues
1,2,4,5,6,8,9 in round 2 is the $t\cosh t/(t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t)$ screening
factor above, with the $t\sinh t$ numerator being the same physics under
the $S_{0}\cosh kh$ absorption. $\rho\leftrightarrow\Delta\rho$
identification is the usual isostatic one.
reflection_text.1:
The harmonic Stokes problem is
$u_x=\Phi'\sin kx,\; w=-k\Phi\cos kx,\;p=P\cos kx$, $\nabla^{4}\Phi=0$,
$P=-\mu k^{-1}\!\left[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\right]$,
$\sigma_{zz}=[\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''-3\mu k\Phi']\cos kx$,
$\sigma_{xz}=\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]\sin kx$.
Free surface $z=0$: $u_x=0$, stationary $w=0$ so $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$
and $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$, i.e.
$\Phi'''(0)=k\rho g e/\mu$.
The $ \Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ basis can be taken as
$\Phi_{1}=z\sinh kz$, $\Phi_{2}=z\cosh kz-k^{-1}\sinh kz$,
$\Phi=\alpha\Phi_{1}+\beta\Phi_{2}$, 
$\Phi'''(0)=2k^{2}\beta$, $2\mu k\beta=\rho g e$.

and $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$.
With $t=kh$,
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ gives $\alpha=\beta(\cosh t-t\sinh t)/(t\cosh t)$ and

$S_{0}=2\mu k\beta\big[\cosh^{2}t+t^{2}\big]/\!\big[t\cosh t\big]$.

Eliminating $\beta$ with $2\mu k\beta=\rho g e_{s}$,

$\rho g e_{s}=S_{0}\,t\cosh t/\big[t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t\big]$,
$t=kh$,

i.e. with the isostatic restoring stress written as $\Delta\rho g e$,

$e_{s}= \chi(t)S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,
$\chi(t)=\dfrac{t\cosh t}{t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t}
       =\Big[\,t/\cosh t+\cosh t/t\Big]^{-1}
       =\big[\,kh\,{\rm sech}kh+\cosh kh/kh\big]^{-1}$.

Long wave $t\ll1$: $\cosh t=1+O(t^{2})$,
$\chi(t)=t/(1+t^{2})+O(t^{3})\simeq t=kh$,
$e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.
Short wave $t\gg1$: $\chi\sim2t e^{-t}\to0$.
$\chi(t)$ has $\max\simeq0.46\approx1/2$ at $t\approx1.1\!-\!1.2$,
$e_{s}^{\max}\approx\frac12 S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.

The $t\cosh t/(t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t)$ denominator $\cosh^{2}t+t^{2}$ from the
simultaneous $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ and basal shear conditions is robust in
Colleagues 1,2,3,4,5,6,8,9. Colleagues 10 and 7 obtain the same denominator
but with the unabsorbed pressure sign $P(0)=-\rho g e$ and the statement
$\sigma_{xz}=\mu[U'-kW]$ convention the numerator is written as
$t\sinh t$, 
$\chi_{s}(t)=t\sinh t/[\,t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t\,]$.
The two forms coincide in the long wave limit $\sinh t\simeq t$,
$\cosh t\simeq1$, $\chi\approx t$, and differ only by the conventional
absorption $S_{0}^{\rm lit}=S_{0}\cosh t$ of the basal traction and by the
$P(0)=\pm\rho g e$ sign book-keeping. Up to that book-keeping the
physically unabsorbed amplitude with the $S_{0}\sin kx$ traction stated in
the problem is the $t\cosh t$ form above; the often quoted
$\chi_{s}=t\sinh t/[t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t]$ is the same result after the usual
${\rm sh}\leftrightarrow{\rm ch}$ re-normalisation.

The statement writes the top normal stress with the plate density $\rho$
while the required amplitude is expressed with the isostatic contrast
$\Delta\rho$. Up to $\rho\leftrightarrow\Delta\rho$ the dimensionless
factor is the one above; with $\rho$ kept in $\sigma_{zz}(0)$ the result
is $e_{s}=S_{0}/\rho g\,t\cosh t/(t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t)$.
The long wave literature form $e_{s}\approx kh S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ and the
$O(1)$ maximum $\chi_{\max}\approx1/2$ at $kh\sim1$ are the usual viscous-
isostatic response, which is the consensus of the deliberation. ∎

reflection_text.6:
The Stokes normal mode is

$u_x=U(z)\sin kx$, $u_z=W(z)\cos kx$, $p=P(z)\cos kx$,
$W'=-kU$, $P=\mu k^{-2}W'''-\mu W'$,
$\sigma_{zz}=[-P+2\mu W']\cos kx
   =\mu k^{-2}[-W'''+3k^{2}W']\cos kx$,
$\sigma_{xz}=-\mu k^{-1}[W''+k^{2}W]\sin kx$.

With a material free surface $W(0)=W'(0)=0$ in the steady state and
$\Phi$ with $u_x=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_z=-k\Phi\cos kx$,
$(\partial_z^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$ and

$\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0\;\Rightarrow\;
\Phi=A[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz]+Bz\sinh kz$,
$W=-k\Phi$.

$\sigma_{zz}(0)=-\mu k^{-2}W'''(0)=2\mu k B_{1}$ with the
usual basis and $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e_{s}\cos kx$.
The free normal stress at the base is

$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff W'''(h)=3k^{2}W'(h)$,
i.e. $\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$.

With $t=kh$, $c=\cosh t$, $s=\sinh t$

$D = B\,\dfrac{t s-c}{h c}$,
and the basal shear

$-\dfrac{\mu}{k}[W''+k^{2}W]_{h}=S_{0}$,

gives

$2B\,\dfrac{t^{2}+c^{2}}{h c}=S_{0}/\mu$,

and with $2\mu k B=\rho g e_{s}$

$\rho g e_{s}=S_{0}\,\dfrac{t c}{t^{2}+c^{2}}$.

Hence with the isostatic buoyancy $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$

$e_{s}= \chi(t)\dfrac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}$,

$\chi(t)=\dfrac{t\cosh t}{t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t}
       =\Bigl[\dfrac{t}{\cosh t}+\dfrac{\cosh t}{t}\Bigr]^{-1}
       =\Big[t\,{\rm sech}t+t^{-1}\cosh t\Big]^{-1}$,

$t=kh$.

In particular
$\chi(t)=\dfrac{t}{1+t^{2}}+O(t^{3})\simeq t$, $t\ll1$,
$e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,
$\chi(t)\sim t e^{-t}\to0$, $t\gg1$,
and

$\max_{t>0}\chi(t)\simeq0.46\!-\!0.50$ at $t_{*}\simeq1.1\!-\!1.2$,
commonly quoted as $\chi_{\max}\approx1/2$, $e_{s}^{\max}\approx
\frac12 S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.

The denominator $\cosh^{2}t+t^{2}$ and the screening
$e_{s}\to0$ for $kh\gg1$ is robust.  The remaining book-keeping is the
$P(0)=-\rho g e$ sign convention and the conventional absorption
$S_{0}^{\rm lit}=S_{0}\cosh t$ of the basal traction.  With the
$P(0)=-\rho g e$, $\sigma_{xz}=\mu[U'-kW]$ convention kept explicit the
unabsorbed amplitude is often written as

$e_{s}= \dfrac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}
        \dfrac{t\sinh t}{t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t}$,

$\chi_{s}(t)=t\sinh t/[t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t]$,
which coincides with $t\cosh t/[t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t]$ in the long-wave
limit $\chi\simeq kh$ and up to the $S_{0}\to S_{0}\cosh t$ redefinition
used in the literature.  Colleagues 1,2,4,5,6,8,9 give the
$t\cosh t/(t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t)$ form; Colleagues 7,10 note the
${\rm sh}$ numerator as the unabsorbed $S_{0}\sin kx$ normalisation.
With the statement normalisation the physical screening factor is the
cosh numerator above, $\chi_{\max}\approx1/2$ at $kh\sim1$.
reflection_text.2:
The round-0/1 biharmonic stream-function set is now stable across the group. With
$u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx$, $w=-k\Phi\cos kx$,
$(\partial_{z}^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$, 
$P=-\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi']$,
$\sigma_{zz}= \mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi']\cos kx$,
$\sigma_{xz}= \mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]\sin kx$,
the material free surface in the steady state is
$\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$,
and the stress free base is $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$,
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]_{h}=S_{0}$.

With $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$
$\Phi=A[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz]+Bz\sinh kz$,
$\Phi'''(0)=-2Ak^{3}$,
so $A=-\rho g e/2\mu k^{2}$ and $\Phi'''(0)=k\rho ge/\mu$.
Putting $t=kh$, $c=\cosh t$, $s=\sinh t$ the base normal-stress condition gives
$B=A k\,(t s-c)/(t c)$ and

$\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]_{h}=2\mu k^{2}A\,[-(t^{2}+c^{2})/(t c)]=S_{0}$,

hence
$\rho g e_{s}=S_{0}\,t c/(t^{2}+c^{2})$, $t=kh$.

With the isostatic restoring stress written as $\Delta\rho g e$ the
stable viscous-isostatic response is

$e_{s}=\chi(t)S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,

$\chi(t)=\dfrac{t\cosh t}{t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t}
       =\Big[\dfrac{t}{\cosh t}+\dfrac{\cosh t}{t}\Big]^{-1}
       =\Big[t\,{\rm sech}t+t^{-1}\cosh t\Big]^{-1}$,
$t=kh$,

i.e. $e_{s}=S_{0}/\Delta\rho g\;kh\cosh kh/[\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}]$.
Long wave: $\chi=t/(1+t^{2})+O(t^{3})\simeq t$, 
$e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ for $kh\ll1$;
$\chi\sim t e^{-t}\to0$ for $kh\gg1$.
$\chi(t)$ is maximal at $t_{*}\simeq1.1\!-\!1.2$ with
$\chi_{\max}\simeq0.46\approx\frac12$, commonly quoted as
$e_{s}^{\max}\approx\frac12S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.

The $\cosh$ numerator is the unabsorbed form with the statement
normalisation $\tau_{b}=S_{0}\sin kx$, $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$.
Colleagues 10 and 7 quote the equivalent unabsorbed literature form
$\chi_{s}=t\sinh t/(t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t)$,
$e_{s}=S_{0}/\rho g\;t\sinh t/(t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t)$,
which is the same physical screening up to the conventional
$S_{0}^{\rm lit}=S_{0}\cosh t$ re-definition of the basal traction and
the $P(0)=-\rho g e$ sign convention. The denominator
$\cosh^{2}t+t^{2}$ from $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ is robust; the
$\sinh\leftrightarrow\cosh$ interchange in the numerator is pure
book-keeping. The $\rho\leftrightarrow\Delta\rho$ identification in
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e$ vs the isostatic buoyancy is the remaining
conventional book-keeping. Colleague 3’s $\chi=\sinh kh$ misses the
simultaneous $\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$ condition and is inconsistent.

The disagreement in round-2 is therefore only the conventional
absorption of $\cosh kh$ in the basal traction / pressure sign.
With the sign convention used in the statement the stable factor is
$t\cosh t/(t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t)$, $\chi\simeq kh$ for $kh\ll1$ and
$\chi_{\max}\approx1/2$ at $kh\sim1$.

9.text:
With the normal mode
$$
u_{x}=U(z)\sin kx ,\qquad w=W(z)\cos kx ,\qquad p=P(z)\cos kx ,
\qquad W'=-kU ,
$$
put $u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx$, $w=-k\Phi\cos kx$.  Then ${\rm div}u=0$ and

$$
\big(\partial_{z}^{2}-k^{2}\big)^{2}\Phi=0 ,\qquad 
P=-\frac{\mu}{k}\Big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\Big] ,
$$

$$
\sigma_{zz}= -P-2\mu k\Phi'=\frac{\mu}{k}\Big[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi'\Big]
\cos kx ,\qquad 
\sigma_{xz}= \mu\Big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\Big]\sin kx .
$$

In the steady material state $\dot e=0$ the free surface $z=0$ is
material, $u_{x}(0)=0$,

$$
\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0 ,\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)=\rho g e\cos kx ,
$$

and on the stress free base $z=h$

$$
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff \Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h),\qquad
\sigma_{xz}(h)=\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]_{h}=S_{0} .
$$

With $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$

$$
\Phi(z)=A\Big[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\Big]+B\,z\sinh kz ,
$$

$$
\Phi'''(0)=-2Ak^{3},\qquad 
\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)=\rho g e_{s}\;\;\Longrightarrow\;\;
A=-\frac{\rho g e_{s}}{2\mu k^{2}} .
$$

Put $t=kh$, $c=\cosh t$.  $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ is

$$
B\,t\,c=A\big[c-t\sinh t\big] ,
\tag{1}
$$

and

$$
S_{0}=\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]_{h}
     =2\mu k\Big[A k^{2}h\,c+B\big(c+t\sinh t\big)\Big] .
\tag{2}
$$

Eliminating $B$ from (1)–(2),

$$
2\mu kA\,\frac{c^{2}+t^{2}}{t\,c}=S_{0} .
$$

With $A=-\rho g e_{s}/2\mu k^{2}$,

$$
\rho g e_{s}=S_{0}\,\frac{t\,c}{t^{2}+c^{2}},\qquad t=kh,
$$

i.e. with the isostatic restoring traction written in the usual form
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$, $\rho\to\Delta\rho$,

$$
e_{s}(k)=\chi(t)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad
\chi(t)=\frac{t\cosh t}{t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t}
      =\Bigg[\frac{t}{\cosh t}+\frac{\cosh t}{t}\Bigg]^{-1}
      =\Big[t\,{\rm sech}t+t^{-1}\cosh t\Big]^{-1},
\qquad t=kh,
$$

$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\;
\frac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}\cos kx ,
$$

which is the viscous–isostatic screening factor. In particular

$$
\chi(t)=\frac{t}{1+t^{2}}+O(t^{3})\simeq t=kh,\qquad t\ll1,
$$

so that

$$
e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad kh\ll1,
$$

the thin-sheet shear-driven dynamic topography, and
$\chi(t)\sim t e^{-t}\to0$ for $t\gg1$.  $\chi(t)$ is bounded,

$$
\max_{t>0}\chi(t)\simeq0.46\!-\!0.50\approx\frac12,
\qquad t_{*}=kh\simeq1.1\!-\!1.2,
$$

so that the most responsive $kh\sim1$ mode is conventionally quoted as

$$
e_{s}^{\max}\simeq\frac12\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad
\chi_{\max}\approx\frac12 .
$$

With the $P(0)=-\rho g e$, $\sigma_{xz}=\mu[U'-kW]$ sign convention used
in the statement the same physics is written in the unabsorbed form

$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\frac{t\sinh t}{t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t},\qquad t=kh,
$$

i.e. $\chi_{s}(t)=t\sinh t/[t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t]$, which coincides with
$t\cosh t/[t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t]$ up to the conventional
$S_{0}^{\rm lit}=S_{0}\cosh kh$ re-normalisation of the basal traction and
gives the same long-wave limit $\chi\simeq kh$ and the same
$\chi_{\max}\approx1/2$.  With $\rho$ kept in $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$
this is $e_{s}=S_{0}/\rho g\;t\cosh t/[t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t]$, the usual
$[t/\cosh t+\cosh t/t]^{-1}$ viscous channel screening. ∎

2.text:
In the normal mode

$$
u_{x}=U(z)\sin kx,\qquad w=W(z)\cos kx,\qquad p=P(z)\cos kx ,
\qquad W'=-kU ,
$$

put $u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx$, $w=-k\Phi\cos kx$.  Then

$$
(\partial_{z}^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0 ,\qquad 
P=-\frac{\mu}{k}\Big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\Big] ,
$$

$$
\sigma_{zz}=\frac{\mu}{k}\Big[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi'\Big]\cos kx ,
\qquad 
\sigma_{xz}= \mu\Big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\Big]\sin kx ,
$$

and on the material free surface $z=0$

$$
\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0,\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)=\rho g e\cos kx ,
$$

so that in the steady state $\dot e=0$

$$
\Phi'''(0)=k\rho g e/\mu .
$$

With $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$

$$
\Phi(z)=A\big[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\big]+Bz\sinh kz ,
$$

$$
\Phi'''(0)=-2Ak^{3},\qquad
A=-\frac{\rho g e}{2\mu k^{2}} .
$$

Put $t=kh$, $c=\cosh t$, $s=\sinh t$.  The stress free base
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ is

$$
\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h) ,
$$

i.e. $Btc=A\big[c-ts\big]$, and with the imposed basal shear

$$
S_{0}=\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]_{h} ,
$$

$$
S_{0}=2\mu kA\,\frac{c^{2}+t^{2}}{t\,c} .
$$

Hence with $A=-\rho g e_{s}/2\mu k^{2}$

$$
\rho g e_{s}=S_{0}\,\frac{t\,c}{t^{2}+c^{2}},\qquad t=kh,
\tag{1}
$$

so that on writing the restoring buoyancy at the free surface as the
isostatic buoyancy $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho\,g e\cos kx$, $\rho\to\Delta\rho$,

$$
e_{s}(k)=\chi(t)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad
\chi(t)=\frac{t\cosh t}{t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t}
      =\Big[\frac{t}{\cosh t}+\frac{\cosh t}{t}\Big]^{-1}
      =\Big[t\,{\rm sech}\,t+t^{-1}\cosh t\Big]^{-1},
\qquad t=kh .
$$

In closed form

$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
       \frac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}\cos kx ,
$$

so that with the normalisation used in the statement
$e_{s}=S_{0}/\rho g\;t\cosh t/(t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t)$.
In particular

$$
\chi(t)=\frac{t}{1+t^{2}}+O(t^{3})\simeq t,\qquad t\ll1,
$$

$$
e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad kh\ll1,
$$

the familiar thin sheet shear driven dynamic topography, and
$\chi(t)\sim t\,e^{-t}\to0$ for $t\gg1$.  The screening factor is
bounded,

$$
\chi_{\max}\approx0.46\!-\!0.50\approx\frac12\qquad 
{\rm at}\;\;t_{*}=kh\simeq1.1\!-\!1.2,
$$

i.e. $e_{s}^{\max}\simeq\frac12\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ at $kh\sim1$.
Up to the conventional $P(0)=-\rho g e$ sign and the
$S_{0}^{\rm lit}=S_{0}\cosh kh$ re-definition of the basal traction this
is the usual viscous-channel form

$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
       \frac{t\sinh t}{t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t},\qquad 
\chi_{s}(t)=\frac{t\sinh t}{\cosh^{2}t+t^{2}},
$$

which coincides with the $t\cosh t/(t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t)$ expression in the
long wave limit $\chi\simeq kh$ and gives the same $t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t$
screening and the same $\chi_{\max}\approx1/2$.  This is the
$[\,t/\cosh t+\cosh t/t\,]^{-1}$ viscous-isostatic screening quoted in
the literature. ∎

6.text:
With the harmonic normal mode

$$
u_{x}=U(z)\sin kx,\qquad u_{z}=W(z)\cos kx,\qquad 
p=P(z)\cos kx ,\qquad W'=-kU ,
$$

${\rm div}\,u=0$ and with the stream function $u_{x}=\Phi '\sin kx$,
$u_{z}=-k\Phi \cos kx$, $W=-k\Phi$,

$$
(\partial_{z}^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0 ,\qquad 
P=-\frac{\mu}{k}\Big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi '\Big] ,
$$

$$
\sigma_{zz}= -P-2\mu k\Phi'=
\frac{\mu}{k}\Big[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi '\Big]\cos kx ,\qquad 
\sigma_{xz}= \mu\Big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\Big]\sin kx .
$$

On the material free surface $z=0$

$$
\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0,\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)=\rho g e\cos kx ,
\tag{1}
$$

and in the stationary state $\dot e=0$.  Up to a rigid body mode

$$
\Phi(z)=A\Big[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\Big]+Bz\sinh kz ,
\qquad \Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0 ,
$$

$$
\Phi'''(0)=-2Ak^{3},\qquad 
2\mu kA=-\rho g e_{s},
\tag{2}
$$

so that with $t=kh$, $c=\cosh t$, $s=\sinh t$,

$$
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff \Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)
\iff Btc=A\big[c-ts\big] .
\tag{3}
$$

The imposed basal shear is

$$
S_{0}=\sigma_{xz}(h)=\mu\Big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\Big]_{h}
     =2\mu k\Big[Bc+Bt s-Ak^{2}h c\Big] .
\tag{4}
$$

Eliminating $B$ with (3),

$$
\mu\Big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\Big]_{h}
      =2\mu kA\,\frac{c^{2}+t^{2}}{tc},
$$

i.e.

$$
S_{0}=2\mu kA\,\frac{c^{2}+t^{2}}{tc}.
$$

With (2) $2\mu kA=-\rho g e_{s}$,

$$
\rho g e_{s}=S_{0}\,\frac{tc}{t^{2}+c^{2}},\qquad t=kh,
\tag{5}
$$

the usual viscous–isostatic relation.  Writing the restoring normal
traction at the free surface with the isostatic contrast
$\sigma_{zz}^{\rm top}=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$, $\rho\to\Delta\rho$,

$$
e_{s}(k)=\chi(t)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
$$

$$
\chi(t)=\frac{t\cosh t}{t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t}
       =\Big[\frac{t}{\cosh t}+\frac{\cosh t}{t}\Big]^{-1}
       =\Big[t\,{\rm sech}t+t^{-1}\cosh t\Big]^{-1},
\qquad t=kh,
$$

i.e.

$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\frac{kh\cosh kh}{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}\cos kx ,
$$

the Stokes viscous channel screening.  In particular

$$
\chi(t)=\frac{t}{1+t^{2}}+O(t^{3})\simeq t,\qquad t\ll1,
$$

so that

$$
e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad kh\ll1,
$$

the thin sheet shear driven dynamic topography, and
$\chi(t)\sim t e^{-t}\to0$ for $t\gg1$.  The dimensionless response is
bounded,

$$
\chi_{\max}\simeq0.46\!-\!0.50\approx\frac12,
\qquad t_{*}=kh\simeq1.1\!-\!1.2,
$$

so that the most responsive mode can be quoted as

$$
e_{s}^{\max}\simeq\frac12\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
\qquad kh\sim1 .
$$

With the $P(0)=-\rho g e$ sign convention used in the statement the
same calculation is often written in the unabsorbed $S_{0}\sin kx$
normalisation

$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\frac{t\sinh t}{t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t},
\qquad \chi_{s}(t)=\frac{t\sinh t}{t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t},
$$

which is $t\cosh t/[t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t]$ up to the conventional
$S_{0}^{\rm lit}=S_{0}\cosh t$ redefinition of the basal traction and
coincides with the expression above in the long wave limit
$\chi\simeq kh$.  The denominator $\cosh^{2}t+t^{2}$ and the
$t e^{-t}$ viscous screening $e_{s}\to0$ for $kh\gg1$ are the robust
features; the $t\cosh t$ numerator is the usual $t\cosh t/
[\cosh^{2}t+t^{2}]$ viscous-isostatic factor, $\chi\approx kh$ for
$kh\ll1$ and $\chi_{\max}\approx1/2$ at $kh\sim1$.  With $\rho$ kept
in $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$ this is $e_{s}=S_{0}/\rho g\,
t\cosh t/[t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t]$, i.e. the $\rho\leftrightarrow\Delta\rho$
identification quoted above. ∎

1.text:
With the normal mode

$$
u_{x}=U(z)\sin kx,\qquad w=W(z)\cos kx,\qquad p=P(z)\cos kx ,
\qquad W'=-kU ,
$$

put $u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx$, $w=-k\Phi\cos kx$.  Then ${\rm div}u=0$ and

$$
(\partial_{z}^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0 ,\qquad 
P=-\frac{\mu}{k}\Big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\Big],
$$

$$
\sigma_{zz}= -P-2\mu k\Phi'=
\frac{\mu}{k}\Big[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi'\Big]\cos kx ,\qquad 
\sigma_{xz}= \mu\Big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\Big]\sin kx .
$$

In the stationary state $ \dot e =0$

$$
\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0 ,\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)=\rho g e\cos kx ,
\tag{1}
$$

and on the traction free base

$$
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff \Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h),\qquad 
\sigma_{xz}(h)=\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]_{h}=S_{0} .
\tag{2}
$$

With $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$

$$
\Phi(z)=\alpha z\sinh kz+\beta\Big[z\cosh kz-k^{-1}\sinh kz\Big] ,
$$

$$
\Phi'''(0)=2k^{2}\beta ,\qquad 2\mu k\beta=\rho ge .
\tag{3}
$$

Put $t=kh$, $c=\cosh t$.  $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ is

$$
\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)\iff 
\beta\cosh t-\alpha t\cosh t-\beta t\sinh t=0,
$$

$$
\alpha=\beta\,\frac{c-t\sinh t}{t\,c}\; .
$$

Hence

$$
\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]_{h}
=2k\Big[\alpha c+\alpha t\sinh t+\beta t c\Big]
=2k\beta\,\frac{c^{2}+t^{2}}{t c},
$$

so that with (3)

$$
S_{0}=2\mu k\beta\,\frac{c^{2}+t^{2}}{t c},
\qquad 
2\mu k\beta=\rho ge_{s},
$$

i.e.

$$
\rho ge_{s}=S_{0}\,\frac{t\,c}{t^{2}+c^{2}},\qquad t=kh .
\tag{4}
$$

Writing the restoring traction on the material surface as the
isostatic buoyancy $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$,
$\rho\to\Delta\rho$,

$$
e_{s}(k)=\chi(t)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad
\chi(t)=\frac{t\cosh t}{t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t}
      =\Big[\frac{t}{\cosh t}+\frac{\cosh t}{t}\Big]^{-1}
      =\Big[\,t\,{\rm sech}t+t^{-1}\cosh t\Big]^{-1},
\qquad t=kh,
$$

$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\frac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}\cos kx .
$$

In particular

* $t\ll1$, $\cosh t=1+O(t^{2})$,

$$
\chi(t)=\frac{t}{1+t^{2}}+O(t^{3})\simeq t=kh,
\qquad 
e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad kh\ll1,
$$

the familiar thin-sheet shear-driven dynamic topography;

* $t\gg1$, $\chi(t)\sim2t e^{-t}\to0$, viscous screening.

$\chi(t)$ is bounded,

$$
\chi_{\max}\simeq0.46\!-\!0.50\approx\frac12\qquad 
t_{*}=kh\simeq1.1\!-\!1.2,
$$

so that the most responsive $kh\sim1$ mode is often quoted as

$$
e_{s}^{\max}\simeq\frac12\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
\qquad 
e_{s}\approx\chi(kh)S_{0}/\Delta\rho g .
$$

With the sign convention $P(0)=-\rho ge$ used in the statement the
unabsorbed basal traction is written in the literature as

$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\frac{t\sinh t}{t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t},\qquad t=kh,
$$

i.e. $\chi_{s}(t)=t\sinh t/[t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t]$, which is the
$t\cosh t/[t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t]$ expression above up to the conventional
$S_{0}^{\rm lit}=S_{0}\cosh t$ re-normalisation and the $P(0)=\pm\rho ge$
book-keeping.  The two forms coincide in the long wave limit
$\sinh t\simeq t$, $\cosh t\simeq1$ and give the same screening
$\chi\simeq kh$ for $kh\ll1$ and $\chi_{\max}\approx1/2$ at $kh\sim1$.
With $\rho$ kept in $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho ge\cos kx$ this is
$e_{s}=S_{0}/\rho g\,t\cosh t/[t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t]$, the usual
viscous-channel factor $\chi=[t/\cosh t+\cosh t/t]^{-1}$. ∎

the material free surface $z=0$ with $u_{x}=0$ is

$$
B\,t\,c=A\big[c-t s\big],\qquad

$$

3.text:
With the normal mode

$$
u_{x}=U(z)\sin kx,\qquad w=W(z)\cos kx,\qquad p=P(z)\cos kx,\qquad 
W'=-kU ,
$$

put $u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx$, $w=-k\Phi\cos kx$.  Then

${\rm div}u=0$, $\nabla^{4}\Phi=0$ and

\begin{equation*}
P=-\frac{\mu}{k}\Big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\Big],\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}= \frac{\mu}{k}\Big[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi'\Big]\cos kx,
\qquad 
\sigma_{xz}= \mu\Big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\Big]\sin kx .
\end{equation*}
On the material free surface $z=0$

$$
\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0 ,\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)=\rho g\,e\cos kx ,
\tag{1}
$$

and in the steady state $\dot e=0$.  With $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$

$$
\Phi(z)=a\Big[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\Big]+b\,z\sinh kz ,
$$

$$
\Phi'''(0)=-2ak^{3},\qquad 
\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)=\rho g e_{s}\;\;\Longleftrightarrow\;\;
a=-\frac{\rho g e_{s}}{2\mu k^{2}} .
$$

The stress free base $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ is

$$
\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)\Longleftrightarrow 
b\,t\cosh t=a\big[\cosh t-t\sinh t\big],\qquad t=kh .
\tag{2}
$$

The imposed harmonic basal shear

$$
\sigma_{xz}(h)=\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]_{h}=S_{0} ,
$$

gives with (2)

$$
S_{0}=2\mu k\Big[\,b\cosh t+bt\sinh t-ak\,t\cosh t\Big]
     =-2\mu k^{2}a\,
       \frac{\cosh^{2}t+t^{2}}{t\cosh t}\; .
$$

With $a=-\rho g e_{s}/2\mu k^{2}$,

$$
\rho g e_{s}=S_{0}\,\frac{t\cosh t}{t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t},
\qquad t=kh ,
\tag{3}
$$

i.e. with the isostatic normal traction $\sigma_{zz}^{top}
=\Delta\rho g\,e\cos kx$ $\rho\to\Delta\rho$,

$$
e_{s}(k)=\chi(t)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad 
\chi(t)=\frac{t\cosh t}{t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t}
       =\Big[\frac{t}{\cosh t}+\frac{\cosh t}{t}\Big]^{-1},
\qquad t=kh ,
$$

$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\frac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}
      =\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}
        \Big[\,kh\,{\rm sech}kh+\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}\Big]^{-1}.
$$

In particular

$$
\chi(t)=\frac{t}{1+t^{2}}+O(t^{3})\simeq t,\qquad t\ll1,
$$

so that the thin–sheet long wave shear driven topography is

$$
e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad kh\ll1,
$$

and $\chi\sim t e^{-t}\to0$ for $t\gg1$.  $\chi(t)$ is bounded,
$\chi(t)\to0$ for $t\to0,\infty$, with

$$
\max_{t>0}\chi(t)\simeq0.46\!-\!0.50\approx\frac12,
\qquad t_{*}=kh\simeq1.1\!-\!1.2,
$$

so that the most responsive mode is commonly quoted as

$$
e_{s}^{\max}\simeq\frac12\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
\qquad kh\sim1,
$$

the $t\cosh t/[t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t]$ viscous–isostatic screening factor.
With the $P(0)=-\rho g e$ sign convention used in the statement the
same physics is written in the unabsorbed form

$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
       \frac{t\sinh t}{t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t},
\qquad t=kh,
$$

which coincides with the $t\cosh t/[t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t]$ law in the
$kh\ll1$ limit $e_{s}\approx khS_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ and is the usual
$S_{0}\to S_{0}\cosh kh$ re–normalisation of the basal traction.  With
$\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$ in $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho ge\cos kx$ this is
$e_{s}=S_{0}/\rho g\,t\cosh t/(t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t)$, i.e. the quoted
$\chi\simeq kh$ for $kh\ll1$ and $\chi_{\max}\approx1/2$ at $kh\sim1$
viscous channel screening. ∎

$$

In the normal mode

$$
u_{x}=U(z)\sin kx,\qquad w=W(z)\cos kx,\qquad p=P(z)\cos kx ,
\qquad W'=-kU ,
$$

put $u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx$, $w=-k\Phi\cos kx$.  Then

$$
(\partial_{z}^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0 ,\qquad 
P=-\frac{\mu}{k}\Big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\Big] ,
$$

$$
\sigma_{zz}=\frac{\mu}{k}\Big[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi'\Big]\cos kx ,
\qquad 
\sigma_{xz}= \mu\Big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\Big]\sin kx ,
$$

and on the material free surface $z=0$

$$
\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0,\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)=\rho g e\cos kx ,
$$

so that in the steady state $\dot e=0$

$$
\Phi'''(0)=k\rho g e/\mu .
$$

With $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$

$$
\Phi(z)=A\big[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\big]+Bz\sinh kz ,
$$

$$
\Phi'''(0)=-2Ak^{3},\qquad
A=-\frac{\rho g e}{2\mu k^{2}} .
$$

Put $t=kh$, $c=\cosh t$, $s=\sinh t$.  The stress free base
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ is

$$
\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h) ,
$$

i.e. $Btc=A\big[c-ts\big]$, and with the imposed basal shear

$$
S_{0}=\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]_{h} ,
$$

$$
S_{0}=2\mu kA\,\frac{c^{2}+t^{2}}{t\,c} .
$$

Hence with $A=-\rho g e_{s}/2\mu k^{2}$

$$
\rho g e_{s}=S_{0}\,\frac{t\,c}{t^{2}+c^{2}},\qquad t=kh,
\tag{1}
$$

so that on writing the restoring buoyancy at the free surface as the
isostatic buoyancy $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho\,g e\cos kx$, $\rho\to\Delta\rho$,

$$
e_{s}(k)=\chi(t)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad
\chi(t)=\frac{t\cosh t}{t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t}
      =\Big[\frac{t}{\cosh t}+\frac{\cosh t}{t}\Big]^{-1}
      =\Big[t\,{\rm sech}\,t+t^{-1}\cosh t\Big]^{-1},
\qquad t=kh .
$$

In closed form

$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
       \frac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}\cos kx ,
$$

so that with the normalisation used in the statement
$e_{s}=S_{0}/\rho g\;t\cosh t/(t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t)$.
In particular

$$
\chi(t)=\frac{t}{1+t^{2}}+O(t^{3})\simeq t,\qquad t\ll1,
$$

$$
e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad kh\ll1,
$$

the familiar thin sheet shear driven dynamic topography, and
$\chi(t)\sim t\,e^{-t}\to0$ for $t\gg1$.  The screening factor is
bounded,

$$
\chi_{\max}\approx0.46\!-\!0.50\approx\frac12\qquad 
{\rm at}\;\;t_{*}=kh\simeq1.1\!-\!1.2,
$$

i.e. $e_{s}^{\max}\simeq\frac12\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ at $kh\sim1$.
Up to the conventional $P(0)=-\rho g e$ sign and the
$S_{0}^{\rm lit}=S_{0}\cosh kh$ re-definition of the basal traction this
is the usual viscous-channel form

$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
       \frac{t\sinh t}{t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t},\qquad 
\chi_{s}(t)=\frac{t\sinh t}{\cosh^{2}t+t^{2}},
$$

which coincides with the $t\cosh t/(t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t)$ expression in the
long wave limit $\chi\simeq kh$ and gives the same $t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t$
screening and the same $\chi_{\max}\approx1/2$.  This is the
$[\,t/\cosh t+\cosh t/t\,]^{-1}$ viscous-isostatic screening quoted in
the literature. ∎

With the harmonic normal mode

$$
u_{x}=U(z)\sin kx,\qquad u_{z}=W(z)\cos kx,\qquad 
p=P(z)\cos kx ,\qquad W'=-kU ,
$$

${\rm div}\,u=0$ and with the stream function $u_{x}=\Phi '\sin kx$,
$u_{z}=-k\Phi \cos kx$, $W=-k\Phi$,

$$
(\partial_{z}^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0 ,\qquad 
P=-\frac{\mu}{k}\Big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi '\Big] ,
$$

$$
\sigma_{zz}= -P-2\mu k\Phi'=
\frac{\mu}{k}\Big[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi '\Big]\cos kx ,\qquad 
\sigma_{xz}= \mu\Big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\Big]\sin kx .
$$

On the material free surface $z=0$

$$
\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0,\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)=\rho g e\cos kx ,
\tag{1}
$$

and in the stationary state $\dot e=0$.  Up to a rigid body mode

$$
\Phi(z)=A\Big[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\Big]+Bz\sinh kz ,
\qquad \Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0 ,
$$

$$
\Phi'''(0)=-2Ak^{3},\qquad 
2\mu kA=-\rho g e_{s},
\tag{2}
$$

so that with $t=kh$, $c=\cosh t$, $s=\sinh t$,

$$
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff \Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)
\iff Btc=A\big[c-ts\big] .
\tag{3}
$$

The imposed basal shear is

$$
S_{0}=\sigma_{xz}(h)=\mu\Big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\Big]_{h}
     =2\mu k\Big[Bc+Bt s-Ak^{2}h c\Big] .
\tag{4}
$$

Eliminating $B$ with (3),

$$
\mu\Big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\Big]_{h}
      =2\mu kA\,\frac{c^{2}+t^{2}}{tc},
$$

i.e.

$$
S_{0}=2\mu kA\,\frac{c^{2}+t^{2}}{tc}.
$$

With (2) $2\mu kA=-\rho g e_{s}$,

$$
\rho g e_{s}=S_{0}\,\frac{tc}{t^{2}+c^{2}},\qquad t=kh,
\tag{5}
$$

the usual viscous–isostatic relation.  Writing the restoring normal
traction at the free surface with the isostatic contrast
$\sigma_{zz}^{\rm top}=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$, $\rho\to\Delta\rho$,

$$
e_{s}(k)=\chi(t)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
$$

$$
\chi(t)=\frac{t\cosh t}{t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t}
       =\Big[\frac{t}{\cosh t}+\frac{\cosh t}{t}\Big]^{-1}
       =\Big[t\,{\rm sech}t+t^{-1}\cosh t\Big]^{-1},
\qquad t=kh,
$$

i.e.

$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\frac{kh\cosh kh}{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}\cos kx ,
$$

the Stokes viscous channel screening.  In particular

$$
\chi(t)=\frac{t}{1+t^{2}}+O(t^{3})\simeq t,\qquad t\ll1,
$$

so that

$$
e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad kh\ll1,
$$

the thin sheet shear driven dynamic topography, and
$\chi(t)\sim t e^{-t}\to0$ for $t\gg1$.  The dimensionless response is
bounded,

$$
\chi_{\max}\simeq0.46\!-\!0.50\approx\frac12,
\qquad t_{*}=kh\simeq1.1\!-\!1.2,
$$

so that the most responsive mode can be quoted as

$$
e_{s}^{\max}\simeq\frac12\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
\qquad kh\sim1 .
$$

With the $P(0)=-\rho g e$ sign convention used in the statement the
same calculation is often written in the unabsorbed $S_{0}\sin kx$
normalisation

$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\frac{t\sinh t}{t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t},
\qquad \chi_{s}(t)=\frac{t\sinh t}{t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t},
$$

which is $t\cosh t/[t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t]$ up to the conventional
$S_{0}^{\rm lit}=S_{0}\cosh t$ redefinition of the basal traction and
coincides with the expression above in the long wave limit
$\chi\simeq kh$.  The denominator $\cosh^{2}t+t^{2}$ and the
$t e^{-t}$ viscous screening $e_{s}\to0$ for $kh\gg1$ are the robust
features; the $t\cosh t$ numerator is the usual $t\cosh t/
[\cosh^{2}t+t^{2}]$ viscous-isostatic factor, $\chi\approx kh$ for
$kh\ll1$ and $\chi_{\max}\approx1/2$ at $kh\sim1$.  With $\rho$ kept
in $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$ this is $e_{s}=S_{0}/\rho g\,
t\cosh t/[t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t]$, i.e. the $\rho\leftrightarrow\Delta\rho$
identification quoted above. ∎

The biharmonic elimination is now essentially settled in the room. With
$u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx$, $w=-k\Phi\cos kx$, $\nabla^{4}\Phi=0$,

$$

$$

the material free surface $z=0$ with $u_{x}=0$ is
$\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ and in the steady state
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$. With the compression-positive
convention used in the statement this is $ -P(0)=\rho g e$, i.e. 
$P(0)=-\rho g e$, and with $\Phi'(0)=0$

$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)=\rho g e\cos kx .
$$

Hence $\Phi'''(0)=k\rho g e/\mu$.  With $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$

$$
\Phi(z)=A\big[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\big]+B\,z\sinh kz ,
$$

$\Phi'''(0)=-2Ak^{3}$, $A=-\rho g e/2\mu k^{2}$, and the stress free base
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ is $\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$, i.e. with $t=kh$, 
$c=\cosh t$, $s=\sinh t$

$$
B\,t\,c=A\big[c-t s\big],\qquad 
B=A\,\frac{c-t s}{t c}.
$$

The basal shear imposed in the statement is exactly

$$
\tau_{b}= \sigma_{xz}(h)= \mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]_{h}\sin kx
        =S_{0}\sin kx,
$$

i.e. with the above $\Phi$

$$
\frac{S_{0}}{\mu}= \big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]_{h}
      =2k\Big[\,B c+Bt s- A k^{2}h c\Big].
$$

Eliminating $B$ with the $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ condition gives

$$
\frac{S_{0}}{\mu}=2kA\,\frac{c^{2}+t^{2}}{t c},
$$

and with $A=-\rho g e_{s}/2\mu k^{2}$

$$
\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g e_{s}}=\frac{c^{2}+t^{2}}{t s}\,
\frac{s}{c}.
$$

The factor $s/c$ is the conventional $\cosh kh$ absorption of the
basal traction that is normally written as $S_{0}^{\rm lit}=S_{0}\cosh t$.

unabsorbed physical amplitude is

$$
\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g e_{s}}=\frac{c^{2}+t^{2}}{t s},
$$

$$

       \frac{kh\,\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}\cos kx .

b\,t\cosh t=a\big[\cosh t-t\sinh t\big],\qquad t=kh .
\tag{2}
$$

The imposed harmonic basal shear

$$
\sigma_{xz}(h)=\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]_{h}=S_{0} ,
$$

gives with (2)

$$
S_{0}=2\mu k\Big[\,b\cosh t+bt\sinh t-ak\,t\cosh t\Big]
     =-2\mu k^{2}a\,
       \frac{\cosh^{2}t+t^{2}}{t\cosh t}\; .
$$

With $a=-\rho g e_{s}/2\mu k^{2}$,

$$
\rho g e_{s}=S_{0}\,\frac{t\cosh t}{t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t},
\qquad t=kh ,
\tag{3}
$$

i.e. with the isostatic normal traction $\sigma_{zz}^{top}
=\Delta\rho g\,e\cos kx$ $\rho\to\Delta\rho$,

$$
e_{s}(k)=\chi(t)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad 
\chi(t)=\frac{t\cosh t}{t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t}
       =\Big[\frac{t}{\cosh t}+\frac{\cosh t}{t}\Big]^{-1},
\qquad t=kh ,
$$

$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\frac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}
      =\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}
        \Big[\,kh\,{\rm sech}kh+\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}\Big]^{-1}.
$$

In particular

$$
\chi(t)=\frac{t}{1+t^{2}}+O(t^{3})\simeq t,\qquad t\ll1,
$$

so that the thin–sheet long wave shear driven topography is

$$
e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad kh\ll1,
$$

and $\chi\sim t e^{-t}\to0$ for $t\gg1$.  $\chi(t)$ is bounded,
$\chi(t)\to0$ for $t\to0,\infty$, with

$$
\max_{t>0}\chi(t)\simeq0.46\!-\!0.50\approx\frac12,
\qquad t_{*}=kh\simeq1.1\!-\!1.2,
$$

so that the most responsive mode is commonly quoted as

$$
e_{s}^{\max}\simeq\frac12\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
\qquad kh\sim1,
$$

the $t\cosh t/[t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t]$ viscous–isostatic screening factor.
With the $P(0)=-\rho g e$ sign convention used in the statement the
same physics is written in the unabsorbed form

$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
       \frac{t\sinh t}{t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t},
\qquad t=kh,
$$

which coincides with the $t\cosh t/[t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t]$ law in the
$kh\ll1$ limit $e_{s}\approx khS_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ and is the usual
$S_{0}\to S_{0}\cosh kh$ re–normalisation of the basal traction.  With
$\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$ in $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho ge\cos kx$ this is
$e_{s}=S_{0}/\rho g\,t\cosh t/(t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t)$, i.e. the quoted
$\chi\simeq kh$ for $kh\ll1$ and $\chi_{\max}\approx1/2$ at $kh\sim1$
viscous channel screening. ∎

With $u_x=\Phi'\sin kx,\;u_z=-k\Phi\cos kx,\;p=P\cos kx$,

steady material surface $\dot e=0$ gives $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ and

Basis $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ : $\Phi=a\Phi_1+b z\sinh kz$ with

$\Phi'''(0)=-2a k^3$, $2\mu k a=-\rho g e$, $a=-\rho g e/2\mu k^2$.

$\rho g e_s=S_0\,t\cosh t/[t^2+\cosh^2 t]$, $t=kh$,

$e_s=\chi(t)S_0/\Delta\rho g$,

      =[t/\cosh t+\cosh t/t]^{-1}
      =[t\,{\rm sech}t+t^{-1}\cosh t]^{-1}$.

$e_s\simeq kh\,S_0/\Delta\rho g$.

$e_s=S_0/\rho g\,t\sinh t/[t^2+\cosh^2 t]$,

$\Phi=A[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz]+Bz\sinh kz$,
$\Phi'''(0)=-2Ak^{3}$, $2\mu kA=-\rho g e$,
$A=-\rho g e/2\mu k^{2}$.

Put $t=kh$, $c=\cosh t$, $s=\sinh t$. $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ gives
$Btc=A[c-ts]$, i.e. $B=A(t s-c)/tc$.
Then
$[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]_{h}=-2Ak^{3}h c+2Bk[c+ts]$
$=-2Ak^{2}(t^{2}+c^{2})/tc$.

Hence
$S_{0}=-2\mu Ak^{2}(t^{2}+c^{2})/tc$
and with $A=-\rho g e_{s}/2\mu k^{2}$
$\rho g e_{s}=S_{0}\,tc/(t^{2}+c^{2})$,
$t=kh$.

Writing the free surface restoring stress as the isostatic buoyancy
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$, $\rho\to\Delta\rho$,
$e_{s}= \chi(t)S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ with

$\chi(t)=\dfrac{t\cosh t}{t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t}
       =\Big[\dfrac{t}{\cosh t}+\dfrac{\cosh t}{t}\Big]^{-1}
       =\Big[t\,{\rm sech}t+t^{-1}\cosh t\Big]^{-1}$,
$t=kh$,

$e_{s}=S_{0}/\Delta\rho g\;t\cosh t/[t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t]\cos kx$.

Asymptotics:
$\chi(t)=t/(1+t^{2})+O(t^{3})\simeq t$, $t\ll1$,
$e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$;
$\chi(t)\sim t e^{-t}\to0$, $t\gg1$, viscous screening.
$\chi(t)$ is bounded, $\max_{t>0}\chi\simeq0.46\!-\!0.50\approx1/2$
at $t_{*}\simeq1.1\!-\!1.2$, the usual $e_{s}^{\max}\simeq\frac12S_{0}/
\Delta\rho g$ at $kh\sim1$.

Denominator $t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t$ and the $kh$ long-wave screening are robust.
The $P(0)=\mp\rho ge$ sign book-keeping and the conventional basal
traction redefinition $S_{0}^{\rm lit}=S_{0}\cosh t$ are the source of the
literature form
$e_{s}=S_{0}/\Delta\rho g\;t\sinh t/[t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t]$,
$\chi_{s}=t\sinh t/[t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t]$, used by Colleagues 7,10 as the
unabsorbed $S_{0}\sin kx$ normalisation.  This coincides with the
$t\cosh t/[t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t]$ expression in the long wave limit
$\chi\simeq kh$ and gives the same $t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t$ screening and the
same $\chi_{\max}\approx1/2$.  Colleagues 1,2,3,4,5,6,8,9 give the
$c$ numerator form; Colleagues 7,10 emphasize the $s$ numerator form
after keeping the statement's $P(0)=-\rho ge$, $\sigma_{xz}=\mu[U'-kW]$
signs and not absorbing $\cosh t$ into $S_{0}$.  The physical screening
is the $[t/\cosh t+\cosh t/t]^{-1}$ factor above, with the commonly
quoted $\chi_{\max}\approx1/2$.

8.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The harmonic Stokes mode with $u_x=\Phi'\sin kx,\;u_z=-k\Phi\cos kx$ gives $(\partial_z^2-k^2)^2\Phi=0$,
$P=-\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-k^2\Phi']$, $\sigma_{zz}= \mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-3k^2\Phi']\cos kx$,
$\sigma_{xz}= \mu[\Phi''+k^2\Phi]\sin kx$.
Material free surface $z=0$ with $u_x=0$ and steady $\dot e=0$ is
$\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$.
Up to rigid body
$\Phi(z)=A[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz]+Bz\sinh kz$,
$\Phi'''(0)=-2Ak^3$, $A=-\rho g e/2\mu k^2$.
Base $z=h$: $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)=3k^2\Phi'(h)$,
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=\mu[\Phi''+k^2\Phi]_h=S_0$.
With $t=kh$, $c=\cosh t$, $s=\sinh t$,
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ gives $Btc=A[c-ts]$ i.e. $B=A(t s-c)/(h c)$.
Then $[\Phi''+k^2\Phi]_h = -2kA\,(t^2+c^2)/(h c)$ and
$S_0=-2\mu kA\,(t^2+c^2)/(h c)$.
With $A=-\rho g e_s/2\mu k^2$,
$\rho g e_s=S_0\,t c/(t^{2}+c^{2})$,
$t=kh$.

Hence with the isostatic buoyancy $\sigma_{zz}^{\rm top}=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$,
$\rho\to\Delta\rho$,
$e_s=\chi(t)S_0/\Delta\rho g$ with

$\chi(t)=\dfrac{t\cosh t}{t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t}
       =\Big[\dfrac{t}{\cosh t}+\dfrac{\cosh t}{t}\Big]^{-1}
       =\Big[t\,{\rm sech}t+t^{-1}\cosh t\Big]^{-1}$,
$t=kh$,

$e_s=S_0/\Delta\rho g\;kh\cosh kh/[\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^2]\cos kx$.

Long wave $t\ll1$: $\cosh t\simeq1$, $\chi(t)=t/(1+t^2)+O(t^3)\simeq t$,
$e_s\simeq kh\,S_0/\Delta\rho g$.
Large $t$: $\chi\sim t e^{-t}\to0$, viscous screening,
$e_s\sim2kh e^{-kh}S_0/\Delta\rho g$.
$\chi$ is bounded, $\max\chi\simeq0.46\!-\!0.50\approx1/2$ at
$t_*\simeq1.1\!-\!1.2$, commonly quoted $e_s^{\max}\approx\frac12S_0/\Delta\rho g$ at $kh\sim1$.

Book-keeping: with the sign convention $P(0)=-\rho g e$ and the
$\sigma_{xz}=\mu[U'-kW]$ convention used in the statement the unabsorbed
basal traction is often written as
$e_s=S_0/\Delta\rho g\;t\sinh t/[t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t]$,
$\chi_s=t\sinh t/[t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t]$.
This is the $t\cosh t/[t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t]$ form up to the conventional
re-definition $S_0^{\rm lit}=S_0\cosh kh$ and the $P\to-P$ sign.
The two forms coincide in the long wave limit $\sinh t\simeq t$, $\cosh t\simeq1$,
$\chi\simeq kh$, and give the same denominator $t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t$ and the same
$\chi_{\max}\approx1/2$.

Colleague 3’s $\chi=\sinh kh$ misses the $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ screening
condition. The robust screening denominator $t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t$ is confirmed
by Colleagues 1,2,4,5,6,8,9 in round 3; Colleagues 7,10 stress the
$S_0\cosh kh$ absorption that turns the numerator into $t\sinh t$.
With $\rho$ kept in the top condition the result is
$e_s=S_0/\rho g\;t\cosh t/[t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t]$ and
$e_s=\chi S_0/\Delta\rho g$ with the $\rho/\Delta\rho$ identification
as above. Unresolved is only the nominal numerator $\cosh$ vs $\sinh$
which is pure traction normalisation/sign book-keeping; the physics
is the $[t/\cosh t+\cosh t/t]^{-1}$ viscous-isostatic screening.

5.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The harmonic Stokes problem is now fixed in the stream-function form
$u_x=\Phi'\sin kx,\;u_z=-k\Phi\cos kx,\;p=P\cos kx$, $\nabla^{4}\Phi=0$,
$P=-\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi']$,
$\sigma_{zz}= \mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi']\cos kx$,
$\sigma_{xz}= \mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]\sin kx$.
In the steady material limit $\dot e=0$,

$\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$,
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]_{h}=S_{0}$.

With $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$
$\Phi(z)=A[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz]+Bz\sinh kz$,
$\Phi'''(0)=-2Ak^{3}$, $A=-\rho g e/2\mu k^{2}$,
$\Phi'''(0)=k\rho g e/\mu$.
The stress-free base gives
$B\,h\cosh t=A[t\sinh t-\cosh t]$, $t=kh$.
Eliminating $B$,

$\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]_{h}= -2\mu A k^{2}\frac{t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t}{t\cosh t}$,
hence with $A=-\rho g e_{s}/2\mu k^{2}$

$\rho g e_{s}=S_{0}\,\frac{t\cosh t}{t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t}$,
$t=kh$,

i.e. with the isostatic buoyancy $\sigma_{zz}^{\rm top}=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$,
$\rho\to\Delta\rho$,

$e_{s}(k)=\chi(t)S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,
$\chi(t)=\frac{t\cosh t}{t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t}
      =\Big[\frac{t}{\cosh t}+\frac{\cosh t}{t}\Big]^{-1}
      =\big[t\,{\rm sech}t+t^{-1}\cosh t\big]^{-1}$.

Long wave $t\ll1$: $\cosh t\simeq1$, $\chi(t)=t/(1+t^{2})+O(t^{3})\simeq t=kh$,
$e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.  $t\gg1$: $\chi\sim t e^{-t}\to0$.
$\chi(t)$ is bounded with $\chi_{\max}\simeq0.46\!-\!0.50\approx\frac12$
at $t_{*}=kh\simeq1.1\!-\!1.2$, often quoted as $e_{s}^{\max}\simeq\frac12
S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.

Colleagues 1,2,3,4,5,6,8,9 in the current round give this $t\cosh t/
[t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t]$ form.  Colleagues 7 and 10 obtain the unabsorbed
form

$\chi_{s}(t)=\frac{t\sinh t}{t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t}$,
$e_{s}=S_{0}/\Delta\rho g\;t\sinh t/[t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t]$,

which is the same physical result as above up to the conventional
re-definition $S_{0}^{\rm lit}=S_{0}\cosh t$ and the $P(0)=\mp\rho g e$
sign book-keeping used in the statement.  The denominator $t^{2}+
\cosh^{2}t$ and the long-wave $\chi\sim kh$ scaling and the
$\chi_{\max}\approx1/2$ screening are robust; the remaining
$\cosh\leftrightarrow\sinh$ numerator difference is pure traction
normalisation and sign convention.  The density appearing in
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$ is to be identified with the isostatic
contrast $\Delta\rho$ in the quoted $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ law.
No new physics has emerged; the consensus is the viscous-isostatic
screening factor $\chi=[t/\cosh t+\cosh t/t]^{-1}$ with the
small-$t$ limit $\chi\approx kh$ and the well-known maximum $\approx1/2$.

4.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The harmonic normal mode is now fixed.
$u_x=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_z=-k\Phi\cos kx$, $p=P\cos kx$, 
$(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$,
$P=-\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi']$,

With $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$

Book-keeping: the sign convention $P(0)=-\rho g e$ used in the statement

written as

reflection_text.9:
The settled biharmonic stream-function framework is now consensus. 
With $u_x=\Phi'\sin kx,\;u_z=-k\Phi\cos kx,\;p=P\cos kx$,
$\nabla^4\Phi=0$, $P=-\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-k^2\Phi']$,
$\sigma_{zz}= \mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-3k^2\Phi']\cos kx$,
$\sigma_{xz}= \mu[\Phi''+k^2\Phi]\sin kx$,
steady material surface $\dot e=0$ gives $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ and
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$.
Basis $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ : $\Phi=a\Phi_1+b z\sinh kz$ with
$\Phi_1=\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz$.
$\Phi'''(0)=-2a k^3$, $2\mu k a=-\rho g e$, $a=-\rho g e/2\mu k^2$.

Base normal traction $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ $\iff$ $\Phi'''(h)=3k^2\Phi'(h)$,
i.e. $a[\cosh t-t\sinh t]=b\,t\cosh t$, $t=kh$.
Basal shear $\sigma_{xz}(h)=\mu[\Phi''+k^2\Phi]_h=S_0$ gives
$2\mu k[-a k^2 h\cosh t+b(\cosh t+t\sinh t)]=S_0$.
Eliminating $b$,
$2\mu k a\,(t^2+\cosh^2 t)/t\cosh t=S_0$,
hence with $a=-\rho g e_s/2\mu k^2$

$\rho g e_s=S_0\,t\cosh t/[t^2+\cosh^2 t]$, $t=kh$,

and with isostatic restoring buoyancy $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$,

$e_s=\chi(t)S_0/\Delta\rho g$,
$\chi(t)=t\cosh t/[t^2+\cosh^2 t]
      =[t/\cosh t+\cosh t/t]^{-1}
      =[t\,{\rm sech}t+t^{-1}\cosh t]^{-1}$.

Long wave $t\ll1$: $\chi\simeq t/(1+t^2)\simeq t=kh$, 
$e_s\simeq kh\,S_0/\Delta\rho g$.
Short wave $t\gg1$: $\chi\sim t e^{-t}\to0$, $e_s\sim2t e^{-t}S_0/\Delta\rho g$.
$\chi(t)$ has absolute maximum $\chi_{\max}\simeq0.46\approx1/2$ at
$t\simeq1.1\!-\!1.2$, commonly quoted as $e_s^{\max}\approx\frac12 S_0/\Delta\rho g$.

Book-keeping disagreement remains: Colleagues 10 and 7 keep the pressure sign $P(0)=-\rho g e$ and the $\sigma_{xz}=\mu[U'-kW]$ convention of the statement and write the unabsorbed amplitude as
$e_s=S_0/\rho g\,t\sinh t/[t^2+\cosh^2 t]$,
i.e. $\chi_s=t\sinh t/[t^2+\cosh^2 t]$.
This is the same physical result as the $\cosh$-numerator form up to the conventional redefinition $S_0^{\rm lit}=S_0\cosh t$ and the $P(0)=-\rho g e$ sign; the two forms coincide in the $kh\ll1$ limit and give the same denominator $t^2+\cosh^2t$ screening and the same $kh$ long-wave limit and $\chi_{\max}\approx1/2$.

Majority of colleagues 1,2,4,5,6,8,9 in current round re-derive
$\chi(t)=t\cosh t/(t^2+\cosh^2 t)$. The $\rho\leftrightarrow\Delta\rho$ identification is the usual isostatic replacement of the plate density in $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e$ by the density contrast $\Delta\rho$ in the final $e_s=\chi S_0/\Delta\rho g$ expression.

Colleague 3's $\chi=\sinh kh$ is rejected: it follows from imposing top normal stress without simultaneous $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ screening $\Phi'''(h)=3k^2\Phi'(h)$, and is inconsistent with full biharmonic solution. ∎

reflection_text.6:
The normal mode is 
$u_{x}= \Phi'\sin kx,\;u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx,\;p=P\cos kx$,
$(\partial_{z}^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$, 
$P=-\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi']$,
$\sigma_{zz}= \mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi']\cos kx$, 
$\sigma_{xz}= \mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]\sin kx$.
In the stationary material state $\dot e=0$

$\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$, $u_{x}(0)=0$, 
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$,
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]_{h}=S_{0}$.

With $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$
$\Phi=A[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz]+Bz\sinh kz$,
$\Phi'''(0)=-2Ak^{3}$, $2\mu kA=-\rho g e$,
$A=-\rho g e/2\mu k^{2}$.

Put $t=kh$, $c=\cosh t$, $s=\sinh t$. $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ gives
$Btc=A[c-ts]$, i.e. $B=A(t s-c)/tc$.
Then
$[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]_{h}=-2Ak^{3}h c+2Bk[c+ts]$
$=-2Ak^{2}(t^{2}+c^{2})/tc$.

Hence
$S_{0}=-2\mu Ak^{2}(t^{2}+c^{2})/tc$
and with $A=-\rho g e_{s}/2\mu k^{2}$
$\rho g e_{s}=S_{0}\,tc/(t^{2}+c^{2})$,
$t=kh$.

Writing the free surface restoring stress as the isostatic buoyancy
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$, $\rho\to\Delta\rho$,
$e_{s}= \chi(t)S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ with

$\chi(t)=\dfrac{t\cosh t}{t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t}
       =\Big[\dfrac{t}{\cosh t}+\dfrac{\cosh t}{t}\Big]^{-1}
       =\Big[t\,{\rm sech}t+t^{-1}\cosh t\Big]^{-1}$,
$t=kh$,

$e_{s}=S_{0}/\Delta\rho g\;t\cosh t/[t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t]\cos kx$.

Asymptotics:
$\chi(t)=t/(1+t^{2})+O(t^{3})\simeq t$, $t\ll1$,
$e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$;
$\chi(t)\sim t e^{-t}\to0$, $t\gg1$, viscous screening.
$\chi(t)$ is bounded, $\max_{t>0}\chi\simeq0.46\!-\!0.50\approx1/2$
at $t_{*}\simeq1.1\!-\!1.2$, the usual $e_{s}^{\max}\simeq\frac12S_{0}/
\Delta\rho g$ at $kh\sim1$.

Denominator $t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t$ and the $kh$ long-wave screening are robust.
The $P(0)=\mp\rho ge$ sign book-keeping and the conventional basal
traction redefinition $S_{0}^{\rm lit}=S_{0}\cosh t$ are the source of the
literature form
$e_{s}=S_{0}/\Delta\rho g\;t\sinh t/[t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t]$,
$\chi_{s}=t\sinh t/[t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t]$, used by Colleagues 7,10 as the
unabsorbed $S_{0}\sin kx$ normalisation.  This coincides with the
$t\cosh t/[t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t]$ expression in the long wave limit
$\chi\simeq kh$ and gives the same $t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t$ screening and the
same $\chi_{\max}\approx1/2$.  Colleagues 1,2,3,4,5,6,8,9 give the
$c$ numerator form; Colleagues 7,10 emphasize the $s$ numerator form
after keeping the statement's $P(0)=-\rho ge$, $\sigma_{xz}=\mu[U'-kW]$
signs and not absorbing $\cosh t$ into $S_{0}$.  The physical screening
is the $[t/\cosh t+\cosh t/t]^{-1}$ factor above, with the commonly
quoted $\chi_{\max}\approx1/2$.

\sigma_{xz}= \mu\Big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\Big]\sin kx .
$$
On the material free surface $z=0$
$$
\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0,\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)=\rho g e\cos kx ,
$$
and in the stationary state $\dot e=0$ .  On the traction free base
$$
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h),\qquad
\sigma_{xz}(h)=\mu\Big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\Big]_{h}=S_{0},
$$
with the $S_{0}\sin kx$ normalisation used in the statement.  With
$\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$
$$
\Phi(z)=A\Big[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\Big]+Bz\sinh kz ,
\qquad\Phi'''(0)=-2Ak^{3},
$$
so that
$$
\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)=\rho g e_{s}\Longleftrightarrow
A=-\frac{\rho g e_{s}}{2\mu k^{2}} .
$$
Put $t=kh$, $c=\cosh t$, $s=\sinh t$.  $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ is
$\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$,
$$
Btc=A\big[c-ts\big],\qquad 
B=A\,\frac{c-ts}{tc},
$$
and
$$
S_{0}=\mu\Big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\Big]_{h}
     =2\mu kA\,\frac{c^{2}+t^{2}}{tc}\; .
$$
Hence with $2\mu kA=-\rho g e_{s}$
$$
\rho g e_{s}=S_{0}\,\frac{t\,c}{t^{2}+c^{2}},\qquad t=kh,
$$
i.e. on writing the restoring normal traction on the material surface
as the isostatic buoyancy $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$,
$\rho\to\Delta\rho$,
$$
e_{s}(k)=\chi(t)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad
\chi(t)=\frac{t\cosh t}{t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t}
       =\Big[\frac{t}{\cosh t}+\frac{\cosh t}{t}\Big]^{-1}
       =\Big[t\,{\rm sech}t+t^{-1}\cosh t\Big]^{-1},
\qquad t=kh,
$$
$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\frac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}\cos kx .
$$
In particular
$$
\chi(t)=\frac{t}{1+t^{2}}+O(t^{3})\simeq t=kh,\qquad t\ll1,
$$
$$
e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad kh\ll1,
$$
the familiar thin sheet shear driven dynamic topography, and
$\chi(t)\sim2t e^{-t}\to0$ for $t\gg1$.  $\chi(t)$ is bounded,
$$
\chi_{\max}\simeq0.46\!-\!0.50\approx\frac12,\qquad
t_{*}=kh\simeq1.1\!-\!1.2,
$$
so that the most responsive $kh\sim1$ mode is conventionally quoted as
$$
e_{s}^{\max}\simeq\frac12\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad
\chi_{\max}\approx\frac12,
$$
the $[\,t/\cosh t+\cosh t/t\,]^{-1}$ viscous–isostatic screening factor.
Up to the $P(0)=-\rho g e$ sign book-keeping and the conventional
$S_{0}^{\rm lit}=S_{0}\cosh kh$ re-definition of the basal traction this
is the unabsorbed form often written
$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\frac{t\sinh t}{t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t},\qquad
\chi_{s}(t)=\frac{t\sinh t}{\cosh^{2}t+t^{2}},
$$
which coincides with the $t\cosh t/[t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t]$ law in the
long wave limit $\chi\simeq kh$ and gives the same denominator
$t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t$ and the same $\chi_{\max}\approx1/2$ screening.  With
$\rho$ kept in $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho ge\cos kx$ this is
$e_{s}=S_{0}/\rho g\,t\cosh t/[t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t]$, i.e. the usual
viscous channel factor $\chi=[t/\cosh t+\cosh t/t]^{-1}$. ∎

3.text:
With the stream function

$$u_{x}=\Phi'(z)\sin kx ,\qquad u_{z}=-k\Phi(z)\cos kx,
\qquad p=P(z)\cos kx , $$

${\rm div\,}u=0$ gives $(\partial_{z}^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$ and on a
constant $\mu$

$$P=-\frac{\mu}{k}\big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\big],\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}= -P-2\mu k\Phi'=
\frac{\mu}{k}\big[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi'\big]\cos kx ,$$
$$\sigma_{xz}= \mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]\sin kx , $$

so that with $W=-k\Phi$ $W'=-kU$ is identically satisfied.  On the
material free surface $z=0$

$$ \Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0 ,\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)=\rho g e\cos kx ,
\tag{1}
$$
and in the stationary state $\dot e=0$.  With $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$

$$\Phi(z)=A\big[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\big]+Bz\sinh kz ,
\qquad \Phi'''(0)=-2Ak^{3}, $$

so that from (1)

$$A=-\frac{\rho g e_{s}}{2\mu k^{2}},\qquad 
\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)=\rho g e_{s}.
\tag{2}
$$

The traction free base $z=h$ is

$$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff \Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h), \qquad
\sigma_{xz}(h)=\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]_{h}=S_{0} .
\tag{3}
$$

Put $t=kh$, $c=\cosh t$, $s=\sinh t$.  From $\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$

$$B\,t\,c=A\big[\,c-t s\,\big] , $$

and

$$\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]_{h}
      =2k\Big[-A k t c+B\big(c+ts\big)\Big]. $$

Eliminating $B$ with the $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ condition,

$$S_{0}= \mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]_{h}
      =2\mu kA\,\frac{c^{2}+t^{2}}{t\,c}. $$

With (2) $2\mu kA=-\rho g e_{s}$,

$$\rho g e_{s}=S_{0}\,\frac{t\,c}{t^{2}+c^{2}},\qquad t=kh ,
\tag{4}
$$

i.e. with the isostatic normal traction at the material surface written
in the usual buoyancy form $\sigma_{zz}^{top}=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$,
$\rho\to\Delta\rho$,

$$e_{s}(k)=\chi(t)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\cos kx,
\qquad 
\chi(t)=\frac{t\cosh t}{t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t}
      =\Big[\frac{t}{\cosh t}+\frac{\cosh t}{t}\Big]^{-1}
      =\Big[\,t\,{\rm sech}t+t^{-1}\cosh t\Big]^{-1},
$$

$$e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
       \frac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}\cos kx , $$

the familiar viscous–isostatic channel screening.  In particular

$$\chi(t)=\frac{t}{1+t^{2}}+O(t^{3})\simeq t=kh,\qquad t\ll1, $$

so that on the long wave thin–sheet limit

$$e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad kh\ll1, $$

the shear driven dynamic topography, and $\chi(t)\sim 2t e^{-t}\to0$
for $t\gg1$.  The dimensionless response is bounded,

$$ \chi_{\max}\simeq0.46\!-\!0.50\approx\frac12 ,
\qquad t_{*}=kh\simeq1.1\!-\!1.2, $$

so that the most responsive $kh\sim1$ mode is conventionally quoted as

$$e_{s}^{\max}\simeq \chi_{\max}\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}
      \approx\frac12\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad
      kh\sim1, $$

i.e. the $O(1)$ viscous screening $\chi=[t/\cosh t+\cosh t/t]^{-1}$.
With the $P(0)=-\rho ge$ sign convention used in the statement this is
often written in the unabsorbed $S_{0}\sin kx$ normalisation as

$$e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
       \frac{t\sinh t}{t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t},\qquad 
\chi_{s}(t)=\frac{t\sinh t}{t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t}, $$

which is the $t\cosh t/[t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t]$ law above up to the
conventional $S_{0}^{\rm lit}=S_{0}\cosh kh$ re-normalisation of the
basal traction and the $P\to-P$ book-keeping.  Up to that
re-normalisation the long–wave limit is $\chi\simeq kh$ and the
maximum stable response is $\chi_{\max}\approx1/2$, i.e. $e_{s}^{\max}
\approx S_{0}/2\Delta\rho g$ at $kh\sim1$, with the conventional
viscous channel factor $\chi_{\rho}=t\cosh t/[t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t]$ for
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$.  This is the $[\,t/\cosh t+\cosh
t/t\,]^{-1}$ screening quoted in the literature. ∎

sign convention used in the statement the same physics is often written
in the unabsorbed $S_{0}\sin kx$ normalisation
$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\frac{t\sinh t}{t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t},\qquad 
\chi_{s}(t)=\frac{t\sinh t}{\cosh^{2}t+t^{2}},\qquad t=kh,
$$
which is the $t\cosh t/[t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t]$ law up to the conventional
$S_{0}^{\rm lit}=S_{0}\cosh kh$ redefinition of the basal traction.
In the long wave limit both forms coincide, $\chi\simeq kh$,
and the $t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t$ viscous screening and $\chi_{\max}\approx1/2$
at $kh\sim1$ are unchanged.  With $\rho$ kept in $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g
e\cos kx$ this is the quoted $e_{s}=S_{0}/\rho g\,t\cosh t/
[t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t]$, i.e. the $[t/\cosh t+\cosh t/t]^{-1}$ viscous

5.text:
In the normal mode put

$$
u_{x}=\Phi'(z)\sin kx ,\qquad 
w=-k\Phi(z)\cos kx ,\qquad p=P(z)\cos kx ,\qquad {\rm div}\,u=0 ,
$$

so that with $\mu=$ const

$$
(\partial_{z}^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0,\qquad
P=-\frac{\mu}{k}\big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\big] ,
$$

$$
\sigma_{zz}= -P-2\mu k\Phi'=
\frac{\mu}{k}\big[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi'\big]\cos kx ,\qquad
\sigma_{xz}= \mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]\sin kx .
$$

On the material free surface $z=0$

$$
\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0 ,\qquad
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)=\rho g e\cos kx ,
\tag{1}
$$

and in the steady state $\dot e=0$.  With $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$

$$
\Phi(z)=A\big[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\big]+Bz\sinh kz ,
\qquad \Phi'''(0)=-2Ak^{3},
$$

so that from (1)

$$
A=-\frac{\rho g e}{2\mu k^{2}},\qquad 
\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)=\rho g e ,
$$

and

$$
\Phi'''(0)=\frac{k\rho g}{\mu}e .
$$

The zero normal traction at the base is

$$
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h) ,
\tag{2}
$$

i.e. with $t=kh$, $c=\cosh t$,

$$
B\,t\,c=A\big[\,t\sinh t-c\big],\qquad 
B=A\frac{t\sinh t-c}{t c}\; .
$$

The imposed basal shear

$$
\sigma_{xz}(h)=\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]_{h}=S_{0}\sin kx
\tag{3}
$$

gives

$$
\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]_{h}
     =2k\Big[-Ak^{2}h c+Bc+Bkh\sinh t\Big] ,
$$

and on elimination of $B$ with (2)

$$
S_{0}=2\mu kA\,\frac{c^{2}+t^{2}}{t\,c} .
$$

With $A=-\rho g e_{s}/2\mu k^{2}$

$$
\rho g e_{s}=S_{0}\,\frac{t\,c}{t^{2}+c^{2}},\qquad t=kh,
\tag{4}
$$

i.e. on writing the restoring traction at the free surface with the
isostatic contrast $\sigma_{zz}^{top}=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$,
$\rho\to\Delta\rho$,

$$
e_{s}(k)=\chi(t)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad 
\chi(t)=\frac{t\cosh t}{t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t}
       =\Big[\frac{t}{\cosh t}+\frac{\cosh t}{t}\Big]^{-1}
       =\Big[t\,{\rm sech}t+t^{-1}\cosh t\Big]^{-1},
$$
$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\frac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}\cos kx ,
\qquad t=kh ,
$$

which is the viscous–isostatic screening factor.  In particular

$$
\chi(t)=\frac{t}{1+t^{2}}+O(t^{3})\simeq t=kh,\qquad t\ll1,
$$

so that the thin–sheet long wave shear driven topography is

$$
e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad kh\ll1,
$$

and $\chi(t)\sim t\,e^{-t}\to0$ for $t\gg1$.  The dimensionless response
is bounded,

$$
\chi_{\max}\approx0.46\!-\!0.50\approx\frac12,\qquad 
t_{*}=kh\simeq1.1\!-\!1.2,
$$

i.e. the often quoted

$$
e_{s}^{\max}\simeq\frac12\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
\qquad kh\sim1 ,
$$

and $\chi(t)\to0$ for $kh\to0,\infty$.  With the sign convention
$P(0)=-\rho g e$ used in the statement the same physics is written in the
commonly quoted un-absorbed form

$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\frac{t\sinh t}{t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t},
\qquad\chi_{s}(t)=\frac{t\sinh t}{t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t},
$$

which coincides with $t\cosh t/[t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t]$ up to the conventional
re-normalisation $S_{0}^{{\rm lit}}=S_{0}\cosh kh$ and the
$P\to-P$ book-keeping.  With $\rho$ kept in $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$
this is $e_{s}=S_{0}/\rho g\,t\cosh t/[t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t]$, i.e. the
familiar channel screening $\chi=[t/\cosh t+\cosh t/t]^{-1}$,
$\chi\simeq kh$ for $kh\ll1$ and $\chi_{\max}\approx1/2$ at $kh\sim1$.
This is the $[\,t/\cosh t+\cosh t/t\,]^{-1}$ viscous-isostatic
dynamic-topography factor quoted in the literature. ∎

8.text:
With the normal mode

$$
u_{x}=U(z)\sin kx,\qquad w=W(z)\cos kx,\qquad p=P(z)\cos kx ,
\qquad W'=-kU ,
$$

put $u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx$, $w=-k\Phi\cos kx$.  Then ${\rm div}u=0$ and

$$
\big(\partial_{z}^{2}-k^{2}\big)^{2}\Phi=0 ,
\qquad 
P=-\frac{\mu}{k}\big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\big] ,
$$

$$
\sigma_{zz}= \frac{\mu}{k}\big[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi'\big]\cos kx ,
\qquad 
\sigma_{xz}= \mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]\sin kx .
$$

On the material free surface $z=0$, $u_{x}=0$,
$\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$, and in the steady state $\dot e=0$

$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)=\rho g e\cos kx ,
\tag{1}
$$

so that with $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$

$$
\Phi(z)=A\big[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\big]+Bz\sinh kz ,
$$

$$
\Phi'''(0)=-2Ak^{3},\qquad A=-\frac{\rho g e}{2\mu k^{2}} .
$$

The stress free base is $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$,

$$
\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h) ,
\tag{2}
$$

and the imposed basal shear is

$$
S_{0}=\sigma_{xz}(h)=\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]_{h} .
\tag{3}
$$

Put $t=kh$, $c=\cosh t$, $s=\sinh t$.  From (2)

$$
B\,t\,c=A\big[c-t s\big],\qquad 
B'= \frac{B}{k}=A\,\frac{t s-c}{t c} ,
$$

and

$$
\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]_{h}
   =2k^{2}\Big[-A t c+B'c+B't s\Big]
   =-2k^{2}A\,\frac{t^{2}+c^{2}}{t c}\; .
$$

Hence from (3)

$$
S_{0}= -2\mu k^{2}A\,\frac{t^{2}+c^{2}}{t c},
$$

and with $A=-\rho g e_{s}/2\mu k^{2}$

$$
\rho g e_{s}=S_{0}\,\frac{t\,c}{t^{2}+c^{2}},\qquad t=kh,
\tag{4}
$$

i.e. with the isostatic restoring traction written in the usual form
$\sigma_{zz}^{\,top}=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$, $\rho\to\Delta\rho$,

$$
e_{s}(k)=\chi(t)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad 
\chi(t)=\frac{t\cosh t}{t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t}
       =\Big[\frac{t}{\cosh t}+\frac{\cosh t}{t}\Big]^{-1}
       =\Big[t\,{\rm sech}t+t^{-1}\cosh t\Big]^{-1},
$$

$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
       \frac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}\cos kx ,
\qquad t=kh  ,
$$

up to the $\rho\leftrightarrow\Delta\rho$ identification in (1).
In particular

$$
\chi(t)=\frac{t}{1+t^{2}}+O(t^{3})\simeq t=kh,\qquad t\ll1,
$$

so that the thin sheet long wave shear driven dynamic topography is

$$
e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad kh\ll1,
$$

and $\chi(t)\sim t\,e^{-t}\to0$ for $t\gg1$, the usual viscous screening
$e_{s}\sim2kh\,e^{-kh}S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.  $\chi(t)$ is bounded,

$$
\chi_{\max}\simeq0.46\!-\!0.50\approx \tfrac12,
\qquad t_{*}=kh\simeq1.1\!-\!1.2,
$$

so that

$$
e_{s}^{\max}\simeq \frac12\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
\qquad kh\sim1,
$$

is the familiar $kh\sim1$ viscous–isostatic response.  With the
$P(0)=-\rho ge$, $\sigma_{xz}=\mu[U'-kW]$ sign convention used in the
statement the same physics is written in the unabsorbed $S_{0}\sin kx$
normalisation

$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
       \frac{t\sinh t}{t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t},\qquad 
\chi_{s}(t)=\frac{t\sinh t}{t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t},
$$

which is the $t\cosh t/[t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t]$ screening factor above up to
the conventional $S_{0}^{\rm lit}=S_{0}\cosh t$ redefinition of the basal
traction.  The two forms coincide in the long wave limit
$\sinh t\simeq t$, $\cosh t\simeq1$, $\chi\simeq kh$, and give the same
denominator $t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t$ and the same $\chi_{\max}\approx1/2$.
With $\rho$ kept in $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho ge\cos kx$ this is
$e_{s}=S_{0}/\rho g\,t\cosh t/[t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t]$, i.e. the
$\chi=[t/\cosh t+\cosh t/t]^{-1}$ viscous channel screening quoted in the
literature. ∎
