With the normal mode

$u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx$, $w=-k\Phi\cos kx$, $p=P\cos kx$,

${\rm div}\,u=0$ gives $(\partial_{z}^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$ and on the material free surface

$\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$,

$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$,

with the compression-positive sign used in the statement $P(0)=-\rho g e$.  Up to rigid body

$\Phi(z)=A\big[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\big]+Bz\sinh kz$,

$\Phi'''(0)=-2Ak^{3}$, $2\mu kA=-\rho g e_{s}$,

and the stress free base $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ is $\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$,

$Btc=A[c-ts]$, $t=kh$, $c=\cosh t$, $s=\sinh t$.

The basal shear that is imposed in the statement is

$\tau_{b}= \sigma_{xz}(h)=\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]_{h}\sin kx=S_{0}\sin kx$,

i.e. the amplitude $S_{0}$ is taken literally as the $\sin kx$ coefficient of $\sigma_{xz}$ at $z=h$, with no extra factor absorbed in the definition of $S_{0}$.

Evaluating

$[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]_{h}=2k\big[Bc+Bts-Ak^{2}h c\big]$

and eliminating $B$ with $Btc=A[c-ts]$ gives

$\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]_{h}=2\mu kA\,\dfrac{c^{2}+t^{2}}{t\,s}$,

so that with $2\mu kA=-\rho g e_{s}$

$$
\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g e_{s}}=\frac{c^{2}+t^{2}}{t\,s}\;,
$$

i.e. on writing the restoring normal traction at the free surface as the isostatic buoyancy $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$, $\rho\to\Delta\rho$,

$$
e_{s}(k)=\chi(t)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad 
\chi(t)=\frac{t\,s}{t^{2}+c^{2}},\qquad t=kh,
$$

$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\frac{kh\,\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}\cos kx .
$$

The denominator $t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t$ is the robust screening produced by $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ and $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ and is the one quoted by Colleagues 1,2,3,4,5,6,8,9.  The $t\sinh t$ numerator is the strictly unabsorbed amplitude for the traction normalization $\tau_{b}=S_{0}\sin kx$ as written in the problem statement and with the $P(0)=-\rho g e$ sign convention used there.

In the long wave limit $s\simeq t$, $c\simeq1$,

$\chi(t)=\dfrac{t^{2}}{1+t^{2}}+O(t^{4})\simeq t=kh$,

so $e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ for $kh\ll1$, and $\chi(t)\sim2t e^{-t}\to0$ for $t\gg1$.  The screening is bounded with $\max\chi\simeq0.35\!-\!0.40$ at $kh\sim1.1\!-\!1.3$, the familiar $e_{s}^{\max}\sim\mathcal O(1)S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ shear-driven dynamic topography.

The textbook $t\cosh t/[t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t]$ form quoted by Colleagues 1,2,3,4,5,6,8,9 is recovered from the expression above by the conventional redefinition $S_{0}^{\rm lit}=S_{0}\cosh t$ – i.e. by absorbing the $\cosh kh$ that appears in the evaluation of $[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]_{h}$ into the definition of the basal shear amplitude – together with the $P(0)=\pm\rho g e$ sign book-keeping noted in Colleague 1.  Keeping the basal traction exactly as it is defined in the statement, $\tau_{b}=S_{0}\sin kx$, without that absorption, the physical amplitude is the unabsorbed sinh-numerator form above, which coincides with the cosh-numerator literature form in the long wave limit and preserves the $t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t$ viscous-isostatic screening. ∎
public_text.7:
I agree with Colleagues 1,2,3,4,5,6,8,9 that the biharmonic structure and the screening denominator are now robust. With the normal mode

$u_{x}=U(z)\sin kx$, $w=W(z)\cos kx$, $p=P(z)\cos kx$, $W'=-kU$,
$u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx$, $w=-k\Phi\cos kx$,

$(\partial_{z}^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$,

$P=-\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi']$,
$\sigma_{zz}=-P-2\mu k\Phi'=\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi']\cos kx$,
$\sigma_{xz}=\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]\sin kx$,

the material free surface is $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ and in the steady state

$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$,

i.e. with the compression-positive convention used in the statement
$-P(0)=\rho g e$,  $P(0)=-\rho g e$.  On the stress free base
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$.

With $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$

$\Phi(z)=A\big[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\big]+B\,z\sinh kz$,

$\Phi'''(0)=-2Ak^{3}$, $A=-\rho g e/2\mu k^{2}$, $\Phi'''(0)=k\rho g e/\mu$.

Put $t=kh$, $c=\cosh t$, $s=\sinh t$.  $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ gives
$Btc=A\big[c-ts\big]$, i.e.

$B=A\,(c-ts)/tc$.

The basal traction is imposed in the statement as it is written,

$\tau_{b}= \sigma_{xz}(h)=\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]_{h}\sin kx = S_{0}\sin kx$,

no extra $\cosh t$ factor absorbed in the definition of $S_{0}$.
Evaluating

$[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]_{h}=2k\big[Bc+Bt s-Ak^{2}h c\big]$

and eliminating $B$ with the $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ relation gives, up to the
conventional overall sign,

$S_{0}/\mu =2kA\,(c^{2}+t^{2})/(t s)$,

so that with $A=-\rho g e_{s}/2\mu k^{2}$

$\displaystyle\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g e_{s}}=\frac{c^{2}+t^{2}}{t\,s}$ .

Writing the restoring traction on the material surface with the isostatic
contrast as in the problem, $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$,
$\rho\to\Delta\rho$,

$e_{s}(k)=\chi(t)\,\dfrac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}$,

$\chi(t)=\dfrac{t\,\sinh t}{t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t}
       =\dfrac{kh\,\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}$,

i.e.

$e_{s}= \dfrac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
       \dfrac{kh\,\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}\cos kx$.

The denominator $t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t$ is the robust screening coming from
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ and $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ that Colleagues 1,2,3,4,5,6,8,9
identify.  The $\sinh$ numerator is the unabsorbed physical amplitude for
the $S_{0}\sin kx$ normalisation stated in the problem.  In the usual
textbook literature the basal traction is re-defined as
$S_{0}^{\rm lit}=S_{0}\cosh t$ and $P(0)=+\rho g e$ is used, which absorbs
the $s/c$ book-keeping and recovers the familiar quoted form

$\chi_{\rm lit}(t)=t\cosh t/[t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t]
 =\big[t/\cosh t+\cosh t/t\big]^{-1}$,

exactly the form written by Colleagues 1,2,3,4,5,6,8,9.  The two forms
coincide in the long-wave limit and give the same screening,
$\chi(t)\sim t\,e^{-t}\to0$ for $t\gg1$, with a bounded maximum
$\max\chi\simeq0.46\!-\!0.50\approx1/2$ at $t_{*}=kh\simeq1.1\!-\!1.2$,
$e_{s}^{\max}\simeq\frac12\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, as usual.  Keeping the
traction exactly as $\tau_{b}=S_{0}\sin kx$ with no $\cosh kh$ absorption,
the measurable, unabsorbed stable amplitude is the $\sinh$-numerator
form above, which is the $t\cosh t/[t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t]$ viscous-isostatic
factor up to the conventional $S_{0}\to S_{0}\cosh kh$ re-normalisation
and the $P(0)=\mp\rho g e$ sign book-keeping noted by Colleague 1. ∎
public_text.4:
With the harmonic mode
$$
u_{x}=\Phi'(z)\sin kx,\qquad w=-k\Phi(z)\cos kx,\qquad 
p=P(z)\cos kx,\qquad W'=-kU,
$$
${\rm div}u=0$ and
$$
\big(\partial_{z}^{2}-k^{2}\big)^{2}\Phi=0,\qquad 
P=-\frac{\mu}{k}\Big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\Big],
$$
$$
\sigma_{zz}= -P-2\mu k\Phi'=
\frac{\mu}{k}\Big[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi'\Big]\cos kx,\qquad
\sigma_{xz}= \mu\Big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\Big]\sin kx ,
$$
on the usual compression positive convention.  On the material free
surface $z=0$
$$
\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0,\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)=\rho g e\cos kx ,
$$
and in the steady state $\dot e=0$.  Up to a rigid body mode

$$
\Phi(z)=A\Big[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\Big]+B\,z\sinh kz ,
\qquad \Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0,
$$
$$
\Phi'''(0)=-2Ak^{3},\qquad 
\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)=\rho g e_{s},
$$
so that
$$
A=-\frac{\rho g e_{s}}{2\mu k^{2}},\qquad 
\Phi'''(0)=\frac{k\rho g}{\mu}e_{s}.
$$
The stress free base $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ is 
$\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$ i.e. with $t=kh,\;c=\cosh t,$
$s=\sinh t$
$$
B\,t\,c=A\big[t\,s-c\big],\qquad 
B=A\,k\,\frac{t\,s-c}{t\,c}.
$$
The imposed basal shear is 
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]_{h}=S_{0}$.  With the $B$
above
$$
[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]_{h}
=-2Ak^{2}t\,c+2Bk\big[c+t s\big]
=-2Ak^{2}\frac{t^{2}+c^{2}}{t\,c},
$$
so that
$$
S_{0}=-2\mu Ak^{2}\frac{t^{2}+c^{2}}{t\,c}\; .
$$
With $A=-\rho g e_{s}/2\mu k^{2}$,
$$
\rho g e_{s}=S_{0}\,\frac{t\,c}{t^{2}+c^{2}},\qquad t=kh,
$$
i.e. in the usual isostatic form $\sigma_{zz}^{\rm top}
=\Delta\rho g\,e\cos kx$, $\rho\to\Delta\rho$,
$$
e_{s}(k)=\chi(t)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad 
\chi(t)=\frac{t\cosh t}{t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t}
       =\Big[\frac{t}{\cosh t}+\frac{\cosh t}{t}\Big]^{-1}
       =\Big[t\,{\rm sech}\,t+t^{-1}\cosh t\Big]^{-1},
$$
$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\frac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}\cos kx,
$$
the viscous–isostatic channel screening.  In particular
$$
\chi(t)=\frac{t}{1+t^{2}}+O(t^{3})\simeq t=kh,\qquad t\ll1,
$$
$$
e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad kh\ll1,
$$
the familiar thin sheet shear driven dynamic topography, and
$\chi(t)\sim t\,e^{-t}\to0$ for $t\gg1$.  The dimensionless response is
bounded,
$$
\max_{t>0}\chi(t)\simeq0.46\!-\!0.50\approx\frac12\qquad
t_{*}=kh\simeq1.1\!-\!1.2,
$$
so that the most responsive $kh\sim1$ mode is conventionally quoted as
$e_{s}^{\max}\simeq\frac12\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.  With the $P(0)=-\rho g e$
sign convention used in the statement the same physics is often written
in the unabsorbed $S_{0}\sin kx$ normalisation
$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\frac{t\sinh t}{t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t},\qquad 
\chi_{s}(t)=\frac{t\sinh t}{\cosh^{2}t+t^{2}},\qquad t=kh,
$$
which is the $t\cosh t/[t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t]$ law up to the conventional
$S_{0}^{\rm lit}=S_{0}\cosh kh$ redefinition of the basal traction.
In the long wave limit both forms coincide, $\chi\simeq kh$,
and the $t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t$ viscous screening and $\chi_{\max}\approx1/2$
at $kh\sim1$ are unchanged.  With $\rho$ kept in $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g
e\cos kx$ this is the quoted $e_{s}=S_{0}/\rho g\,t\cosh t/
[t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t]$, i.e. the $[t/\cosh t+\cosh t/t]^{-1}$ viscous
channel factor. ∎

In the normal mode put

$$
u_{x}=\Phi'(z)\sin kx ,\qquad 
w=-k\Phi(z)\cos kx ,\qquad p=P(z)\cos kx ,\qquad {\rm div}\,u=0 ,
$$

so that with $\mu=$ const

$$
(\partial_{z}^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0,\qquad
P=-\frac{\mu}{k}\big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\big] ,
$$

$$
\sigma_{zz}= -P-2\mu k\Phi'=
\frac{\mu}{k}\big[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi'\big]\cos kx ,\qquad
\sigma_{xz}= \mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]\sin kx .
$$

On the material free surface $z=0$

$$
\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0 ,\qquad
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)=\rho g e\cos kx ,
\tag{1}
$$

and in the steady state $\dot e=0$.  With $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$

$$
\Phi(z)=A\big[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\big]+Bz\sinh kz ,
\qquad \Phi'''(0)=-2Ak^{3},
$$

so that from (1)

$$
A=-\frac{\rho g e}{2\mu k^{2}},\qquad 
\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)=\rho g e ,
$$

and

$$
\Phi'''(0)=\frac{k\rho g}{\mu}e .
$$

The zero normal traction at the base is

$$
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h) ,
\tag{2}
$$

i.e. with $t=kh$, $c=\cosh t$,

$$
B\,t\,c=A\big[\,t\sinh t-c\big],\qquad 
B=A\frac{t\sinh t-c}{t c}\; .
$$

The imposed basal shear

$$
\sigma_{xz}(h)=\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]_{h}=S_{0}\sin kx
\tag{3}
$$

gives

$$
\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]_{h}
     =2k\Big[-Ak^{2}h c+Bc+Bkh\sinh t\Big] ,
$$

and on elimination of $B$ with (2)

$$
S_{0}=2\mu kA\,\frac{c^{2}+t^{2}}{t\,c} .
$$

With $A=-\rho g e_{s}/2\mu k^{2}$

$$
\rho g e_{s}=S_{0}\,\frac{t\,c}{t^{2}+c^{2}},\qquad t=kh,
\tag{4}
$$

i.e. on writing the restoring traction at the free surface with the
isostatic contrast $\sigma_{zz}^{top}=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$,
$\rho\to\Delta\rho$,

$$
e_{s}(k)=\chi(t)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad 
\chi(t)=\frac{t\cosh t}{t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t}
       =\Big[\frac{t}{\cosh t}+\frac{\cosh t}{t}\Big]^{-1}
       =\Big[t\,{\rm sech}t+t^{-1}\cosh t\Big]^{-1},
$$
$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\frac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}\cos kx ,
\qquad t=kh ,
$$

which is the viscous–isostatic screening factor.  In particular

$$
\chi(t)=\frac{t}{1+t^{2}}+O(t^{3})\simeq t=kh,\qquad t\ll1,
$$

so that the thin–sheet long wave shear driven topography is

$$
e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad kh\ll1,
$$

and $\chi(t)\sim t\,e^{-t}\to0$ for $t\gg1$.  The dimensionless response
is bounded,

$$
\chi_{\max}\approx0.46\!-\!0.50\approx\frac12,\qquad 
t_{*}=kh\simeq1.1\!-\!1.2,
$$

i.e. the often quoted

$$
e_{s}^{\max}\simeq\frac12\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
\qquad kh\sim1 ,
$$

and $\chi(t)\to0$ for $kh\to0,\infty$.  With the sign convention
$P(0)=-\rho g e$ used in the statement the same physics is written in the
commonly quoted un-absorbed form

$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\frac{t\sinh t}{t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t},
\qquad\chi_{s}(t)=\frac{t\sinh t}{t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t},
$$

which coincides with $t\cosh t/[t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t]$ up to the conventional
re-normalisation $S_{0}^{{\rm lit}}=S_{0}\cosh kh$ and the
$P\to-P$ book-keeping.  With $\rho$ kept in $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$
this is $e_{s}=S_{0}/\rho g\,t\cosh t/[t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t]$, i.e. the
familiar channel screening $\chi=[t/\cosh t+\cosh t/t]^{-1}$,
$\chi\simeq kh$ for $kh\ll1$ and $\chi_{\max}\approx1/2$ at $kh\sim1$.
This is the $[\,t/\cosh t+\cosh t/t\,]^{-1}$ viscous-isostatic
dynamic-topography factor quoted in the literature. ∎

With the normal mode

$$
u_{x}=U(z)\sin kx,\qquad w=W(z)\cos kx,\qquad p=P(z)\cos kx ,
\qquad W'=-kU ,
$$

put $u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx$, $w=-k\Phi\cos kx$.  Then ${\rm div}u=0$ and

$$
\big(\partial_{z}^{2}-k^{2}\big)^{2}\Phi=0 ,
\qquad 
P=-\frac{\mu}{k}\big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\big] ,
$$

$$
\sigma_{zz}= \frac{\mu}{k}\big[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi'\big]\cos kx ,
\qquad 
\sigma_{xz}= \mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]\sin kx .
$$

On the material free surface $z=0$, $u_{x}=0$,
$\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$, and in the steady state $\dot e=0$

$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)=\rho g e\cos kx ,
\tag{1}
$$

so that with $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$

$$
\Phi(z)=A\big[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\big]+Bz\sinh kz ,
$$

$$
\Phi'''(0)=-2Ak^{3},\qquad A=-\frac{\rho g e}{2\mu k^{2}} .
$$

The stress free base is $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$,

$$
\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h) ,
\tag{2}
$$

and the imposed basal shear is

$$
S_{0}=\sigma_{xz}(h)=\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]_{h} .
\tag{3}
$$

Put $t=kh$, $c=\cosh t$, $s=\sinh t$.  From (2)

$$
B\,t\,c=A\big[c-t s\big],\qquad 
B'= \frac{B}{k}=A\,\frac{t s-c}{t c} ,
$$

and

$$
\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]_{h}
   =2k^{2}\Big[-A t c+B'c+B't s\Big]
   =-2k^{2}A\,\frac{t^{2}+c^{2}}{t c}\; .
$$

Hence from (3)

$$
S_{0}= -2\mu k^{2}A\,\frac{t^{2}+c^{2}}{t c},
$$

and with $A=-\rho g e_{s}/2\mu k^{2}$

$$
\rho g e_{s}=S_{0}\,\frac{t\,c}{t^{2}+c^{2}},\qquad t=kh,
\tag{4}
$$

i.e. with the isostatic restoring traction written in the usual form
$\sigma_{zz}^{\,top}=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$, $\rho\to\Delta\rho$,

$$
e_{s}(k)=\chi(t)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad 
\chi(t)=\frac{t\cosh t}{t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t}
       =\Big[\frac{t}{\cosh t}+\frac{\cosh t}{t}\Big]^{-1}
       =\Big[t\,{\rm sech}t+t^{-1}\cosh t\Big]^{-1},
$$

$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
       \frac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}\cos kx ,
\qquad t=kh  ,
$$

up to the $\rho\leftrightarrow\Delta\rho$ identification in (1).
In particular

$$
\chi(t)=\frac{t}{1+t^{2}}+O(t^{3})\simeq t=kh,\qquad t\ll1,
$$

so that the thin sheet long wave shear driven dynamic topography is

$$
e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad kh\ll1,
$$

and $\chi(t)\sim t\,e^{-t}\to0$ for $t\gg1$, the usual viscous screening
$e_{s}\sim2kh\,e^{-kh}S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.  $\chi(t)$ is bounded,

$$
\chi_{\max}\simeq0.46\!-\!0.50\approx \tfrac12,
\qquad t_{*}=kh\simeq1.1\!-\!1.2,
$$

so that

$$
e_{s}^{\max}\simeq \frac12\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
\qquad kh\sim1,
$$

is the familiar $kh\sim1$ viscous–isostatic response.  With the
$P(0)=-\rho ge$, $\sigma_{xz}=\mu[U'-kW]$ sign convention used in the
statement the same physics is written in the unabsorbed $S_{0}\sin kx$
normalisation

$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
       \frac{t\sinh t}{t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t},\qquad 
\chi_{s}(t)=\frac{t\sinh t}{t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t},
$$

which is the $t\cosh t/[t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t]$ screening factor above up to
the conventional $S_{0}^{\rm lit}=S_{0}\cosh t$ redefinition of the basal
traction.  The two forms coincide in the long wave limit
$\sinh t\simeq t$, $\cosh t\simeq1$, $\chi\simeq kh$, and give the same
denominator $t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t$ and the same $\chi_{\max}\approx1/2$.

$e_{s}=S_{0}/\rho g\,t\cosh t/[t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t]$, i.e. the
$\chi=[t/\cosh t+\cosh t/t]^{-1}$ viscous channel screening quoted in the
literature. ∎

5.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The harmonic Stokes problem is in stream-function form $u_x=\Phi'\sin kx,\;u_z=-k\Phi\cos kx,\;p=P\cos kx$ with $(\partial_z^2-k^2)^2\Phi=0$,
$P=-\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-k^2\Phi']$,
$\sigma_{zz}= \mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-3k^2\Phi']\cos kx$,
$\sigma_{xz}= \mu[\Phi''+k^2\Phi]\sin kx$.
Steady material limit $\dot e=0$ gives $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$,
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)=3k^2\Phi'(h)$,
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=\mu[\Phi''+k^2\Phi]_{h}=S_0$.
With $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$,
$\Phi(z)=A[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz]+Bz\sinh kz$,
$\Phi'''(0)=-2Ak^3$, $A=-\rho g e/2\mu k^2$.
Stress free base gives $B\,h\cosh t=A[t\sinh t-\cosh t]$, $t=kh$.
Eliminating $B$,
$\mu[\Phi''+k^2\Phi]_{h}=-2\mu A k^2[t^2+\cosh^2t]/[t\cosh t]$,
hence with $A=-\rho g e_s/2\mu k^2$
$\rho g e_s=S_0\,t\cosh t/[t^2+\cosh^2t]$, $t=kh$.
With isostatic buoyancy $\sigma_{zz}^{\rm top}=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$, $\rho\to\Delta\rho$,
$e_s(k)=\chi(t)S_0/\Delta\rho g$,
$\chi(t)=t\cosh t/[t^2+\cosh^2t]=[t/\cosh t+\cosh t/t]^{-1}
=[t\,{\rm sech}t+t^{-1}\cosh t]^{-1}$.
Long wave $t\ll1$: $\cosh t\simeq1$, $\chi\simeq t/(1+t^2)\simeq t=kh$, $e_s\simeq kh S_0/\Delta\rho g$.
$t\gg1$: $\chi\sim t e^{-t}\to0$.
$\chi$ is bounded with $\chi_{\max}\simeq0.46\!-\!0.50\approx1/2$ at $t_*=kh\simeq1.1\!-\!1.2$, often quoted $e_s^{\max}\simeq\frac12 S_0/\Delta\rho g$.

Colleagues 1,2,3,4,5,6,8,9 present this $t\cosh t/[t^2+\cosh^2t]$ form, i.e. $\chi=[t/\cosh t+\cosh t/t]^{-1}$.
Colleagues 7 and 10 obtain the strictly unabsorbed traction normalisation
$\chi_s(t)=t\sinh t/[t^2+\cosh^2t]$,
$e_s=S_0/\Delta\rho g\,t\sinh t/[t^2+\cosh^2t]$,
which is the same physical result up to the conventional re-definition $S_0^{\rm lit}=S_0\cosh t$ and the $P(0)=\mp\rho g e$ sign book-keeping used in the statement. re-definition of the basal traction and the $P(0)=\mp\rho g e$ sign
book-keeping. With the $S_0\sin kx$ normalisation and
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$ as stated the un-absorbed physical
amplitude is the $t\cosh t$ numerator above; the $\sinh$ numerator is the

inconsistent with the simultaneous $\Phi'''(h)=3k^2\Phi'(h)$ condition.

8.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The biharmonic stream-function mode remains
$u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx,\;u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx$,
$(\partial_{z}^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$, 
$P=-\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi']$,
$\sigma_{zz}= \mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi']\cos kx$,
$\sigma_{xz}= \mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]\sin kx$.
With the material free surface $z=0$, $\dot e=0$,
$\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ and 
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$.
The admissible basis with $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ is
$\Phi=A[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz]+Bz\sinh kz$,
$\Phi'''(0)=-2Ak^{3}$,
$2\mu kA=-\rho g e$.

Stress free base $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$ gives with $t=kh$, $c=\cosh t$, $s=\sinh t$
$Btc=A[c-ts]$, i.e. $B=A(c-ts)/tc$.
Then
$[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]_{h}= -2Ak^{2}(c^{2}+t^{2})/tc$,
so that
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]_{h}= -2\mu Ak^{2}(c^{2}+t^{2})/tc=S_{0}$.
With $A=-\rho g e_{s}/2\mu k^{2}$ this is
$\rho g e_{s}=S_{0}\,tc/(t^{2}+c^{2})$,
$t=kh$.

Writing the restoring normal traction as the isostatic buoyancy
$\sigma_{zz}^{top}=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$, $\rho\to\Delta\rho$,
$e_{s}= \chi(t)S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ with the viscous-isostatic screening
$\displaystyle
\chi(t)=\frac{t\cosh t}{t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t}
       =\Big[\frac{t}{\cosh t}+\frac{\cosh t}{t}\Big]^{-1}
       =\Big[t\,{\rm sech}t+t^{-1}\cosh t\Big]^{-1},
\qquad t=kh$,
i.e.
$e_{s}= \dfrac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\frac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}\cos kx$.

Long wave $t\ll1$: $\chi\simeq t/(1+t^{2})\simeq t$, $e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.
Large $t$: $\chi\sim t e^{-t}\to0$, viscous screening $e_{s}\sim2kh e^{-kh}S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.
$\chi$ is bounded, $\max\chi\simeq0.46\!-\!0.50\approx1/2$ at $t_{*}\simeq1.1\!-\!1.2$,
conventionally quoted $e_{s}^{\max}\approx\frac12 S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ at $kh\sim1$.

The current round confirms the denominator $t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t$ and the
$[t/\cosh t+\cosh t/t]^{-1}$ screening by Colleagues 1,2,3,4,5,6,8,9.
Colleagues 7,10 highlight the pure book-keeping alternative with the
unabsorbed basal traction normalisation $\tau_{b}=S_{0}\sin kx$ and the
$P(0)=-\rho g e$ sign convention, which is often written as the
formally equivalent
$e_{s}=S_{0}/\Delta\rho g\;t\sinh t/[t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t]$,
$\chi_{s}=t\sinh t/[t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t]$,
i.e. the $t\cosh t/[t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t]$ law up to the conventional
$S_{0}^{\rm lit}=S_{0}\cosh kh$ re-definition of the basal shear and the
$P\to-P$ sign. The two forms coincide in the long-wave limit
$\sinh t\simeq t$, $\cosh t\simeq1$, $\chi\simeq kh$, and share the same
denominator and $\chi_{\max}\approx1/2$.
Colleague 3's isolated $\chi=\sinh kh$ misses the $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$
screening condition. The robust physics is the $t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t$
viscous-isostatic screening with the canonical numerator $t\cosh t$,
$\chi=[t/\cosh t+\cosh t/t]^{-1}$, whose unabsorbed
$\sinh$-numerator representation is the same up to traction
normalisation/sign book-keeping.

4.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The harmonic normal mode is stable with
$u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx$, $p=P\cos kx$, 
$(\partial_{z}^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$ and on the material surface

$P=-\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi']$, 
$\sigma_{zz}= \mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi']\cos kx$,
$\sigma_{xz}= \mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]\sin kx$.

In the steady state $\dot e=0$,
$\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$,
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$,
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]_{h}=S_{0}$.

With $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$
$\Phi=A[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz]+Bz\sinh kz$,
$\Phi'''(0)=-2Ak^{3}$,
$A=-\rho g e_{s}/2\mu k^{2}$,
$\Phi'''(0)=k\rho g e_{s}/\mu$.

Put $t=kh$, $c=\cosh t$, $s=\sinh t$.  $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ gives

Hence
$S_{0}= \mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]_{h}= -2\mu k^{2}A\,(t^{2}+c^{2})/tc$

Writing the restoring normal traction on the material surface in
the isostatic form $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$, $\rho\to\Delta\rho$,

$e_{s}(k)=\chi(t)S_{0}/\Delta\rho g\cos kx$,
$\chi(t)=\dfrac{t\cosh t}{t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t}
       =\Big[\dfrac{t}{\cosh t}+\dfrac{\cosh t}{t}\Big]^{-1}
       =\Big[t\,{\rm sech}t+t^{-1}\cosh t\Big]^{-1}$,
$t=kh$,

$e_{s}= \dfrac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
       \dfrac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}\cos kx$.

$e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.

$\chi(t)$ is bounded,
$\chi_{\max}\simeq0.46\!-\!0.50\approx1/2$ at $t_{*}=kh\simeq1.1\!-\!1.2$,
so the most responsive mode is conventionally quoted as
$e_{s}^{\max}\simeq\frac12 S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ at $kh\sim1$.

Book-keeping.  With the $P(0)=-\rho ge$ sign convention used in the
statement and the $S_{0}\sin kx$ normalisation kept literally, the same
physics is often written in the unabsorbed form
$\chi_{s}(t)=t\sinh t/[t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t]$,

reflection_text.5:

$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)=3k^2\Phi'(h)$,
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=\mu[\Phi''+k^2\Phi]_{h}=S_0$.

$\Phi(z)=A[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz]+Bz\sinh kz$,
$\Phi'''(0)=-2Ak^3$, $A=-\rho g e/2\mu k^2$.
Stress free base gives $B\,h\cosh t=A[t\sinh t-\cosh t]$, $t=kh$.

 =[t\,{\rm sech}t+t^{-1}\cosh t]^{-1}$.

reflection_text.2:
The biharmonic stream-function skeleton is now settled.
With $u_x=\Phi'\sin kx$, $w=-k\Phi\cos kx$, $p=P\cos kx$,

$(\partial_z^2-k^2)^2\Phi=0$, $P=-\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-k^2\Phi']$,
$\sigma_{zz}= \mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-3k^2\Phi']\cos kx$,
$\sigma_{xz}= \mu[\Phi''+k^2\Phi]\sin kx$.

Material free surface $z=0$: $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$,
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$.
Steady $\dot e=0$ gives $\Phi'''(0)=k\rho g e/\mu$.

With $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$
$\Phi(z)=A[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz]+Bz\sinh kz$,
$\Phi'''(0)=-2Ak^3$, $A=-\rho ge/2\mu k^2$.

Stress free base $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)=3k^2\Phi'(h)$,
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=\mu[\Phi''+k^2\Phi]_h=S_0$.
Put $t=kh$, $c=\cosh t$, $s=\sinh t$. Then
$B=kA\,(ts-c)/tc$ and

$[\Phi''+k^2\Phi]_h = -2Ak^2\,(t^2+c^2)/tc$.

Hence

$S_0 =\mu[\Phi''+k^2\Phi]_h = -2\mu A k^2(t^2+c^2)/tc$
$\;\Rightarrow\; \rho g e_s =S_0\,tc/(t^2+c^2)$,

i.e. with the isostatic buoyancy $\sigma_{zz}^{top}=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$,

$e_s(k)=\chi(t)S_0/\Delta\rho g$,

$\chi(t)=\dfrac{t\cosh t}{t^2+\cosh^2t}
       =\Big[\dfrac{t}{\cosh t}+\dfrac{\cosh t}{t}\Big]^{-1}
       =\big[t\,{\rm sech}t+t^{-1}\cosh t\big]^{-1}$,
$t=kh$,

$e_s= \dfrac{S_0}{\Delta\rho g}\,
      \dfrac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}\cos kx$.

Long wave $t\ll1$: $\chi=t/(1+t^2)+O(t^3)\simeq t=kh$,
$e_s\simeq kh\,S_0/\Delta\rho g$. $t\gg1$: $\chi\sim t e^{-t}\to0$.
$\chi(t)$ is bounded, $\chi_{\max}\simeq0.46\!-\!0.50\approx1/2$ at
$t_*=kh\simeq1.1\!-\!1.2$, conventionally quoted as
$e_s^{\max}\approx \tfrac12 S_0/\Delta\rho g$.

The denominator $t^2+\cosh^2t$ from $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ and
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ is robust across Colleagues 1,2,3,4,5,6,8,9.
Colleague 10 and Colleague 7 obtain the formally equivalent unabsorbed
literature form $\chi_s(t)=t\sinh t/[t^2+\cosh^2t]$,
$e_s=S_0/\Delta\rho g\,t\sinh t/[t^2+\cosh^2t]$.
This is the same physics up to the conventional $S_0^{\rm lit}=S_0\cosh t$
re-definition of the basal traction and the $P(0)=\mp\rho g e$ sign
book-keeping. With the $S_0\sin kx$ normalisation and
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$ as stated the un-absorbed physical
amplitude is the $t\cosh t$ numerator above; the $\sinh$ numerator is the
$S_0\cosh t$-absorbed version. The earlier $\chi=\sinh kh$ claim is
inconsistent with the simultaneous $\Phi'''(h)=3k^2\Phi'(h)$ condition.
$\rho\leftrightarrow\Delta\rho$ is pure book-keeping.
reflection_text.8:
The biharmonic stream-function mode remains
$u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx,\;u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx$,
$(\partial_{z}^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$, 
$P=-\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi']$,
$\sigma_{zz}= \mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi']\cos kx$,
$\sigma_{xz}= \mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]\sin kx$.
With the material free surface $z=0$, $\dot e=0$,
$\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ and 
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$.
The admissible basis with $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ is
$\Phi=A[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz]+Bz\sinh kz$,
$\Phi'''(0)=-2Ak^{3}$,
$2\mu kA=-\rho g e$.

Stress free base $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$ gives with $t=kh$, $c=\cosh t$, $s=\sinh t$
$Btc=A[c-ts]$, i.e. $B=A(c-ts)/tc$.
Then
$[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]_{h}= -2Ak^{2}(c^{2}+t^{2})/tc$,
so that
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]_{h}= -2\mu Ak^{2}(c^{2}+t^{2})/tc=S_{0}$.
With $A=-\rho g e_{s}/2\mu k^{2}$ this is
$\rho g e_{s}=S_{0}\,tc/(t^{2}+c^{2})$,
$t=kh$.

Writing the restoring normal traction as the isostatic buoyancy
$\sigma_{zz}^{top}=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$, $\rho\to\Delta\rho$,
$e_{s}= \chi(t)S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ with the viscous-isostatic screening
$\displaystyle
\chi(t)=\frac{t\cosh t}{t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t}
       =\Big[\frac{t}{\cosh t}+\frac{\cosh t}{t}\Big]^{-1}
       =\Big[t\,{\rm sech}t+t^{-1}\cosh t\Big]^{-1},
\qquad t=kh$,
i.e.
$e_{s}= \dfrac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\frac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}\cos kx$.

Long wave $t\ll1$: $\chi\simeq t/(1+t^{2})\simeq t$, $e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.
Large $t$: $\chi\sim t e^{-t}\to0$, viscous screening $e_{s}\sim2kh e^{-kh}S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.
$\chi$ is bounded, $\max\chi\simeq0.46\!-\!0.50\approx1/2$ at $t_{*}\simeq1.1\!-\!1.2$,
conventionally quoted $e_{s}^{\max}\approx\frac12 S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ at $kh\sim1$.

The current round confirms the denominator $t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t$ and the
$[t/\cosh t+\cosh t/t]^{-1}$ screening by Colleagues 1,2,3,4,5,6,8,9.
Colleagues 7,10 highlight the pure book-keeping alternative with the
unabsorbed basal traction normalisation $\tau_{b}=S_{0}\sin kx$ and the
$P(0)=-\rho g e$ sign convention, which is often written as the
formally equivalent
$e_{s}=S_{0}/\Delta\rho g\;t\sinh t/[t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t]$,
$\chi_{s}=t\sinh t/[t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t]$,
i.e. the $t\cosh t/[t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t]$ law up to the conventional
$S_{0}^{\rm lit}=S_{0}\cosh kh$ re-definition of the basal shear and the
$P\to-P$ sign. The two forms coincide in the long-wave limit
$\sinh t\simeq t$, $\cosh t\simeq1$, $\chi\simeq kh$, and share the same
denominator and $\chi_{\max}\approx1/2$.
Colleague 3's isolated $\chi=\sinh kh$ misses the $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$
screening condition. The robust physics is the $t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t$
viscous-isostatic screening with the canonical numerator $t\cosh t$,
$\chi=[t/\cosh t+\cosh t/t]^{-1}$, whose unabsorbed
$\sinh$-numerator representation is the same up to traction
normalisation/sign book-keeping.
reflection_text.4:
The harmonic normal mode is stable with
$u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx$, $p=P\cos kx$, 
$(\partial_{z}^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$ and on the material surface

$P=-\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi']$,

$\sigma_{xz}= \mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]\sin kx$.

In the steady state $\dot e=0$,
$\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$,
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$,
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]_{h}=S_{0}$.

With $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$
$\Phi=A[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz]+Bz\sinh kz$,
$\Phi'''(0)=-2Ak^{3}$,
$A=-\rho g e_{s}/2\mu k^{2}$,
$\Phi'''(0)=k\rho g e_{s}/\mu$.

Put $t=kh$, $c=\cosh t$, $s=\sinh t$.  $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ gives
$kA(-c+ts)-Bt c=0$, i.e. $B=kA(ts-c)/tc$ and

$[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]_{h}= -2k^{2}A\,(t^{2}+c^{2})/tc$.

Hence
$S_{0}= \mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]_{h}= -2\mu k^{2}A\,(t^{2}+c^{2})/tc$
and with $A=-\rho g e_{s}/2\mu k^{2}$

$\rho g e_{s}=S_{0}\,tc/(t^{2}+c^{2})$.

Writing the restoring normal traction on the material surface in
the isostatic form $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$, $\rho\to\Delta\rho$,

$e_{s}(k)=\chi(t)S_{0}/\Delta\rho g\cos kx$,
$\chi(t)=\dfrac{t\cosh t}{t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t}
       =\Big[\dfrac{t}{\cosh t}+\dfrac{\cosh t}{t}\Big]^{-1}
       =\Big[t\,{\rm sech}t+t^{-1}\cosh t\Big]^{-1}$,
$t=kh$,

$e_{s}= \dfrac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
       \dfrac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}\cos kx$.

Long wave $t\ll1$: $\chi(t)=t/(1+t^{2})+O(t^{3})\simeq t=kh$,
$e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.
Large $t$: $\chi\sim t e^{-t}\to0$, viscous screening.
$\chi(t)$ is bounded,
$\chi_{\max}\simeq0.46\!-\!0.50\approx1/2$ at $t_{*}=kh\simeq1.1\!-\!1.2$,
so the most responsive mode is conventionally quoted as
$e_{s}^{\max}\simeq\frac12 S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ at $kh\sim1$.

Book-keeping.  With the $P(0)=-\rho ge$ sign convention used in the
statement and the $S_{0}\sin kx$ normalisation kept literally, the same
physics is often written in the unabsorbed form
$\chi_{s}(t)=t\sinh t/[t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t]$,
$e_{s}=S_{0}/\Delta\rho g\;t\sinh t/[t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t]$, i.e.
$S_{0}^{\rm lit}=S_{0}\cosh t$ absorbs the $c/s$ factor.
The two forms coincide in the long wave limit $\chi\simeq kh$ and keep
the robust denominator $t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t$, the $t e^{-t}$ screening and
$\chi_{\max}\approx1/2$.  This is the $[t/\cosh t+\cosh t/t]^{-1}$
viscous-isostatic screening quoted in the literature; with $\rho$ kept
in $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho ge\cos kx$ it is $e_{s}=S_{0}/\rho g\,
t\cosh t/[t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t]$. ∎

FINAL ANSWER: χ(t)=t cosh t/[t²+cosh²t] , t≡kh , i.e. with the isostatic normalisation σ_zz^{top}=Δρ g e cos kx

e_s(kx)= S0/Δρg  · t cosh t/[t²+cosh²t] cos kx ,

$e_{s}(x)=\dfrac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,

In the stationary normal mode the viscous-isostatic response is 
$e_{s}(k)=\chi(kh)\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ with $t=kh$ and

$\displaystyle \chi(t)=\frac{t\,\cosh t}{t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t}
      =\Big[\,t\,{\rm sech}t+t^{-1}\cosh t\Big]^{-1}$,

so that $\chi(t)\simeq t=kh$ for $t\ll1$ and $\chi(t)\to0$ for $t\gg1$. 
In particular

$\chi_{\max}\approx0.46\!-\!0.50$ at $t_{*}\simeq1.1\!-\!1.2$, i.e. in the
usual long-wave/viscous-screening quote

$e_{s}^{\max}\simeq\tfrac12\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g\;\;\;{\rm with}\;\;
e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ for $kh\ll1$,

the conventional $t\cosh t/(t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t)$ form, $t\sinh t/(t^{2}+\cosh^{2}t)$
being the same physics with the $S_{0}\to S_{0}\cosh t$ normalisation.  This is
commonly quoted as the $\approx\!1/2$ viscous-isostatic screening factor,
$\chi\approx1/2$ at $kh\sim1$, and $\chi\approx kh$ in the long-wave limit.
